- complete_header(partial) fills missing keys.
- check_header(h) -> list of E3/E4 strings.

WRITER: TraceWriter(path, header, *, reserve=16384, tokens_sidecar=True, strict=True). It is a context manager.
- Attributes: n, H, L, K, E, P, record_size, dtype, header, chunks.
- .write(token_index|None, pos, token_id, phase, chunk_id, ids[L,K], weights[L,K], probs=None). probs is one of: a structured (id,p) array [L,P], an (ids, probs) pair, or an array [L,P,2]. chunk_id may be the full index; the record stores it mod 256.
- .write_many(ids[n,L,K], weights[n,L,K], *, phase=None, pos=None, token_ids=None, chunk_ids=None, probs=None). pos defaults to counting from 0 per chunk_ids run.
- .write_array(structured records of exactly .dtype).
- .begin_chunk(source=None, **extra) -> chunk index.
- .flush().
- .close(chunks=None, **header_updates). The structural keys n_expert, n_expert_used, moe_layers and probs_top cannot change.
- Chunk tracking: a header that already holds non-empty chunks is final. Otherwise a new chunk starts whenever chunk_id changes, or at begin_chunk; source defaults to corpus_id.
- strict=True refuses: a token_index other than the next one, ids >= E or duplicated, phase outside {0,1}, chunk ids out of sequence. strict=False only requires the values to fit their field types.

READER: TraceReader(path, *, use_mmap=True). It is a context manager; close() releases the Windows file lock.
- Attributes: path, path_str, header, n, truncated, n_records_field, header_json_len, record_size, data_start, file_size, trailing_bytes, L, K, E, P, moe_layers, dtype, records (structured memmap).
- Cached column copies: ids uint8 [n,L,K]; weights float32 [n,L,K]; phase uint8; chunk uint8 (record chunk_id); pos uint32; token_index uint32; token_id int32 (record column); token_ids int32 (tokens.bin if present, else the records; token_ids_source says which); probs = (id uint8 [n,L,P], p float32 [n,L,P]) or None.
- segments() -> [{index, start, end, chunk, derived}]; chunk_index() -> int64 [n] full chunk index; chunk_sources() -> list[str].
- read_header(path) parses only the JSON header; read_fixed_header(path) returns the 32 fixed bytes as a dict.

VALIDATION:
- validate(path) -> list[str] of errors only, each starting with 'E1'..'E14'. Warnings are logged on logger 'pigemma.trace'.
- validate_report(path) -> ValidationReport(path, errors, warnings, n_records, truncated, .ok, .as_dict()).
- Warnings are W1..W7 plus the extensions W8 and W9 (see the summary).

MERGE: merge(paths, out, *, argv=None, write_gen=True, write_meta_file=True) -> {out, n_records, n_chunks, sources, notes, tokens, gen, meta}.
- Raises MergeError naming the first differing MERGE_KEY, and FileNotFoundError for a missing input.
- Output header: corpus_id='merged', sources = the input strings, chunks renumbered with from_source, notes when n_ctx/n_batch/n_ubatch/n_threads/gguf_path/llama differ.

STATS: stats(reader_or_path, train_frac=0.7, item='layer-expert'|'expert', *, coverage_points, working_set_windows, corpus_top) -> dict.
- It has exactly the stats.json keys of data_formats/TRACE_FORMAT 5.2.
- Extra keys, which readers ignore:
  - top level: n_train, n_test, n_expert, n_expert_used, moe_layers, item, truncated;
  - global: n_accesses, n_items;
  - cross_layer: mutual_info_bits_null_mean (plug-in MI against a fixed-seed permutation; report MI minus null), per_pair[{layer, next_layer, precision_at_8, precision_at_16, baseline_static_top16, baseline_same_ids, mutual_info_bits, mutual_info_bits_null}], n_train, n_test.
- Raises ValueError on an empty trace or on ids >= E.

STATS BUILDING BLOCKS (for cache_sim / gguf_map):
- access_items(ids[N,L,K], E, item) -> (int64 items in t,j,k order, with item = j*E+e; n_items).
- stack_distances(items, n_items, batch=256) -> int64 per access (0 = cold, else LRU distance).
- stack_distance_hist(items, n_items) -> length n_items+1.
- lru_hit_curve(hist) -> [[C, hit]] for C = 1..n_items. hit = sum(hist[1..C]) / total: the overall rate, warmup 0, cold misses counted.
- lru_hit_rate(hist, C).
- coverage_curve(counts, ns), entropy_bits, gini, js_divergence_bits(a,b) (None if either is empty), mutual_info_bits(a, b, n_values, miller_madow=False).
- cross_layer_table(ids, n_train, E) -> L-1 float64 [E,E] tables of P(e' in S_{j+1} | e in S_j), reusable by lru_prefetch.
- write_stats_csv(st, dir, prefix) writes <prefix>.per_layer.csv, .freq.csv, .lru_curve.csv and .cross_layer.csv.

SIDECARS:
- write_meta(stem, dict) -> Path. stem is the trace path (or the meta path); 'trace' is added if missing. JSON is written atomically with NaN mapped to null.
- read_meta(stem) -> dict or None.
- build_meta(trace, *, gguf=None, corpus=(), argv=None, wall_ms=None, summary=None, coherent='auto'|True|False|None, host=None, notes=(), with_sha=True) -> the TRACE_FORMAT 4.4 dict.
  - A /work/... gguf path is mapped to the repo.
  - With coherent='auto', pigemma.quality.is_coherent is applied to each gen.txt chunk and the result also goes into 'coherent_by_chunk'.
- read_gen(trace) -> {chunk_index: text}.
- read_tokens(path) -> int32 array.
- parse_probe_summary(stderr_text) -> the last PIGEMMA_SUMMARY dict, or None.

ACTS:
- read_acts_dir(dir) -> Acts(path, meta, n_tokens, layers, kinds{kind: ne0}, phase uint8|None, token_ids int32|None).
  - .file(layer, kind) and .available() -> [(layer, kind)].
  - .get(layer, kind) -> float16 memmap [T, ne0]. It recovers an unpatched npy (rows = min(header rows, rows in the file)) and emits a TraceWarning.
- write_acts_dir(dir, {(layer, kind): array[T, ne0]}, *, phase=None, token_ids=None, meta=None) -> Path.
- npy_header_f16(T, ne0) -> the canonical 128 bytes.
- read_npy_header(path) -> (descr, fortran_order, shape, data_offset).

CLI: python -m pigemma.trace [--log-level L] <cmd>
- validate <trace>... [--json] [--quiet]: exit 1 if and only if any error; a missing file counts as an E1 error.
- info <trace> [--no-header]: JSON with path, file_size, header_json_len, record_size, n_records, n_records_field, truncated, L, K, E, P, n_prefill, n_gen, n_chunks, chunks_derived, sources, sidecars{tokens, gen, meta}, header, warnings.
- stats <trace> [--train-frac 0.7] [--item layer-expert|expert] [--out stats.json] [--csv-dir DIR] [--no-mmap]: without --out the JSON goes to stdout; the CSVs are named after the trace basename minus .moetrace.
- merge <out> <in...> [--no-gen] [--no-meta].
- meta <trace> [--gguf P] [--corpus F...] [--argv-json J] [--wall-ms N] [--summary-file probe_stderr] [--host-json F] [--coherent auto|true|false|null] [--note T]... [--no-sha] [--out F].
- acts <dir>.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 missing input file.
entries.self_test:
All runs were on Windows, Python 3.14, numpy 2.3.3, from the repo root.

1. `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -o addopts="" -m "not integration" -rs tests/` gave 218 passed, 4 skipped, 3 deselected in 7.0 s. Of the 32 tests in test_trace.py, 30 pass and 2 skip by design: the golden 26B trace is not captured yet, and pigemma.cache_sim does not exist yet.
2. test_trace.py checks:
   - The 1000-record round trip (L=4, K=8, E=16) is bit-exact: ids, f16 weights, phase, chunk, pos, token_index and tokens.bin. A probs round trip is checked too.
   - A sentinel n_records is inferred with truncated=True plus TraceWarning and W1. A writer that is never closed gives a readable truncated trace.
   - The header-rewrite path at close runs: 150 chunks with reserve=0.
   - Strict-writer refusals work.
   - validate catches E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6 (truncated record), E7, E8, E9, E10 (bad id; the message format matches the spec example), E11 (duplicates), E12 (sum 1.5 and inf) and E14.
   - Stack distances equal a brute-force LRU stack on 5 random configurations, including batch sizes 1, 7, 33 and 1024.
   - The LRU curve equals an OrderedDict LRU simulation within 1e-9 at capacities 8, 24 and 50.
   - Coverage is monotone and 1.0 at K=E. The K=E trace has entropy log2(E) and Gini 0.
   - A single-hot trace gives coverage@1 = 1.0, entropy 0 and Gini (E-1)/E.
   - With layer correlation 0.9: precision@16 is 0.89 against static top-16 at 0.57. With no correlation the two agree within 0.05.
   - Merge renumbers token_index and chunks, concatenates tokens.bin, renumbers gen.txt (including Hebrew text), skips the output matched by the glob, and refuses incompatible inputs naming the n_expert key.
   - meta works through --summary-file and --corpus.
   - npy_header_f16 equals np.save's 128 bytes. Acts round-trips, and an unpatched npy is recovered.
   - The constants match the docs/TRACE_FORMAT.md block.
   - CLI exit codes 0, 1, 2 and 3 are covered.
3. Scale run on a synthetic trace with the 26B shape (L=30, K=8, E=128), using the scratchpad only:
   - 16k tokens: an 11.8 MB file; validate 0.1 s; stats 5.6 s for 3.84M accesses. The LRU curve on a 1000-token prefix equals brute force to 12 decimals at capacities 240, 960 and 1920.
   - 100k tokens: the file holds exactly 73.6 MB of records, matching MOETRACE_BYTES_26B_100K_TOKENS; validate takes 0.6 s.
   - Merging 116k records takes 0.2 s and the result validates.
4. CLI through `python -m pigemma.trace`:
   - validate, info, stats with --out and --csv-dir (4 CSVs), and merge with a quoted glob all exit 0.
   - A missing file exits 1 for validate and 3 for stats; an unknown command exits 2.
   - The stats summary for the 16k trace printed MI 0.564 bits against a shuffle null of 0.521.
5. Both files are normalized to LF line endings, like the rest of the repo.
6. No model inference was run; the spec does not require any.
open_issues: Validator extensions not in TRACE_FORMAT 3.9: W8 (fixed-header reserved != 0) and W9 (tokens.bin content != record token_id; 4.2 requires them equal). Both are warnings only, so exit codes are unaffected. The owner of docs/TRACE_FORMAT.md should list them in 3.9 or ask for their removal.

The plug-in mutual information required by the stats.json contract is heavily biased upward when the joint table is undersampled. On independent synthetic layers (E=64, N=3000) it reads 0.64 bits. On a 26B-shaped 16k-token synthetic trace it reads 0.564 against a shuffle null of 0.521. Miller-Madow does not fix this. stats() therefore adds cross_layer.mutual_info_bits_null_mean, and the H1 write-up must report MI minus null, never raw MI.

The normative additive cross-layer predictor (score = sum of P(e' given e) over S_j) is pulled toward globally popular experts. With strong synthetic correlation, precision@8 (0.53) can fall below static top-16 (0.57) while precision@16 is 0.89. This is the defined behaviour, not a bug, but the cache_sim lru_prefetch author and the write-up should be aware of it.

test_lru_curve_equals_cache_sim_module guesses the cache_sim API from the manifest: simulate(reader, map_dict, 'lru', capacity*unit, warmup_tokens=0, read_granularity=1), reading result.overall['hit_rate']. It skips on TypeError, KeyError or AttributeError. The cache_sim author should adjust that call to the real API; tests/test_cache_sim.py asserts the same equality from the other side.

tests/synth.py does not exist yet. test_trace.py carries its own synth_routing/write_synth (Zipf per layer, Gumbel top-K, optional layer correlation). The tests agent may move them to tests/synth.py; write_synth_trace there can call TraceWriter.write_many.
The golden-trace test skips until pc/trace_collect.sh --smoke has produced tests/fixtures/golden_26b_72tok.moetrace.

`meta --coherent auto` assumes pigemma.quality.is_coherent(text) returns a bool; a tuple or dict is tolerated. It is evaluated per gen.txt chunk and adds 'coherent_by_chunk'. If quality.py is missing, coherent is null and a note says why.

build_meta records the fingerprint of the host that writes meta.json. When pc/trace_collect.sh runs `meta` on Windows after a Docker probe run, it should pass --host-json with `python -m pigemma.paths host` captured inside the container; otherwise a note marks the host as the writer's.
On Windows a live np.memmap locks the trace file. Use `with TraceReader(...)` or close(), or use_mmap=False, before replacing or deleting a trace. merge and validate already do this.
Header JSON is written compactly (separators ',' and ':', UTF-8 with non-ASCII kept). The C++ probe may format its JSON differently; readers parse with json.loads, so formatting does not matter.

entries.summary:
pigemma/gguf_map.py does four things:
- Maps a GGUF into byte ranges: every tensor as an absolute file range with a kind and a layer, plus each expert's slab per layer.
- Counts per-token traffic and KV-cache bytes.
- Plans the hot set: non-expert tensors first, then the hottest experts. It writes hotset.json and hotset.ranges.txt for the pinner.
- Refreshes catalog.json sizes, sha256 and (optionally) the byte split from Hugging Face.

There are two header readers. The default is gguf-py's GGUFReader, as the spec asks; it takes about 11 s per real model on Windows. The second is a stdlib-only parser that takes about 0.12 s. It is used automatically when gguf-py cannot be imported, which is the case on the emulated Pi: it has no pyyaml.

Results on the real models (MEASURED, header reads only, no inference):
- 26B: data_offset 15,823,936; 658 tensors; expert unit 3,345,408 B; expert bytes 12,846,366,720; non-expert bytes 1,577,172,088; worst-case expert bytes per token 802,897,920. KV cache at 4096 tokens: 293.6 MB in f16, 156.0 MB in q8_0.
- 31B: data_offset 15,833,440; 833 tensors; every one of the 180 FFN matrices is 65,028,096 B; non-expert bytes 17,635,166,448.
- Both readers produce identical maps.

As the run order asked, I built results/map26.json and traces/h2/map31.json with the CLI. On a synthetic Zipf stats file, a 4.1e9 B hot set holds the 1.578 GB non-expert set plus 753 experts, which cover 89% of routings. This is an illustration only; real stats from a trace do not exist yet.

Pi path (MEASURED in the arm64 Debian 13 container under emulation, Python 3.13, no pyyaml): it fell back to the stdlib reader and built the 26B map in 5.8 s. hotset worked with page 4096, and a too-small budget was refused with exit 4.

catalog-refresh, run read-only against Hugging Face (`--all --dry-run`): all 15 entries match the live listing and catalog.json is byte-identical afterwards. `--split` on the two IQ2_XXS quants ran with no changes. A separate direct check of 26b-ud-q3_k_m read its header remotely and reproduced all 13 byte-split catalog fields.
entries.interface_notes:
MODULE pigemma.gguf_map
- Run as `python -m pigemma.gguf_map`.
- No numpy or gguf import at module level. hotset and summary are stdlib only; this is tested by checking sys.modules.

CLI (`--log-level L` is accepted before or after the subcommand):
- `build <gguf|registry-id> --out map.json [--page-size 16384] [--backend auto|gguf|stdlib] [--no-sha] [--reuse] [--json]`
  - Prints the summary table, including GB per token.
  - `--reuse` keeps an existing map when basename, size and page size match.
- `summary --map map.json [--json]`
- `hotset --map map.json [--stats stats.json] --budget-bytes N [--page-size 16384] [--no-nonexpert] [--per-layer-min 0] [--rank count|weight] [--min-hits 0] --out hotset.json [--ranges-out P]`
  - N may be written 5200000000, 5.2e9, 5.2GB or 2GiB.
  - The ranges file defaults to `<out without .json>.ranges.txt`; pi/out/hotset.json gives pi/out/hotset.ranges.txt.
  - Without `--stats` it pins the non-expert tensors only.
- `catalog-refresh [--catalog P] [--ids a,b] [--all] [--split] [--dry-run] [--out P] [--token-file F]`

Exit codes:
- 0 ok.
- 1 error: malformed or truncated GGUF, missing KV key, stats inconsistent with the map, network error, or nothing to pin (`--no-nonexpert` without stats).
- 2 usage.
- 3 missing GGUF, map or stats file, or missing huggingface_hub.
- 4 refused: the budget is smaller than the mandatory non-expert set, or fits nothing. stderr line: `pigemma.gguf_map: REFUSED: ...`. No files are written.

Python API:
- `build_map(path_or_id, page_size=16384, *, backend='auto', with_sha=True) -> GgufMap`
- `build_map_from_header(hdr, page_size, gguf_label=None, sha256_prefix=None)`
- `read_gguf_header(path_or_stream, backend='auto', file_size=None, label=None) -> GgufHeader(path, version, file_size, alignment, data_offset, fields, tensors[TensorRecord(name, type_id, type, shape, n_bytes, offset)], backend)`
- `load_map(path|dict|GgufMap)`
- `GgufMap` is a read-only Mapping over the map.json dict:
  - Properties: gguf, gguf_basename, file_size, page_size, n_layer, n_expert, n_expert_used, tensors, expert_layers, summary, moe_layers, is_moe, path.
  - Methods: tensor(name), tensors_of_kind(*kinds), nonexpert_tensors(), expert_layer(il), expert_parts(il), expert_ranges(il, e) -> [(offset, length) per expert tensor], expert_unit_bytes_at(il), kv_bytes(n_ctx, cache_type='f16'|'q8_0'|...), to_dict(), save(path), GgufMap.load(path).
- `classify_tensor(name) -> (kind, layer)`
- `aligned(offset, length, page=16384, limit=None) -> (offset, length)`: floors the start, ceils the end, and `limit` clamps the end to the file size.
- `merge_ranges([(off, len)]) -> merged`: overlapping or touching ranges are merged.
- `kv_bytes_for(...)`, `kv_bytes_per_token_f16(...)`
- `plan_hotset(map, stats|None, budget_bytes, *, page_size=16384, include_nonexpert=True, per_layer_min=0, rank='count', min_hits=0, stats_path=None, map_sha256=None) -> dict`
- `write_hotset(hs, out_json, ranges_txt=None) -> (json_path, ranges_path)`
- `format_ranges_txt(hs)`, `read_ranges_txt(path_or_text) -> {header:{gguf,size,page,budget}, comments, ranges:[{offset,length,kind,layer,expert}]}` (strict, uses the pinner's grammar)
- `ranges_txt_path(out_json)`, `load_stats(path)`, `format_summary(map)`
- `catalog_refresh(catalog_path, *, ids, refresh_all, split, dry_run, out_path, token, api, opener, today) -> report`
- `format_catalog_json(obj)`: reproduces catalog.json's layout byte for byte.
- `hf_token(token_file=None)`
- Exceptions: GgufMapError(ValueError) > MissingKeyError(.key); HotsetError(ValueError) > HotsetBudgetError.
- Constants: GGML_TYPES, KINDS, DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE.

map.json (superset of data_formats):
- Top level: format_version 1, generator, created_at, backend, gguf (repo-relative when inside the repo), gguf_basename, gguf_sha256_prefix, gguf_version, file_size, data_offset, alignment, page_size, arch, n_layer, n_expert, n_expert_used, n_embd, n_ff, n_ff_exp, n_head, head_count_kv[], key_length, key_length_swa, value_length, value_length_swa, sliding_window, sliding_pattern[bool], context_length, n_tensors, moe_layers[], tensors[], expert_layers[], summary.
- tensors[]: {name, type, shape (ne order), n_bytes, offset (absolute), kind, layer}.
- expert_layers[]: {layer, gate_up|gate|up|down: {offset, n_bytes, nb_expert}, n_expert, unit_bytes}.
- summary: nonexpert_bytes, expert_bytes, expert_unit_bytes (int mean), expert_unit_bytes_min, expert_unit_bytes_max, expert_unit_bytes_aligned_mean, n_moe_layers, expert_bytes_per_token_worst (= n_expert_used × sum of per-layer units), nonexpert_bytes_per_token, bytes_per_token_worst, head, head_bytes, embd_row_bytes, kv_bytes_per_token_f16, kv_bytes_f16_at_4096, kv_bytes_q8_at_4096, tensor_bytes_total, file_data_bytes, bytes_per_kind{}, tensors_per_kind{}.
- Dense models: n_expert 0, expert_layers [], all expert figures 0.

hotset.json:
- Spec keys: gguf, map_sha256 (SHA-256 of the map file), stats (path or null), page_size, budget_bytes, total_bytes (always <= budget_bytes), nonexpert_included, n_experts, expert_coverage_fraction (null without stats), rank, ranges[{offset, length, kind, layer, expert, hits, n_parts}] (sorted, aligned, merged, clamped to the file size).
- Extra keys: format_version, generator, created_at, gguf_basename, gguf_size, map, raw_bytes, page_overhead_bytes, nonexpert_bytes_aligned, n_expert_items_total, expert_weight_coverage_fraction, per_layer_min, min_hits, n_ranges, bytes_by_kind, per_layer_selected[{layer, n}], experts_selected[[layer, e, freq]] in selection order.

hotset.ranges.txt:
- Line 1: `# pigemma-ranges v1 gguf=<basename> size=<bytes> page=<page> budget=<bytes>`
- Then 3 comment lines.
- Then `offset length # kind=<k> layer=<l|-> expert=<e|->`
- ASCII, LF line endings.

Generated artifacts (both page_size 16384, built with the gguf-py reader):
- results/map26.json (131 KB)
- traces/h2/map31.json (155 KB)

open_issues: nonexpert_bytes_per_token differs between map.json and catalog.json. map.json uses the spec formula (all read-every-token kinds including 'other', plus the tied token_embd head, plus one embedding row): 1,577,174,398 B for the 26B and 17,635,170,858 B for the 31B. catalog.json and tests/test_catalog.py require nonexpert_bytes_per_token == nonexpert_bytes, so catalog-refresh writes the catalog convention. The values are 2,310 B (26B) and 4,410 B (31B) apart.

Kind 'attn' covers only the attn_{q,k,v,output} matmul weights; q/k norms and attn_norm count as 'norm'. So bytes_per_kind.attn = 624,476,160 B for the 26B, versus 624,885,760 in FACTS/catalog, which include the norms. Totals are unaffected. 'layer_output_scale' counts as norm, 'rope_freqs' as other.

KV for the 31B: kv_bytes_q8_at_4096 = 623.9 MB (f16 1,174.4 MB). This is an upper bound that counts K and V on every layer, including the K==V global layers, and caps sliding layers at the 1024-token window. The feasibility spec's constant KV_Q8_4K = 420e6 for the 31B does not match it; the 26B figure (156.0 MB) does match its 160e6. The feasibility owner should take the value from the map or document the difference.

For the tests agent: conftest's planned tiny_moe_gguf with feed_forward_length 48 cannot quantize ffn_down [48,64] to Q4_0 (ne[0] must be a multiple of 32). My test uses n_ff 96 and builds its own GGUF, so it does not depend on conftest.

'auto' prefers gguf-py's GGUFReader, as the spec says: about 11 s per real model on Windows. The stdlib reader is about 0.12 s and is tested to give identical maps. Scripts that rebuild maps often can pass --backend stdlib.

hotset refuses (exit 4, no files written) when the budget cannot hold the mandatory non-expert set (1,578,169,344 B aligned at 16 KiB for the 26B). pi/06_pin_hotset.sh should report exit 4 to the operator, or deliberately rerun with --no-nonexpert. It should not treat exit 4 as a crash.
The first non-expert range is floored to a page boundary, so it starts inside the GGUF header (15,810,560 for the 26B at 16 KiB). The pinner locks a few KB of header; this is harmless.

catalog-refresh queries the 'main' revision and updates 'revision' and 'sha256' if main has moved; it does not pin the recorded revision. If no HF_TOKEN-style env variable is set, it reads the token from HF_TOKEN_FILE if that file exists (per FACTS). The token is never printed. The listed repos are ungated.

I generated results/map26.json and traces/h2/map31.json because run_order_today asked the gguf_map agent to run build on both real GGUFs, and dependents reference those paths. Both are tracked by .gitignore rules (.json under results/ and traces/) and contain a created_at timestamp.

entries.summary: Stdlib-only Pi 5 feasibility verdict module. It reads facts.json and catalog.json, optionally merged with measured io_mem.json, sim.json LRU hit rates and calibration.json. Output is one row per runnable model/quant: FITS_REPACKED, FITS_MAPPED, STREAM_OK, STREAM_SLOW, NOT_VIABLE, NEVER_GOOD_SPEED or NO_DISK. Each row carries the projected tok/s and per-input sources, a recommended model with llama.cpp flags and its MTP draft, protected-host and busy refusals, and exit codes 0/1/2/3/4. The CLI prints a table plus details, writes --json, and with --emit env prints shell-safe KEY=value lines. Results on the four Pi profiles with assumed catalog numbers: 4GB+microSD gives all 26b rows NOT_VIABLE, exit 3, or exit 4 when the host is protected. 8GB+USB3 26b-q4 is STREAM_OK at 1.46 tok/s, matching the hand arithmetic. 8GB+NVMe Gen3 is STREAM_OK at 1.94 tok/s with -nr flags. On 16GB+NVMe Gen3, 26b-q4 is FITS_MAPPED with repack false and flags '-nr -lm mmap+mlock -t 4 -c 4096 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0', at 2.73 tok/s in-RAM bound. 31b is always NEVER_GOOD_SPEED with the s/token arithmetic, e.g. 20.8 s/token streamed on 16GB NVMe Gen3. All tok/s are projections.
entries.interface_notes:
CLI: python3 -m pigemma.feasibility --facts F|- [--catalog pigemma/data/catalog.json] [--want 26b|31b|<model-id>] [--sim results/h1/sim.json] [--json OUT|-] [--emit env] [--io-mem auto|none|PATH] [--calibration auto|none|PATH] [--device NAME] [--threads N] [--ctx N] [--os-reserve-gib X] [--max-loadavg X] [--emulated] [--quiet] [--log-level L].

Exit codes: 0 = some row is FITS_* or STREAM_OK. 1 = usage or input error; argparse errors are remapped to 1 because 2 is taken. 2 = the best row is STREAM_SLOW or a runnable NEVER_GOOD_SPEED. 3 = nothing viable, or NO_DISK. 4 = refused (protected or busy host).

Auto behaviour: io_mem 'auto' merges results/pi/io_mem.json and calibration 'auto' uses results/pi/calibration.json when present; 'none' disables either. Environment read by the CLI only: THREADS, CTX, OS_RESERVE_GIB, DENY_HOSTS and PROTECTED_SERVICE_GLOBS (space or comma lists that join the catalog lists), PIGEMMA_MAX_LOADAVG, PIGEMMA_EMULATED=1.

Output streams: without --emit, the report goes to stdout; with --emit env or --json -, the report goes to stderr.

--emit env lines, every value shlex-quoted: MODEL_ID, MODEL_REPO, MODEL_FILE, MODEL_BYTES, MODEL_QUANT, MODEL_FAMILY, MODEL_SHA256, MODEL_REVISION, MODEL_URL, LLAMA_FLAGS, FITS_REPACKED (0/1), DRAFT_ID, DRAFT_REPO, DRAFT_FILE, DRAFT_BYTES, DRAFT_SHA256, DRAFT_SPEC_TYPE, PIN_BUDGET_BYTES (0 for FITS rows), VERDICT, VERDICT_EXIT, PROJECTED_TOK_S. MODEL_ID and LLAMA_FLAGS are empty when refused or not viable. Both `eval $(...)` and `eval "$(...)"` were verified in bash.

--json top-level keys: tool, version, kind='projected', created_at, ok, exit_code, runnable, host_refused, busy, refusal_reasons, rows_informational_only, want, hit_source ('assumed'|'simulated'), host{...}, device{name, matched_catalog_device, match_reason, ram_total_bytes, ram_available_bytes, os_reserve_bytes, compute_buffers_bytes, n_ctx, threads, mem_bw_gbps{value,source}, storage{type,class,seq_read_mbps,rand_read_3mb_mbps,access_ms}, sources}, assumptions{name:{value,unit,source}}, rows[], recommended (a row plus draft{id,repo,file,bytes,sha256,spec_type,url,note}) or null, llama_flags, fits_repacked, reasons[] (the last entry is always RECOMMENDATION_LINE), recommendation_line, inputs.

Row keys: model_id, family, kind, quant, bytes, repo, file, sha256, revision, url, verdict, verdict_without_disk, fits_mapped, fits_repacked, runnable, eligible, mode, usable_bytes, kv_bytes, os_reserve_bytes, compute_buffers_bytes, expert_cache_bytes, resident_fraction, hit_rate, hit_kind, hit_source, miss_bytes_per_token, n_miss_per_token, t_ram_s, t_io_s, tok_s, s_per_token, tok_s_kind='projected', tok_s_source, flags, pin_budget_bytes, disk_ok, present_bytes, placeholder, reason, details.

Python API:
- load_catalog(path=None, io_mem=None) -> dict. io_mem may be a path or a dict. It never rewrites the file and never auto-merges. A merge sets source 'measured: ...', records catalog['_io_mem']={host,device,...}, and synthesizes a profile for an unknown device name.
- verdict(facts, catalog=None, want=None, sim=None, *, calibration=None, device=None, threads=None, n_ctx=None, os_reserve_bytes=None, extra_deny_hosts=(), extra_service_globs=(), max_loadavg1=None, emulated=None, check_present=True) -> Verdict. Verdict has ok, exit_code, rows, recommended, reasons, host_refused, busy, refusal_reasons, device, host, want, hit_source, assumptions, recommendation_line, the properties runnable and refused, and to_dict(). facts, catalog, sim and calibration each accept a dict or a path.
- Helpers: merge_io_mem, load_facts, load_calibration, resolve_device, storage_class_for, interpolate_curve, kv_bytes, nominal_ram_gb, tier_os_reserve, quant_bpw, flags_for, emit_env, format_table, main(argv, environ).
- Constants: FITS_REPACKED, FITS_MAPPED, STREAM_OK, STREAM_SLOW, NOT_VIABLE, NEVER_GOOD_SPEED, NO_DISK, VERDICTS, RECOMMENDATION_LINE, KV_Q8_4K, COMPUTE_BUFFERS, MIN_STREAM_CACHE, MIN_FREE_RAM_TO_RUN, LLAMA_EFFICIENCY, BUSY_LOADAVG1, DISK_FACTOR, FLAGS_*.

Optional facts keys accepted beyond the data_formats spec: device (catalog device name), cgroup_mem_max (bytes; caps RAM for --memory containers), emulated (bool). memlock_limit is read as ulimit -l kB or 'unlimited'. The NVMe class comes from pcie_link_speed via catalog.nvme_link_speed_class; '8.0 GT/s PCIe' maps to nvme-gen3.

open_issues: Spec conflict: '31b always NEVER_GOOD_SPEED' vs the FITS formula. The 31B UD-IQ2_XXS (8.5 GB) fits a 16 GB Pi. Resolution: a dense row that fits but projects below selection.viable_stream_tok_s in RAM is NEVER_GOOD_SPEED with runnable=true when it reaches at least 0.3 tok/s. The best such row gives exit 2, so `--want 31b` on 16 GB yields exit 2 with 31b-q3_k_s at about 0.49 tok/s. Its FITS_REPACKED margin is only about 30 MB on a nominal 16e9 RAM; the real MemTotal decides.

RECOMMENDATION_LINE is printed verbatim per spec ('8 GB + USB3: weak'), but the assumed-curve arithmetic gives STREAM_OK at 1.46 tok/s for 26b-q4 on the catalog pi5-8gb-usb3 profile. The docs writers should reconcile the wording with the numbers.

facts.json carries no device name, so the device profile is derived from the facts. A catalog device is used only when named explicitly, when io_mem.json was measured on the same hostname, or when RAM tier and storage class both match; otherwise storage_classes plus the RAM-tier rule apply. The pi/lib/common.sh collect_facts author should add an optional cgroup_mem_max (bytes) for the emulated --memory-capped containers; otherwise MemTotal reports the Docker VM's ~31 GB.
Deviation: the busy loadavg1 limit is 2.0 * max(1, nproc/4). That is 2.0 on a 4-core Pi and 6.0 in a 12-vCPU emulated container. It can be overridden with --max-loadavg or PIGEMMA_MAX_LOADAVG.
Usage and input errors exit 1, not argparse's default 2, because exit 2 means 'only slow streaming possible' to every pi/*.sh script.
STREAM rows reaching at least 1 tok/s but failing a STREAM_OK precondition (cache below 2 GB, or storage unknown or microSD) are STREAM_SLOW. The literal spec left them unclassified.

KV constants (160e6 for the 26B, 420e6 for the 31B at 4096 context, q8_0) are used as given and scaled by max(1, n_ctx/4096). My rough estimate for the 31B is closer to 0.5-0.6 GB, so they should be cross-checked against gguf_map kv_bytes. A catalog model field kv_bytes_q8_at_4096 overrides them.

io_mem merge choices: seq = max(qd1, qd8); rand_3mb = qd1 (conservative, falls back to qd4); mem_bw = max over read_gbps_by_threads (falls back to copy, then triad). The CLI auto-merges results/pi/io_mem.json and results/pi/calibration.json when present; load_catalog() alone never does.

NO_DISK uses the spec's 1.05 x file bytes, minus any partially downloaded file found under model_dir. pi_config.env's MIN_FREE_DISK_FACTOR=1.1, used by pi/04, is stricter. Draft sidecar bytes are not counted toward disk.
The emitted draft is the family's MTP sidecar, and its note says MTP never drafted on the desktop and DFlash was slower.

tests/fixtures/facts_*.json (owned by the tests/conftest.py author) do not exist yet. test_feasibility uses inline facts and skips the loose fixture-invariant check until they appear; it expects the 4gb fixture to give exit 3 or 4 and all 31b rows NEVER_GOOD_SPEED.

entries.summary:
I wrote tools/probe/probe.cpp (pigemma-probe, C++17, links llama-common + llama). It builds cleanly with the official Docker check (cmake -S /work/tools -B /tmp/tb, Release). No warnings come from probe.cpp; two jinja-header warnings are silenced by a pragma around #include "chat.h".

It has three cb_eval modes. names lists sorted unique tensor names. moe-trace writes a .moetrace with its .tokens.bin and .gen.txt sidecars. act-dump writes fp16 L<il>.<kind>.npy files with a fixed 128-byte header, plus phase.u8, tokens.bin, meta.json and gen.txt.

Input is one of three kinds:
- -p/-f text, split into fresh-context chunks with BOS inserted.
- --gen-prompts JSON.
- --replay of an i32 stream, with optional --replay-range and --replay-chunks.

Other behaviour:
- Greedy --gen after each chunk; generated tokens are recorded as phase 1.
- --probs-top P takes the top-P of ffn_moe_probs.
- --io-csv writes one row per ubatch on Linux, from /proc/self/io, stat and status.
- warmup is always false, every tensor is read through its nb[] strides, and the type and shape of each recorded tensor are checked (exit 4 on a mismatch).
- After each call the probe checks that each layer received exactly chunk_len columns (exit 4).
- On SIGINT/SIGTERM it closes the outputs cleanly; a second signal patches n_records and exits immediately.
- Every exit path prints one PIGEMMA_SUMMARY line.

Smoke runs, all MEASURED in Docker on the desktop under `python -m pigemma.paths lock --hold`, -t 6, with no other llama process running:
- 26B moe-trace smoke (-f en_tech, --chunk-tokens 64 --gen 8 --tokens 72): 72 records of 736 B, 30 layers. `python -m pigemma.trace validate` passes and the weight sums are 0.9997 to 1.0003. Layer 0, token 0 routes to experts [102,79,114,81,58,83,54,46], the same ids llama-debug printed in FACTS. Prefill ran at 37.1 tok/s, generation at 13.0 tok/s, and the callback cost 4.6 ms. The run wrote tests/fixtures/golden_26b_72tok.moetrace, and tests/test_trace.py::test_golden_26b_trace_validates passes.
- names on the 26B: 2129 names, including ffn_moe_topk-0, ffn_moe_weights_norm-0, ffn_norm_2-0 and result_output.
- act-dump on the 31B (--layers 0 --tokens 8): L0.ffn_geglu.npy has shape (8, 21504) and ffn_norm/ffn_out have shape (8, 5376). The headers are byte-identical to np.save, and pigemma.trace acts reads the directory. Generation ran at 2.05 tok/s.
- moe-trace on the 31B exits 4 and leaves no files behind.
entries.interface_notes:
CLI: pigemma-probe --mode names|moe-trace|act-dump -m MODEL.gguf, plus any llama.cpp COMMON flag (-p -f -t -tb -c -b -ub -nr -lm -ctk -ctv -fa ...). The probe flags below are removed from argv before common_params_parse; --opt=value also works.

Probe flags:
- --trace-out F: moe-trace output. Sidecars are F.tokens.bin and F.gen.txt; parent dirs are created.
- --gen N: default 0. With --gen-prompts the default is each item's max_tokens.
- --probs-top P: moe-trace only, 0..n_expert.
- --chunk-tokens N: default 1024, minimum 2. Text chunks include the inserted BOS.
- --max-chunks N: process at most N chunks.
- --tokens T: stop after T recorded tokens (prefill + generated) in every mode. For act-dump it is also the npy T_MAX, default 512.
- --chat: wrap prompts as a user turn plus generation prompt.
- --chat-style template|gemma4|gemma3: default template, i.e. the GGUF chat template with thinking off.
- --chat-think: enable the thinking channel in the template.
- --parse-special: parse special-token text in raw -p/-f input.
- --gen-prompts F.json: a list of strings, or objects with prompt and optional max_tokens and id; an object holding a "prompts" list is also accepted.
- --replay tokens.bin, --replay-range A:B (Python slice), --replay-chunks F.json (an object with a chunks list of {n_prompt, n_gen}, e.g. <trace>.meta.json).
- --io-csv F: Linux only.
- --layers 5,20,35,50 and --kinds ffn_norm,ffn_geglu,ffn_out: act-dump defaults.
- --act-out DIR.
- --corpus-id S: default is the -f stem, 'prompt' for -p, the prompts-file stem, or 'replay'.
- -h/--help prints a 3-line banner, the llama.cpp help, then the PIGEMMA section.

Exit codes:
- 0 ok.
- 2 usage, including bad probe flags, bad llama args, no input, a chunk larger than n_ctx, a replay token outside the vocabulary, or layers >= n_layer.
- 3 load, compute or output-I/O failure.
- 4 contract violation, including moe-trace on a dense model.
- 128+signal when interrupted (130 SIGINT, 143 SIGTERM).
- 1 only from llama.cpp's own argument parser on internal exceptions.

Summary line: stderr gets 'PIGEMMA_SUMMARY ' followed by compact JSON. It has every TRACE_FORMAT 4.5 key, plus n_p_eval, n_eval, t_prefill_wall_ms, t_gen_wall_ms, wall_tok_s_prompt, wall_tok_s_gen (the probe's wall clock including the callback, a source separate from llama_perf), wall_ms, n_ctx, n_threads, interrupted, error, probe_version, llama_build and llama_commit. In names mode the names go to stdout, sorted by byte value.

.moetrace output:
- Exactly TRACE_FORMAT section 3: header with the 16384 B reserve, moe_layers = layers where ffn_moe_topk was seen in chunk 0, header written at the first flush and patched at close with n_records written last.
- Optional header keys: chat, gen_max, replay {tokens_file, range}, notes.
- Extra keys: probe_version, n_threads_batch, input (text|gen-prompts|replay), chat_style.
- chunks[] entries may carry prompt_index and prompt_id.
- gen.txt holds '\n--- chunk i ---\n' plus pieces rendered with special=true.

act-dump meta.json keys: model (the GGUF basename), model_name, gguf_path, gguf_size_bytes, layers, kinds {name: ne0} (ints only), n_tokens, dtype, phase_file, tokens_file, gen_file, chunks, corpus_id, llama_build, llama_commit, arch, n_layer, n_embd, n_ctx, n_batch, n_ubatch, n_threads, t_max, created_at, flags, complete, error. Optional: f16_nonfinite, chat_style, notes, probe_version.

io.csv: header exactly IO_CSV_HEADER, then one row per ubatch, emitted when the callback sees result_output. MEASURED: with -ub 1 there is one row per token, including ubatches that produce no logits. The first row counts from the first llama_process after load.

Binary location: tools/build-linux-x86/bin/pigemma-probe after `pc/docker_run.sh build-tools`. I built into a scratch volume and removed it afterwards, so that directory does not hold my build.
entries.self_test:

Model runs, MEASURED, all under `python -m pigemma.paths lock --hold`:

This is the ub=1 vs ub=512 numeric effect TRACE_FORMAT 3.8 anticipates, not a bug.
- C. 31B act-dump --layers 0 --tokens 8 (5 prompt + 3 generated): shapes (8,21504) and (8,5376), finite, headers equal to np.save's, phase [0,0,0,0,0,1,1,1], tokens [2,818,5279,529,7001,563,9079,236761], i.e. "The capital of France" -> " is Paris.". io.csv had 4 rows.
- D. 31B moe-trace: exit 4 with "moe-trace needs an MoE model", and the outputs were removed.

Full `pytest -q` passes with the fixture present. I ran 2 extra small model jobs beyond the spec's list (B used the chat path; E covered replay and io.csv); both were short decodes of at most 24 tokens.

After the golden run I made only non-format changes: llama_synchronize after each llama_process, extra summary keys, the kinds-null fix and the summary trace_out fix. The golden bytes are unaffected, and the final source was rebuilt and re-tested without a model.
open_issues: DEVIATION (D-a): the manifest's --chat literal '<start_of_turn>user...<end_of_turn>...<start_of_turn>model' is not Gemma 4's format. The 26B vocab has no <start_of_turn>; the real markers are <|turn> (id 105) and <turn|> (id 106). --chat therefore renders the GGUF's own chat template with thinking off, and --chat-style gemma3 keeps the manifest literal. The Python consumers (quality.py, trace_collect.sh) should know this; results/smoke-* used the old literal as plain text.

Load time over the Docker 9p bind mount with -nr (mmap), MEASURED: the 26B took 884 s on the first load and 449-473 s on later loads, and the 31B took 1082 s, then 602 s. The VM page cache (31 GB, swapping) does not keep a 14-18 GB file reliably. The one-process-per-corpus-file plan in pc/trace_collect.sh --quick (about 7 loads) would spend about 1 hour loading. Suggestion for the trace_collect author: concatenate the files and use --corpus-id per run, or put the GGUF on the pigemma-models Docker volume as pagecache_limit.sh does.

Replay fidelity, MEASURED: a -ub 1 replay of a trace collected at ub=512 agrees on 97.97% of expert slots; the differences are near-ties on the 8th expert that propagate to deeper layers. The pagecache_limit/cache_sim comparison (E5) should expect this small mismatch, or collect the reference trace with the same -ub.
--tokens and --max-chunks are additions (D-c), and the manifest's --tokens was act-dump only. trace_collect.sh --smoke should pass `--chunk-tokens 64 --gen 8 --tokens 72` to get exactly 72 records.

The default n_ctx when -c is absent is max(4096, chunk+gen+8) instead of the 262144 training context (D-e). Chunks longer than n_batch are decoded in sub-batches (D-d). Raw -p/-f text is tokenised literally (parse_special=false, D-b), and replay never inserts BOS (D-f).

llama_perf counters only update inside llama_synchronize, and llama_perf_context reports max(1,n). The probe now syncs after each llama_process and also reports its own wall-clock tok/s (wall_tok_s_*) as separate summary keys. tok_s_* stays llama_perf-sourced.

The golden fixture (tests/fixtures/golden_26b_72tok.moetrace + .tokens.bin + .gen.txt) was written by this agent because the probe's test field names it; it lives under tests/ (the tests agent's area). It records the container path /work/... in gguf_path and flags. The .gen.txt continuation is '-<channel|>ly, $N$ experts' (prompt cut mid-sentence, raw text, no chat).

Not exercised with a model: --probs-top>0, act-dump on the 26B with MoE-specific kinds, multi-sub-batch chunks (chunk > n_batch), SIGINT handling, and the header-rewrite path (more than about 150 chunks). The code paths exist and compile.

Not compiled on aarch64: the build was checked only on x86-64 gcc 13.3 in Docker. The code is portable C++17/POSIX, but the Pi (gcc 14) and arm64-emulator builds of the probe are untested; an emulated llama build takes about 22 min per FACTS.
The tools/build-linux-x86/bin/pigemma-probe binary is not produced by this agent (I built into a scratch volume, since deleted); run `pc/docker_run.sh build-tools` to place it.

entries.summary:
I wrote tools/pinner/pinner.c (C11, Linux only, libc only; `#error` on anything that is not Linux). It builds through tools/CMakeLists.txt with the flags the CMake file really emits (`-D_GNU_SOURCE -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2`). It also builds warning-free without `-D_GNU_SOURCE`, at `-O3`, and with stricter checks (`-Wshadow -Wformat=2 -Wformat-truncation=2 -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`) on gcc 13.3 x86-64 and on gcc 14.2 aarch64 (emulated Debian 13).

What it does, following the manifest:
- **Reads** the hotset.ranges.txt grammar from TRACE_FORMAT §9.3.
- **Aligns** every range to sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE). requested_bytes is the merged set of pages, so a page shared by two ranges counts once, the same way RLIMIT_MEMLOCK and VmLck count.
- **Guards** run before any page is touched (exit 3, numbers printed): --max-bytes; the RLIMIT_MEMLOCK soft limit (with the 'ulimit -l unlimited' / /etc/security/limits.d/90-pigemma.conf / CAP_IPC_LOCK fix text); and requested + 512 MiB against available memory. Available memory is the smaller of MemAvailable and the container's cgroup headroom, because inside a docker --memory container /proc/meminfo shows the host.
- **Locks** with mmap(MAP_SHARED) of the whole file, then per range in file order (the file lists the most important ranges first), in 64 MiB chunks: madvise(MADV_WILLNEED), then mlock. EPERM and EAGAIN are handled as specified (EAGAIN: touch the pages, retry once).
- **Checks residency** with mincore(): before and after locking with --verify, plus per-kind totals.
- **Reports** one summary line (JSON with --json) carrying all manifest keys, then either exits (--once) or writes the pidfile and waits for SIGTERM, then munlockall, munmap, removes the pidfile.

Two changes beyond the spec, both measured or required:
1. **Read-ahead before locking.** mlock alone pulled cold pages in one at a time: madvise(MADV_RANDOM), which the pinner sets on its own mapping, turns off read-around, and the kernel caps WILLNEED read-ahead at the device read-ahead window. Measured in Docker on a cold 667.6 MiB hot set: 21.3–23.1 s (30–33 MB/s). I added a sequential pread() of each chunk through an 8 MiB buffer before mlock, skipped when the chunk is already cached: 1.42–1.44 s (about 490 MB/s), two runs each. `--no-warm` turns it off for comparison.
2. **Protected-host guard.** FACTS.md was updated during my run: context-friend-1 is now the real target Pi, and its safety rules say "no mlock of model weights". The pinner refuses to lock (exit 3) when:
   - the hostname is a protected host (default context-friend-1, extendable with PIGEMMA_PROTECTED_HOSTS);
   - or a process runs whose name, or a path component of one of its arguments, starts with contextfriend or context-friend (extendable with PIGEMMA_PROTECTED_SERVICES).

   The defaults mirror catalog.json. Only an explicit `--allow-protected-host` flag overrides it; there is deliberately no environment-variable override. `--verify-only` locks nothing and is always allowed.
entries.interface_notes:
BINARY: tools/build-linux-x86/bin/pinner (Docker build) and tools/build/bin/pinner (Pi build), CMake target "pinner".

CLI: pinner --gguf FILE --ranges hotset.ranges.txt [--verify] [--once] [--max-bytes N] [--pidfile P] [--json] [--hold-seconds S] [--no-mem-check] [--best-effort] [--no-warm] [--quiet] [--allow-protected-host]
- Also: pinner --gguf FILE --ranges F --verify-only [--json]; and --help / -h / --version.
- '--opt=value' works too.
- --max-bytes takes plain decimal digits only.
- --hold-seconds takes 0 to 31536000 and may be fractional.

FLAGS NOT IN THE MANIFEST:
- --hold-seconds S: with --once, hold the locks S seconds before exiting (the test field needs this to read VmLck). In daemon mode, stop by itself after S seconds.
- --verify-only: no locking and no guards; prints mincore residency and exits 0. Use it for `pi/06 status` while a daemon runs. A second `--verify --once` would try to lock again, and the memory guard may then refuse, because the daemon's pages no longer count as available.
- --no-mem-check skips the memory guard.
- --best-effort: when RLIMIT_MEMLOCK is too small, lock in file order until the limit is hit (exit 2).
- --no-warm is diagnostic (disables the read-ahead step).
- --quiet silences notes (warnings and errors still print).
- --allow-protected-host: see SAFETY.

RANGES FILE: TRACE_FORMAT §9.3.
- The first non-blank line, if it starts with '# pigemma-ranges', is the header. 'v1' is required, else exit 1.
- The header's size= must equal the file size (exit 1). A different gguf= name only warns; a different page= is re-aligned with a note.
- A file with no header is accepted with a warning.
- Range line: '<offset> <length>' in decimal, spaces or tabs between them, optionally followed by a '#' comment; 'kind=<word>' in that comment labels the range.
- Trailing CR and a UTF-8 BOM are tolerated.
- Exit 1, naming 'file:LINE:', for: a malformed line, length 0, a range beyond EOF, or a file with no ranges.
- Unsorted or overlapping ranges only produce a note or warning.

STDOUT, --json: exactly one line. Manifest keys are always present: requested_bytes, locked_bytes, resident_bytes, ranges, failed, page_size, memlock_limit, vm_lck_kb. Extra keys:
- tool, version, status (ok|partial|refused|interrupted), exit_code, mode (daemon|once|verify-only), pid
- gguf, ranges_file, file_size, header{gguf,size,page,budget} or null
- segments, requested_raw_bytes, resident_before_bytes, not_attempted
- errors{EPERM,ENOMEM,EAGAIN,other}, first_error{line,errno,message} or null
- memlock_hard, memlock_unlimited, cap_ipc_lock
- mem_available_bytes, mem_available_source, max_bytes, mincore_reliable
- verify (ok|mismatch|null)
- kinds{<kind>|'(none)': {ranges, requested_bytes, locked_bytes, resident_bytes, resident_before_bytes}} or null
- lock_s, hold_s (0 = exits now, -1 = until signal, else seconds), reason

Value conventions:
- memlock_limit and memlock_hard are bytes, or null when unlimited.
- resident_bytes is null on a refusal, or when mincore is unreliable (the caller is neither the file's owner, nor has CAP_FOWNER, nor can write the file; Linux 5.0 and later then claims every page is resident).
- requested_bytes is the merged page-aligned set. locked_bytes is the merged set this process actually locked, including the locked part of a range that failed half way. In the normal case vm_lck_kb*1024 == locked_bytes; if VmLck is lower, a warning says mlock looks intercepted (sanitizer or LD_PRELOAD).
- A refusal also prints a JSON summary (status 'refused', with reason).

STDOUT, text mode: 'pinner: status=.. exit=.. mode=.. requested_bytes=.. locked_bytes=.. resident_bytes=.. ranges=.. failed=.. not_attempted=.. page_size=.. memlock_limit=..|unlimited vm_lck_kb=.. segments=.. (...)', then per kind with --verify 'pinner: kind=K ranges= requested_bytes= locked_bytes= resident_bytes= resident_before_bytes= resident_pct=', and 'pinner: reason=..'.

Stderr carries notes, progress every 2 s, warnings, and lines starting 'pinner: hint:' and 'pinner: REFUSED:'. The summary is flushed before the daemon blocks.

EXIT CODES:
- 0: everything locked (or --verify-only finished).
- 2: partial. Some ranges failed or were not tried; locking stops at the first RLIMIT or out-of-memory failure. A daemon still holds what it locked and exits 2 after SIGTERM (the manifest says 0 here).
- 3: refused, by protected host, live pinner on the pidfile, --max-bytes, RLIMIT_MEMLOCK below the request without CAP_IPC_LOCK, or requested + 512 MiB above available memory; or mlock was not permitted and nothing was locked.
- 1: usage, I/O or malformed-file error, unwritable pidfile or stdout, or a stop signal while still locking (status 'interrupted').

PIDFILE: written atomically (temp file, then rename) BEFORE locking starts, so 'summary line present' implies 'pidfile present'. It is written only when the run will hold the locks (daemon mode, or --once with --hold-seconds). Startup refuses (exit 3) if the pidfile names a live process whose name starts with 'pinner'; a dead or foreign pid is treated as stale and replaced. It is removed on exit only if it still holds our pid.

SIGNALS: SIGTERM always stops it. SIGINT and SIGHUP stop it only when they were not ignored at start (nohup, or '&' jobs in non-interactive bash, start with them ignored, and the pinner keeps it that way). SIGPIPE is ignored.

FOR CALLERS:
- pi/06 start: run `nohup pinner ... --verify --json --pidfile pi/out/pinner.pid > pi/out/pinner.log &` and wait for the JSON line; check status/exit_code, do not assume success. stop: kill -TERM "$(cat pidfile)". status: `pinner ... --verify-only --json`. Never pass --allow-protected-host automatically.
- pc/pagecache_limit.sh: run the pinner inside the same --memory container as the probe; locked pages count against that container's memory cap. Docker Desktop is cgroup v1 here (memory.limit_in_bytes); the guard uses it.
- tests/test_pi_scripts.py: Docker containers default to memlock unlimited and root lacks CAP_IPC_LOCK, so `bash -c 'ulimit -l 64; pinner ...'` gives exit 3 with the hint. Use --hold-seconds 2 and read /proc/<pid>/status VmLck. Do not test under ASan (it turns mlock into a no-op). Run test scripts from a file, not as `docker run bash -c '<long script>'`: the container's PID 1 command line is then scanned by the protected-host guard, and a path component like /context-friend... inside it trips the guard.
entries.self_test:
All runs were inside Docker; nothing ran on the Pi or against the real models.

1. **Builds:**
   - Through the real tools/CMakeLists.txt (`cmake -S /work/tools -B /tmp/tb -G Ninja`, `--target pinner`). `ninja -t commands` confirms '-D_GNU_SOURCE -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2'. Built OK.
   - Stand-alone, warning-free with -Werror under: c11 -D_GNU_SOURCE -O2; c11 without the define at -O3; gnu11 with -Wshadow -Wformat=2 -Wformat-truncation=2 -Wformat-overflow=2 -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3. Done on gcc 13.3 (pi-gemma4-build, x86-64) and gcc 14.2 (pi-gemma4-pi-emu:trixie, --platform linux/arm64).
2. **Functional script** (scratchpad pinner_selftest.sh, 71 checks): 71/71 PASS on x86 (both the CMake build and a direct gcc build) and 71/71 PASS on emulated arm64. Coverage:
   - The manifest test, on a 64 MiB random file with 3 unaligned ranges: requested_bytes 5,771,264 == locked == resident, vm_lck_kb 5636 == requested/1024.
   - `--hold-seconds 2`: VmLck 5636 kB while running.
   - `ulimit -l 64`: exit 3, with 'ulimit -l unlimited', '90-pigemma.conf' and 'CAP_IPC_LOCK' in stderr.
   - 9 kinds of malformed line: exit 1 naming the line.
   - --best-effort with ulimit -l 1024: exit 2, locked 528,384, failed 1, not tried 1. ulimit -l 0: EPERM, exit 3.
   - Daemon with pidfile; second instance refused; --verify-only during the daemon; SIGTERM gives exit 0 and the pidfile is removed.
   - --max-bytes; header size mismatch; range beyond EOF; no header; v2 header; text output; ignored vs real SIGINT; daemon --hold-seconds; CRLF+BOM; mincore unreliable as nobody (resident null); unsorted/overlapping ranges; no ranges; CLI errors; stale pidfile; closed stdout (exit 1).
   - Protected-host guard: a fake contextfriend-box process gives exit 3; --verify-only still allowed; --allow-protected-host locks with a warning; a /Context-Friend/ path component matches case-insensitively; both env lists work; a clean host locks.
3. **ASan/UBSan build** through the same script: no sanitizer errors or leaks. The 7 VmLck/EPERM checks fail only because ASan turns mlock into a no-op (VmLck 0), which is why I added the VmLck warning.
4. **cgroup guard** in `docker run --memory=400m`: the 6 MB request was refused, quoting 392.5 MiB of headroom from cgroup v1 memory.limit_in_bytes. With --no-mem-check, a 200 MiB lock succeeded (VmLck 204,800 kB).
5. **Cold 1 GiB file** (sync, then vmtouch -e to 0% cached), 3 ranges / 667.6 MiB: --no-warm took 23.05 and 21.28 s (30–33 MB/s); the default took 1.44 and 1.42 s (~490 MB/s). verify ok every time, and per-kind before/after numbers are correct.
6. **Stop signal while locking** (SIGTERM already pending at start): status interrupted, exit 1, 64 MiB locked before it noticed, pidfile removed.
open_issues: Safety (FACTS.md update during this run): context-friend-1 is now the real target Pi, and its rules forbid mlock of model weights. The pinner refuses to lock there (exit 3) unless --allow-protected-host is given, and that Pi's ulimit -l of 8192 kB would refuse anyway. So E6 pinning on the real Pi needs the operator's explicit approval. Until then E6 can run in Docker via pc/pagecache_limit.sh, and on the Pi only --verify-only (no locking) is allowed. pi/06_pin_hotset.sh must not add --allow-protected-host automatically.

Differs from the manifest: added --verify-only, --hold-seconds (the test field asks for it), --no-mem-check, --best-effort, --no-warm, --quiet and --allow-protected-host. Added the pread read-ahead before mlock (measured 16x faster on cold data). The pidfile is written before locking, not after. A daemon that locked only part of the set holds it and exits 2 after SIGTERM, where the manifest says 0. A stop signal during locking exits 1. memlock_limit uses null for 'unlimited'.

Being lenient on purpose: a ranges file with no '# pigemma-ranges v1' header is accepted with a warning (size not cross-checked), although TRACE_FORMAT says the producer MUST write the header. A header with an unknown version is still exit 1.

The memory guard counts the whole request, including pages already cached (they stop counting as available once locked). With a daemon already holding the set, a second locking pinner may be refused; status checks should use --verify-only.

Not tested on real hardware: 16 KiB pages (Docker and qemu both use 4 KiB; the code only uses the runtime page size), and microSD read-ahead speed on the Pi. The Docker numbers are from overlayfs on the WSL2 disk, not Pi measurements.

The protected-service check looks at /proc command lines. A process whose argument has a path component starting with contextfriend or context-friend counts as a protected service, including a shell whose script text contains such a path. Refusing on a false match is the safe direction, but test harnesses should run scripts from files.

The functional self-test script stays in my scratchpad (pinner_selftest.sh), not in the repo. Whoever writes tests/test_pi_scripts.py can port parts of it. I did not write any test file in the repo because the spec's test field points at that file, which another agent owns.

pc/docker_run.sh and pc/pagecache_limit.sh: Docker Desktop containers already start with memlock unlimited (measured), so no --ulimit flag is needed. Pinning inside a --memory container charges the locked pages to that container's memory cap.

entries.summary:
pc/docker_run.sh (bash, 1118 lines, stdlib shell only) is written, linted (bash -n) and tested for real against Docker Desktop.

Core behaviour (spec):
- Runs a command in pi-gemma4-build:latest with the repo bind-mounted at /work.
- The repo path comes from the script's own location (pwd -W on Git Bash, cygpath -m as fallback, plain pwd on Linux/WSL).
- MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 and MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' are exported.
- Default flags: --rm -i --init. -t only when both stdin and stdout are terminals.
- --memory M also sets --memory-swap=M. --cpus, repeatable --volume, --name.
- The image can be overridden with PIGEMMA_IMAGE or --image.
- Refuses with exit 4 if the docker CLI is missing, `docker info` fails, or the daemon is in Windows-container mode.
- The exit code of `docker run` is forwarded.

Subcommands:
- build-tools: the exact spec cmake configure + build into /work/tools/build-linux-x86, then prints the binary paths, `pigemma-probe --help | head -3` and `membw --version`.
- vm-df: `df -P -B1 /` in a container plus `docker system df` plus key=value lines.
- build-image: builds docker/Dockerfile.build, or docker/Dockerfile.pi-emu with --pi-emu.

Additions beyond the spec, all verified:
- A python->python3 shim. The images have no `python`, but the manifest's callers write `python -m pigemma...`.
- Container env: UTF-8 settings, PYTHONPATH=/work, a pycache prefix outside the bind mount, and forwarded PIGEMMA_* variables.
- PIGEMMA_LOCK_FILE is translated to its /work path. A host `pigemma.paths lock --hold -- bash pc/docker_run.sh -- python -m pigemma.paths lock --hold -- ...` is therefore inherited in the container instead of deadlocking.
- --pi-emu: arm64 emulated Pi image, PIGEMMA_EMULATED=1, and the pigemma-arm64-llama volume at /opt/llama with PIGEMMA_LLAMA_BIN=/opt/llama/build/bin.
- --dry-run prints the docker command(s) without calling docker.
- On mintty, a -t refusal is retried once without -t.
- build-tools safeguards: refuses while the bench lock is held, serialises concurrent builds with flock, runs under nice, and builds only targets whose source exists.
- vm-df also detects the Windows drive that holds docker_data.vhdx.
entries.interface_notes:
INVOCATION
- `bash pc/docker_run.sh [options] -- <command...>` from Git Bash, from any cwd.
- From PowerShell or Windows Python, call Git Bash explicitly. A bare `bash` there can resolve to WSL's C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe. This was observed with Python subprocess. pigemma.paths `lock --hold` already maps a bare bash to Git Bash. Under WSL bash the script falls back to POSIX paths and prints a hint.
- The container's working directory is /work. Relative paths in the command are repo-relative, e.g. tools/build-linux-x86/bin/membw.

GLOBAL OPTIONS (before the subcommand or `--`; both `--opt V` and `--opt=V` work)
- `--memory M` emits --memory=M --memory-swap=M. Validated: digits[.digits][b|k/m/g/t[i][b]].
- `--cpus N` (positive number).
- `--volume SRC:DST[:MODE]`, repeatable. Named volumes and drive paths pass unchanged; relative or Git-Bash paths are made absolute and converted with cygpath -m.
- `--name N`
- `--env K=V` or `--env K`, repeatable. Wins over the automatic variables.
- `--workdir DIR` (relative means under /work).
- `--image I`, `--platform P`.
- `--pi-emu`, `--no-llama-volume`.
- `--tty` / `--no-tty`, `--no-stdin` (omit -i), `--no-init`, `--no-shim`, `--as-root`.
- `--docker-arg A`, repeatable raw `docker run` argument.
- `--dry-run` prints `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 docker ...` lines to stdout and exits 0 without touching docker. Also accepted after a subcommand.
- `--verbose` logs to stderr. Also accepted after a subcommand.
- `-h`/`--help`, `--version` (prints "pc/docker_run.sh 1.0.0").
- A bare `-v` is rejected as ambiguous.

ENVIRONMENT KNOBS
PIGEMMA_IMAGE, PIGEMMA_PI_EMU_IMAGE (default pi-gemma4-pi-emu:trixie), PIGEMMA_VMDF_IMAGE, PIGEMMA_ARM64_LLAMA_VOLUME (default pigemma-arm64-llama), PIGEMMA_DOCKER_TTY=auto|0|1, PIGEMMA_DOCKER_STDIN=0|1, PIGEMMA_DOCKER_VERBOSE=1, PIGEMMA_BUILD_JOBS=N, PIGEMMA_REQUIRE_ALL_TOOLS=1.

CONTAINER ENVIRONMENT (always set)
- PIGEMMA_IN_CONTAINER=1, PYTHONUTF8=1, PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8, LANG=C.UTF-8.
- PYTHONPATH=/work, PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp/pigemma-pycache.
- PIGEMMA_REPO_HOST=<host repo path, e.g. REPO_ROOT>.

FORWARDED HOST VARIABLES
- Host PIGEMMA_* are forwarded, except: IMAGE, PI_EMU_IMAGE, VMDF_IMAGE, ARM64_LLAMA_VOLUME, DOCKER_*, BASH, GGUF_PY, MODELS_DIR, LLAMA_BIN, TOOLS_BIN, BUILD_JOBS, and any value that looks like a Windows path.
- PIGEMMA_LOCK_FILE is mapped to /work/... when it is inside the repo; otherwise it is dropped with a warning.
- PIGEMMA_LOCK_HELD is forwarded, so a host-held bench lock shows as 'inherited' in the container (verified).
- With --pi-emu the container also gets PIGEMMA_EMULATED=1 and PIGEMMA_LLAMA_BIN=/opt/llama/build/bin (the latter only if the volume exists).

PYTHON SHIM
- The command runs as `/bin/sh -c '<shim>; exec "$@"' pigemma-run <command...>`.
- When `python` is missing, the shim puts /tmp/.pigemma-shim/python -> python3 first on PATH.
- `python -m pigemma.X` therefore works in both images: 3.12 in the build image, 3.13 in pi-emu.

STDIN
- `-i` is on by default. Use `--no-stdin` inside `while read` loops, otherwise docker consumes the loop's input.

SUBCOMMAND: build-tools
- Options: `[--clean] [--jobs N|-jN] [--targets pigemma-probe,pinner,membw] [--require-all] [--ignore-lock]`.
- Configure line, verbatim spec: `cmake -S /work/tools -B /work/tools/build-linux-x86 -G Ninja -DLLAMA_DIR=/work/third_party/llama.cpp -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_AVX2=ON -DGGML_AVX512=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DPIGEMMA_REQUIRE_ALL_TOOLS=OFF|ON`.
- Build line: `nice -n 10 cmake --build ... -j <N, default nproc=12> --target <tools whose source exists>`.
- stdout ends with:
  - `== pigemma tools: /work/tools/build-linux-x86/bin (host: <repo>/tools/build-linux-x86/bin) ==`
  - one line per tool: `%-14s <container path>`, or `(not built: source tools/<src> does not exist yet)`, or `... MISSING after the build`
  - `build info     /work/tools/build-linux-x86/bin/pigemma-tools-build.json`
  - `build time     N s ...`
  - `== pigemma-probe --help | head -3 ==` plus 3 lines (only when the probe was built)
  - `== membw --version ==` plus 1 line.
- Exit codes:
  - 0 ok
  - 3: no tool sources, --require-all with a missing source, a requested target without a source, or a binary missing after the build
  - 4: bench lock held, or another build-tools run holds tools/build-linux-x86/.pigemma-build.lock
  - 1: probe or membw does not run
  - otherwise cmake's own exit code.
- Refused with exit 2 under --pi-emu or a non-amd64 --platform. The aarch64 path is pi/02 inside --pi-emu.

SUBCOMMAND: vm-df
- Text mode:
  - stdout line 1 is the df header and line 2 is `overlay <size> <used> <avail> <pct> /`, so `awk 'NR==2{print $4}'` works.
  - Then a blank line, then `docker system df`, then key=value lines: vm_root_image, vm_root_filesystem, vm_root_size_bytes, vm_root_used_bytes, vm_root_avail_bytes.
  - Git Bash only: host_vm_disk_dir, host_vm_disk_file, host_vm_disk_file_bytes, host_vm_disk_drive_avail_bytes, host_vm_disk_source.
  - Always last: vm_effective_avail_bytes = min(VM root avail, host drive avail).
  - A note goes to stderr.
- `vm-df --bytes` prints only vm_effective_avail_bytes.
- `vm-df --json` prints `{image, vm_root:{filesystem,size_bytes,used_bytes,avail_bytes,mount}, host_vm_disk:{dir,file,file_bytes,drive_avail_bytes,source}|null, vm_effective_avail_bytes, docker_system_df:[{Type,TotalCount,Active,Size,Reclaimable}...], note}`.

SUBCOMMAND: build-image
`[--pi-emu] build-image [--tag T]` runs `docker build -t T -f <repo>/docker/Dockerfile.build <repo>/docker`, or with --pi-emu `--platform linux/arm64` and Dockerfile.pi-emu.

EXIT CODES (wrapper)
- 0 ok; 2 usage; 3 missing (repo layout, a local pi-gemma4-* image, sources, binaries); 4 refused.
- Otherwise the code of `docker run`: the command's own code, 125 for a docker error, 126/127 for not executable / not found (verified: `exit 7` gives 7, an unknown command gives 127).
- Wrapper errors always start with "docker_run:" on stderr.

open_issues: FACTS.md says the Docker VM disk lives on C:. On this desktop it is on F:. Docker Desktop's settings-store.json has CustomWslDistroDir F:\Docker\DockerDesktopWSL, and disk/docker_data.vhdx (101.7 GB) is there, with 797.6 GB free on F:. pc/pagecache_limit.sh's 'Windows C: free >= 18 GB' gate should use vm-df's host_vm_disk_drive_avail_bytes or vm_effective_avail_bytes instead.

Docker Desktop here runs cgroup v1, so /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max does not exist in containers. The cap is in /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.limit_in_bytes (plus memory.memsw.limit_in_bytes; page-cache usage in memory.stat). pc/pagecache_limit.sh --inner, which plans to record /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max, must handle both v1 and v2. membw already does.

tools/probe/probe.cpp did not exist yet, so build-tools has not yet compiled llama-common/llama on the bind mount or run the `pigemma-probe --help | head -3` step. Re-run `bash pc/docker_run.sh build-tools` once the probe lands; the first such build compiles the llama.cpp libraries and will take minutes. I did not prebuild them, so that a 12-way compile would not distort a concurrent native benchmark by another agent.

Deviation from the spec: -t requires stdin AND stdout to be terminals; the spec tests stdin only. On mintty a -t refusal is retried once without -t. Override with --tty, --no-tty or PIGEMMA_DOCKER_TTY.

Deviation from the spec: vm-df uses the local pi-gemma4-build image (alpine:latest as fallback) instead of always pulling alpine. It is the same overlay filesystem, and both report the same numbers. vm_root_avail (933 GB) is room inside the sparse virtual disk, not real free space; --bytes therefore prints min(VM root avail, host drive avail).

Additions not in the manifest: --init, the python->python3 shim, PIGEMMA_* forwarding with PIGEMMA_LOCK_FILE translation, --pi-emu (with the pigemma-arm64-llama volume and PIGEMMA_LLAMA_BIN), --dry-run, --docker-arg, --env, --workdir, --platform, --image, --no-stdin, --as-root (native Linux runs as uid:gid), and the build-image subcommand.

build-tools safeguards that are stricter than the spec: it refuses (exit 4) while results/.bench.lock is held by someone else (--ignore-lock overrides) and serialises concurrent runs with flock on tools/build-linux-x86/.pigemma-build.lock. With default arguments it builds only the targets whose source exists (it warns about the others); --require-all or PIGEMMA_REQUIRE_ALL_TOOLS=1 restores the strict spec target list.
Callers in `while read` loops must pass --no-stdin: -i is the spec default, and docker would otherwise consume the loop's input.
PowerShell callers (pc/h2_run.ps1) must invoke Git Bash explicitly. A bare `bash` can resolve to WSL's System32 bash.exe, as observed with Windows Python subprocess.
The file is not marked executable; git on Windows tracks it as 100644. Call it as `bash pc/docker_run.sh`. the operator may want `git update-index --chmod=+x pc/docker_run.sh` when committing.

tests/test_pi_scripts.py belongs to the tests agent and should include pc/docker_run.sh in its bash -n sweep. It could also assert --dry-run output, which needs no docker: e.g. `bash pc/docker_run.sh --dry-run --memory 6g -- true` contains '--memory=6g --memory-swap=6g' and '-v <repo>:/work -w /work'; bad usage exits 2.

Note for other agents testing through the Claude Bash tool: the tool's transport halves backslashes (\\ arrives as \). Write files containing backslashes with the Write tool or from Python. This caused false failures during my own escaping tests; the script itself is correct.

I wrote the test infrastructure: tests/conftest.py (hooks and fixtures), tests/synth.py (synthetic traces, tiny GGUFs, activation dumps, facts loaders) and tests/test_synth.py (82 tests of the fixtures themselves). I also added 20 fixture files under tests/fixtures, with README.md giving the provenance of each one.

**Real output in the fixtures.** I captured the real llama.cpp b11398 binaries (Windows native, run under `pigemma.paths lock --hold`) on a tiny runnable llama-architecture model that synth.py builds. These give llama_bench_sample.json (8 rows), completion_stderr_sample.txt and completion_stderr_norepack_sample.txt, and perplexity_kld_sample.txt and perplexity_base_sample.txt. The real Gemma 4 outputs were copied from results/: completion_stderr_gemma26b_sample.txt, server_timings_sample.json (draft_n 321, accepted 91), server_timings_nodraft_sample.json, thinking_sample.txt and thinking_pi31b_he_sample.txt. membw_sample.json and fio_sample.json are real runs in the Docker build image, and the fio job file is checked in as fio_sample.fio. Every number in these samples comes from a tiny model or the desktop and is not a project measurement. Text fixtures are stored with LF line endings.

**Facts fixtures.** There are seven, in the data_formats facts.json shape, each with a `notes` field saying which values are quoted from FACTS.md or results/pi-real and which are illustrative. Five are the manifest's list. Two are extra: pi5-16gb-microsd-real (the real board behind context-friend-1 since 2026-10-05) and pi5-8gb-nvme-busy. Each produces the scenario it is named for in pigemma.feasibility:

entries.summary:
pigemma/cache_sim.py is the expert-cache simulator for H1, written to the manifest spec and data_formats 'sim.json'.

What it does:
- Replays a .moetrace (item = slot j*E + e, the same ids as trace.access_items) under six policies: lru (OrderedDict), lfu (exponential decay per token, ties evicted oldest-first), static (train-split top-N, never replaced), belady (MIN with bypass, from precomputed next-use indices), lru_prefetch (cross-layer predictor from trace.cross_layer_table), and lru_perlayer.
- Cache size per item is the exact unit bytes from map.json. The read cost of a miss is rounded up to --read-granularity per slab; an 'aligned' mode uses the real file offsets.
- Reports steady, overall and test (common out-of-sample) blocks, cold_bytes, per_layer_hit_rate, and projections per catalog device profile. Every input carries {value, unit, source} labelled measured, assumed or simulated.
- Writes sim.json, sim.csv (exact header), an optional per-token .npz, and one E4 'projected' envelope per (profile, policy) plus one dense-line envelope per profile. Envelope names are deterministic, so a re-run overwrites them. All envelopes pass results.check_result, and `results summarize` renders them.
- An `io-point` subcommand compares a probe --io-csv run with sim.json and merges points into validation.json, so pc/pagecache_limit.sh step 3 needs no comparison code of its own.
- Self-check: every LRU run is compared against trace's stack-distance curve. It matched exactly (max |diff| 0.0) on the golden real trace and on a 16k-token synthetic trace.

Self-test results (no inference was run):
- tests/test_cache_sim.py: 45 passed in about 5 s.
- Full repo `pytest`: green in 1m29s. The 5 skips belong to other modules.
- test_trace's cache_sim cross-check now runs instead of skipping, and passes.

Measured run time and memory:
- 3.84M accesses (16k tokens x 30 x 8): lru 1.1 s, lfu 3.8 s, belady 3.6 s, lru_prefetch 2.9 s, lru_perlayer 0.6 s, static 0.04 s.
- Full default CLI with 6 policies x (9 budgets + 5 profiles) = 84 runs: 3 min 22 s, under E4's 10 min.

Smoke check on real data (golden 72-token trace + results/map26.json):
- Profile budgets: pi5-8gb = 5,166,852,232 B (1544 items); pi5-16gb = 12,966,852,232 B, so FITS_RAM.
- Dense 31B line: 17.64 GB/token, 0.369 tok/s in RAM and 20.7 s/token streamed (both PROJECTED).
- These are toy numbers from 72 tokens, not E4 results.
entries.interface_notes:
MODULE pigemma.cache_sim
Imports: numpy, pigemma.{paths, trace, gguf_map, results, feasibility}. Run with `python -m pigemma.cache_sim`.

CLI (simulate; the leading word `simulate` is optional)
`python -m pigemma.cache_sim <trace> --map map.json --out sim.json` with options:
- --catalog P (default pigemma/data/catalog.json)
- --policies lru,lfu,static,belady,lru_prefetch[,lru_perlayer] (default: the first 5)
- --budgets-gb 0.5,1,... and/or --profiles all|pi5|desktop|name[,name]. If neither is given, both defaults apply: the 9 budgets and every catalog device.
- --train-split 0.3, --warmup-tokens 256, --read-granularity 131072, --read-model round|aligned, --lfu-decay 0.999, --prefetch-n K
- --token-range A:B (Python slice)
- --io-mem auto|none|PATH (merged through feasibility.load_catalog)
- --calibration auto|none|PATH, --llama-efficiency X, --e0-dir DIR (default results/e0)
- --no-bypass, --no-stack-check
- --dense-model 31b-q4, --dense-map P
- --csv P, --series P.npz
- --results-dir DIR (default: the directory of --out) | --no-envelopes
- --log-level L

Output: stdout gets a run table; stderr gets one INFO line per (policy, budget/profile).
Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 error (bad or incompatible trace/map, malformed catalog, or the LRU vs stack-distance self-check failed; sim.json is still written); 2 usage (unknown policy or profile, out-of-range option); 3 missing input file.

CLI (io-point)
`python -m pigemma.cache_sim io-point --io-csv io.csv --sim sim.json --mem-cap-bytes N` with options:
- [--pinned] [--pin-budget-bytes N] [--pin-locked-bytes N] [--anon-rss-bytes N] [--file-cache-bytes N]
- [--tier-mbps X] [--ram-tok-s X] [--access-ms 0] [--warmup-tokens 200] [--page-size 4096]
- [--volume pigemma-models|bind-mount] [--oom] [--sim-budget-bytes N] [--gguf P] [--token-range A:B] [--note T]...
- [--validation results/h1/validation.json]

It prints the point JSON to stdout. With --validation it merges the point, replacing any point with the same (mem_cap_bytes, pinned). Exit codes: 0; 1 for a bad io.csv; 3 for a missing file.

Python API
- `simulate(trace, map, policy, budget_bytes, *, warmup_tokens, read_granularity, read_model, train_split, lfu_decay, token_range, prefetch_table, prefetch_n, static_items, belady_bypass, profile, keep_series) -> SimResult`
  - trace: a path, TraceReader or PreparedTrace.
  - map: a path, GgufMap, dict or MapInfo. A minimal dict {n_expert, n_expert_used, summary{expert_unit_bytes, n_moe_layers[, nonexpert_bytes...]}} is accepted.
  - SimResult has attributes and dict-style access: res["overall"]["hit_rate"]. .to_dict() returns the runs[] entry and .series holds the per-token arrays.
- `project(sim_result, profile, map, calibration=None, *, catalog=None, budget_info=None) -> dict`
  - calibration: None (0.65 assumed), a float, (value, source) or {value, source}.
- `profile_budget(profile, map) -> {expert_cache_bytes, budget_bytes, infeasible, fits_all_experts, ram_bytes, os_reserve_bytes, nonexpert_bytes, kv_bytes (q8_0 via gguf_map.kv_bytes_for), compute_buffers_bytes, n_ctx, expert_bytes, sources}`
- `classify(tg_serial, tg_overlap, expert_cache_bytes, expert_bytes, *, good=2.0, viable=1.0, weak=0.5)`
- `run_simulation(...) -> (doc, runs, prep)` and `write_outputs(...)`
- `prepare(trace, token_range) -> PreparedTrace`, `map_info(m) -> MapInfo`
- `dense_line`, `efficiency_for_profile`, `efficiency_from_e0`, `select_profiles`, `static_selection`, `predict_next_layer`, `sim_csv_text`
- `read_io_csv`, `measure_io`, `validation_point`, `write_validation`
- Constants: POLICIES, VERDICTS (FITS_RAM, STREAM_GOOD, STREAM_WEAK, NOT_VIABLE, INFEASIBLE), SIM_CSV_HEADER, IO_CSV_HEADER
- Exception: CacheSimError(ValueError)

sim.json
The data_formats keys exactly, plus extras that readers may ignore:
- Top level: format_version, generator, created_at, kind:'simulated', n_tokens, model{id, file, sha_prefix, bytes}, shape, bytes{unit_bytes, read_cost_bytes_mean, read_inflation, ...}, llama_efficiency per profile, checks.lru_vs_stack_distance{ok, max_abs_diff, points}, summary.comparisons[] (belady_gap, static_over_lru, decision flags), notes, envelopes.
- runs[] extras: test{}, steady_window/test_window (absolute record indices), in_sample, capacity_items_exact, unique_items_touched, budget{}, params, info, notes.
- steady/overall/test blocks also carry stall_bytes_per_token, hit_bytes_per_token, io_bytes_per_token (demand + prefetch), prefetch_items_per_token, wasted_prefetch_bytes_per_token, and per-layer prefetch lists.
- projection extras: t_io_demand_s, t_io_prefetch_s, overlapped_s, expert_cache_bytes, window, thresholds, notes. Each assumption is {value, unit, source}.
- dense_31b_line: {model, bytes_per_token, tok_s_at_mem_bw, s_per_token_at_storage_bw, reference_profile, kind:'projected', per_profile{...}}.

Consumers
- feasibility --sim reads the 'lru' runs' steady.hit_rate and capacity_items. Verified end to end by a test.
- For E4, write sim.json into results/h1/ so `python -m pigemma.results summarize results/h1` picks up the E4 envelopes (it skips sim.json itself as a non-envelope).
- E4 envelope fields: kind 'projected'; variant '<policy>@<profile>'; tg.tok_s = tg_serial; read_bytes_per_token = demand + prefetch bytes; tg_overlap and the verdict are in extra. The host block is the machine that ran the simulation, not the device; the device profile is named in variant and extra.
