- `python -m pigemma.cache_sim <trace> --policies lru,belady --budgets-gb <cap - anon - nonexpert - 0.1 GB> --token-range A:B --warmup-tokens 200 --read-granularity <read_ahead_kb*1024> --no-envelopes --out sim_e5_<cap>g.json` (sim_e6_ for pinned runs).
- `python -m pigemma.cache_sim io-point ... --validation <out>` merges the point.
- The point gets extras, and E5/E6 results envelopes are written (replay measured, gen measured, predicted projected).

At the end it prints a summary table and mechanical previews of the E5/E6 pre-registered thresholds (also stored as validation.json checks_preview), plus reference/driver blocks. Every gate decision is logged as 'GATE:' on stderr and to results/h1/raw/pagecache_limit-<UTC>.log.
entries.interface_notes:
CLI (host): bash pc/pagecache_limit.sh [options]

Manifest options:
- --mem 3,4,5,6,8: caps in GB, GB = 1e9 B; passed to docker as --memory <bytes>b.
- --tokens traces/26b/all.moetrace: TRACE.tokens.bin is replayed, TRACE is simulated; a .tokens.bin path is also accepted.
- --range 0:1500: Python slice.
- --pin
- --skip-copy: the volume must already hold a verified copy, else exit 3.
- --allow-bind-mount
- --out results/h1/validation.json: default results/h1/validation_pin.json with --pin.

Extra options:
- Inputs: --model 26b-q4|PATH, --map results/map26.json, --stats <trace stem>.stats.json, --completion-prompt F.
- Run: --threads 6, --cpus 6, --ctx 2048 (minimum; raised to fit the longest chunk piece), --warmup-tokens 200, --completion-tokens 64 (0 = skip).
- Reference run: --ref-mem 20 (0 = none), --ram-tok-s X, --redo-ref.
- fio: --fio-runtime 15 (0 = skip), --fio-bs 3345k.
- Pinning: --pin-anon-gb 0.6, --pin-slack-gb 0.3, --pin-timeout 900.
- Simulator: --sim-slack-gb 0.1, --read-granularity N, --sim-on-replay.
- Timing: --probe-timeout S (partial io.csv kept and counted as a valid partial point).
- E6 comparison: --compare FILE (repeatable; results/h1/validation.json is added automatically when --out differs).
- Locations: --trace-dir traces/h1, --volume pigemma-models.
- Gates: --min-vm-free-gb 16, --min-host-free-gb 18, --min-free-gb 20 (bench-lock RAM gate).
- Behaviour: --no-lock, --keep-going, --no-envelopes, --dry-run (prints every gate and the exact docker and python command lines; no containers, no writes), -h/--help, --version.
- --opt=value also works.
- All user paths must lie inside the repo (the container only sees /work); otherwise exit 2.

Exit codes:
- 0: all requested runs completed. PASS/FAIL of the thresholds is a result, not an error.
- 1: a run failed or OOM (stops the remaining caps unless --keep-going), or another error.
- 2: usage.
- 3: missing input: trace, tokens, map, stats, model, binary, or --skip-copy without a copy.
- 4: refused: disk gate, bench lock busy or low RAM, docker unavailable. stderr line 'pagecache_limit: REFUSED: ...'.

Inner CLI (internal, Linux only): bash /work/pc/pagecache_limit.sh --inner [--task run|preflight|copy]
- run: --gguf --tokens-bin --range A:B --out-dir --trace-dir --tag --threads --ctx --replay-chunks --chunk-tokens --mem-cap-bytes --volume-kind --fio-runtime --fio-bs --completion-tokens --completion-prompt --completion-ctx --probe-timeout --pin-ranges --pin-timeout --bpt-worst-bytes --sample-interval.
- copy: --src --dst --expect-bytes.
- preflight: prints key=value lines (page_size, mem_total_kb, cgroup_version, have_vmtouch/fio, probe_ok/pinner_ok/completion_ok, gguf_present, gguf_size, gguf_sha256_16m, read_ahead_kb, fstype).
- run exits 0 once its run record is written (the record holds the probe outcome), 130 if interrupted.

Test hooks (container paths, forwarded by docker_run as PIGEMMA_*):
- PIGEMMA_PAGECACHE_PROBE, PIGEMMA_PAGECACHE_PINNER, PIGEMMA_PAGECACHE_COMPLETION replace the three binaries.
- PIGEMMA_PAGECACHE_VOLUME replaces the volume name.
- Default binaries: /work/tools/build-linux-x86/bin/{pigemma-probe,pinner} and /work/third_party/llama.cpp/build-linux-x86/bin/llama-completion.

Outputs (the directory of --out, default results/h1/):
- validation[_pin].json: written by cache_sim io-point; point keys exactly per data_formats.
  - Extra point keys: run_record, io_csv, sim_json, natural_gen_tok_s, routing_agreement, pinner_resident_before_bytes, pinner_resident_after_bytes, repack_detected; failed:true for points without rows.
  - Extra top-level keys: checks_preview {E5: {simulator_bytes{points,pass|null}, time_model{points,n_pass,pass}, oom_points}, E6: {points[{tok_s_ratio_pinned_over_unpinned, bytes_per_token_reduction, pin_locked_over_budget, pass}], pass_at_5gb}}, reference {ram_tok_s, source, run_record}, driver {script, version, argv, updated_at}.
- io_<cap>[_pin].csv: the probe io.csv copied.
- pagecache_<tag>.json: the run record, {record:'pigemma.pagecache_run', tag, volume, gguf, gguf_size, token_range, threads, ctx, mem_cap_bytes_requested, page_size, pinned, host (container paths.host_fingerprint), cgroup{version, memory_limit_bytes, before/after_probe/after{anon,file,file_mapped,usage,peak,oom_kill,io_rbytes}, oom_kill_probe_delta, io_rbytes_probe_delta}, device{dev,read_ahead_kb,logical_block_size,fstype,source}, fio{ok,direct,bs,bs_bytes,mbps,iops,lat_mean_ms,clat_p50_ms,clat_p99_ms,...}, evict{tool,resident_before,resident_after}, pinner{start,start_rc,verify_after,stop_rc,ranges_file}, probe{argv,exit_code,wall_s,timed_out,summary,io_csv_info,skipped}, completion{argv,exit_code,wall_s}, mem_samples{<phase>:{n,max_anon,max_file,max_file_mapped,max_usage,last}}, outputs{...}, notes[], interrupted, host_analysis{io, anon_rss_bytes, file_cache_bytes, oom, tier_mbps, read_granularity, sim_budget_bytes, completion (pigemma.bench.parse_completion_stderr), repack_detected, routing_agreement{set_agreement, mean_overlap, n_tokens}, notes}}. It has no 'experiment' key, so results.summarize skips it.
- sim_e5_<cap>g.json / sim_e6_<cap>g.json: cache_sim, lru+belady at the matching budget.
- hotset_<cap>.json + hotset_<cap>.ranges.txt: --pin, generated on the host with --page-size = container page size.
- Envelopes:
  - E5_pagecache_cap<cap>g_{replay,gen,predicted}.json for unpinned runs.
  - E6_pagecache_cap<cap>g_pin_{replay,gen,predicted}.json for pinned runs.
  - E5_pagecache_ref<G>g_{replay,gen}.json for the reference run.
  - Variants: replay-ub1@cap5g[+pin], gen64@cap5g[+pin], predicted@cap5g[+pin].
- raw/*.log: gitignored; probe, completion, fio, pinner, memory samples, inner and host logs.
- raw/replay_chunks.json: the trace header chunks for --replay-chunks.
- traces/h1/replay_<tag>.moetrace (+ .tokens.bin): the replayed routing (gitignored).
entries.self_test:
All tests ran on this desktop (Git Bash + Docker Desktop) on 2026-10-05.

1. Lint and CLI:
   - `bash -n pc/pagecache_limit.sh`: OK. The file is LF-only ASCII.
   - --help and --version return 0. Unknown option, bad --mem and an out-of-repo --out return 2. --inner on Windows returns 2.

2. Dry runs:
   - `--dry-run --mem 5` and `--dry-run --mem 5,6 --pin --skip-copy ...` print every GATE line and the exact docker command lines (via docker_run --dry-run), plus the gguf_map hotset, cache_sim and io-point commands.
   - The pin budget is 4.1e9 B at a 5 GB cap, matching EXPERIMENT_PLAN. Exit 0, nothing written.

3. End-to-end stub runs (real Docker, cgroup caps, fio, vmtouch, the real pinner, and the real cache_sim / gguf_map / results / bench parsers):
   - Setup: a tiny gemma4-shaped GGUF from tests/synth (4 layers, 16 experts, top-8), a 600-token synthetic trace, its map and stats, and stub probe/llama-completion scripts passed through the PIGEMMA_PAGECACHE_* hooks.
   - E5: copy into a fresh volume (verified by size + SHA-256), reference run at a 2 GB cap (ram_tok_s), caps 0.5 and 1 GB. The cgroup v1 limit was seen as 499,998,720 B; read_ahead_kb 128 on /dev/sdc ext4; fio O_DIRECT ran. 2 points were merged and the summary table printed. Exit 0.
   - E6: --pin --skip-copy reused the reference. The real pinner locked 311,296/311,296 B and stopped with rc 0 after SIGTERM to its pidfile; resident before and after were recorded. The E6 comparison against the --compare file worked. Exit 0.
   - All 11 envelopes passed `python -m pigemma.results validate --strict`, and `python -m pigemma.results summarize` renders E5/E6.

4. Failure paths:
   - Real OOM: the stub allocated 3 GB under a 0.5 GB cap. The cgroup oom_kill delta was +1 and the probe exited 137; the point was marked oom; the next cap was skipped; exit 1.
   - Probe failure without rows plus --keep-going: two points recorded with failed:true; exit 1.
   - --skip-copy on a missing volume: exit 3, and the volume was not created.
   - Disk gate forced to fail (--min-host-free-gb 999999): GATE line plus 'docker builder prune would reclaim ~20.88GB', REFUSED, exit 4. With --allow-bind-mount the run used the bind mount, majflt x page bytes and the bind-mount note; exit 0.
   - --probe-timeout 4: partial io.csv kept and the point recorded; exit 0.
   - docker stop of my own test container mid-probe: the inner trap stopped the probe (143) and wrote a record with interrupted:true; container exit 130; the host recorded the point and stopped.
   - Bench lock: re-exec under `pigemma.paths lock --hold` worked (Windows python launching Git Bash; the child logged 'held by this run's parent'). With a busy lock: 'pigemma.paths: REFUSED: another model-loading job is running', exit 4. Isolated lock files were used.

5. Repo tests:
   - `pytest tests/test_pi_scripts.py::test_bash_syntax` (covers pc/*.sh): 11 passed.
   - The LF and EXPERIMENT_PLAN command-flag / relative-link tests passed; pagecache_limit.sh's flags (--mem --tokens --range --pin --skip-copy --out --inner) were checked against the script text.
   - tests/test_cache_sim.py passed.

6. llama-completion: in Docker, `llama-completion --help` confirms -nr, -no-cnv, --no-display-prompt and -lv are accepted at this build.

7. Not run with the real 26B (no inference, per the rules): the probe binary is not built, the E3 trace does not exist yet, and the 14.4 GB volume copy was not made.

All test artifacts were removed: the .tmp-pagecache-selftest directory, the Docker volumes pigemma-models-selftest and pigemma-models-selftest2 (both created by me), and the empty traces/h1. No pigemma-pagecache-* containers are left.
open_issues: Not yet run on the real 26B: pigemma-probe is not built in tools/build-linux-x86/bin (run `bash pc/docker_run.sh build-tools`), traces/26b/all.moetrace and all.stats.json (E3) do not exist yet, and the one-time 14.4 GB copy into the pigemma-models volume has not been made. E5/E6 integration belongs to the experiment phase.

Runtime: the manifest's '~5 min per cap' is likely optimistic. fio in the Docker VM measured ~275 MB/s for 3 MB O_DIRECT random reads (one 1 s sample on the overlay disk). At small caps the worst case of 803 MB/token can mean seconds per token, so 1500 tokens per cap may take very long. The inner side logs a worst-case ETA after fio; use --probe-timeout or a smaller --range if needed.

D2: the gate checks the drive that actually holds docker_data.vhdx, which is F: on this desktop (796 GB free), not C: as the manifest says. C: is used only when the vhdx location is unknown. The gate applies only when a copy is needed.

D1: GB = 1e9 B. Docker's '5g' would be 5 GiB, so caps are passed as --memory <M*1e9>b. The kernel rounds the cgroup limit down to a page (5e9 -> 4,999,999,488). A difference over 1 MiB becomes a note.

Docker Desktop runs cgroup v1 here. OOM comes from memory.oom_control 'oom_kill' (verified with a real OOM). anon/file/file_mapped are mapped from total_rss/total_cache/total_mapped_file. There are no blkio/io.stat counters, so io_rbytes_per_token stays null. v2 hosts use memory.max/memory.stat/memory.events/io.stat.
D3: the order is fio (O_DIRECT, does not populate the cache) BEFORE vmtouch -e. That is equivalent to the manifest's order, and safer if fio falls back to buffered I/O on a bind mount.

D4: the replay uses --replay-chunks (built from the trace header) and --chunk-tokens B-A, so the KV cache resets exactly at the source chunk starts; -c = max(2048, longest piece + 8, rounded up to 256). Routing can still differ slightly from the source trace (-ub 1 replay vs -ub 256 collection), so each point records routing_agreement, and --sim-on-replay simulates the replayed sequence. The replay trace is saved to traces/h1/replay_<tag>.moetrace instead of /tmp/replay.moetrace.

Deviation from EXPERIMENT_PLAN's literal commands: pinned runs write sim_e6_<cap>g.json, computed with the pinned run's own measured anon RSS, instead of reusing sim_e5_<cap>g.json. With --pin and no --out the default is results/h1/validation_pin.json (plan convention) rather than the manifest's generic validation.json. E6's 'Writes' row in the plan could list sim_e6_*.json.

The script writes E5/E6 results envelopes itself (replay measured, gen measured, predicted projected), so the plan's fallback of copying numbers by hand is not needed. Measured envelopes carry the container's host fingerprint (in_container true, cgroup_mem_max = cap). The projected envelope uses the Windows host, following the E4 convention of 'the host that computed it'.

The E0 repack gate is not checked automatically. Instead, every run's llama-completion -lv 4 buffer split is scanned for CPU_REPACK (repack_detected, plus a loud note). An OOM stops the remaining caps unless --keep-going.
fio bs=3345k (from the manifest) is 3,425,280 B, because fio's k is 1024. That is 2.4% larger than one 26B expert unit (3,345,408 B = 3267k). It is kept as specified and can be changed with --fio-bs.

The time-model ram_tok_s comes from a reference run at a 20 GB cap, which assumes the whole GGUF fits in VM page cache (VM MemTotal 32.6 GB). It is reused when results/h1/pagecache_ref20.json matches the GGUF, range, threads and volume. If the reference still reads > 1 MB/token after the warm-up, a warning says ram_tok_s is an underestimate.

Only tested from Git Bash on Windows. On a native Linux host docker_run runs containers as the caller's uid (the copy uses --as-root), and mlock limits inside the container may then differ; untested there.
Timestamps: the inner log lines use UTC with a 'Z' (the container clock); the host log lines use local time.

entries.summary:
pi/00_feasibility.sh is written and tested. It is step 0 on any Pi and is read-only.

**What it does**
- Sources pi/lib/common.sh and runs pigemma_init.
- Collects facts with write_facts, or takes an existing file via `--facts F`.
- Runs `python3 -m pigemma.feasibility --facts ... --catalog ... --json ... [--want] [--sim] [--io-mem] [--calibration] [--device]` through run_feasibility.
- Prints one report and exits with the verdict code (0/2/3/4, 1 on error).

**Why it does not call assert_safe_host**
That function exits before anything is printed. Instead, pi/00 runs protected_host_reasons itself, prints a loud banner and still shows the verdict table. The banner says every other pi/*.sh script refuses on this host (exit 4) and that PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1 is the only override. With the override set, a second banner lists the safety rules. A third banner appears for a busy host.

**Report sections (stdout)**
1. Header line: READ-ONLY, plus an EMULATED label when that applies.
2. `==== host facts`:
   - RAM total and available, including the cgroup cap
   - storage type, device, link speed (e.g. `8.0 GT/s PCIe x1 = Gen3`), read_ahead_kb, rotational
   - model dir, whether it sits on `/`, and free disk
   - page size, kernel, governor, temperature, throttled state
   - CPU flags in the 'asimddp: yes, i8mm: no' style
   - HAT and pciex1_gen, memlock, tool versions
   - running services with the protected matches
   - container, emulated and fake-root flags, and the protected-host flag
3. The banner, when there is one.
4. `==== verdict table`: pigemma.feasibility's own table, with projected tok/s and its source.
5. `==== summary`:
   - verdict and recommended model, quant and flags
   - the flags as they will actually be used on this host, after common.sh's mlock policy (mlock is removed on a protected host with the override)
   - download URL and the optional draft
   - a disk check using pi/04's require_free_disk rule. On context-friend-1 it says the 26B Q4_0 does not fit the microSD and names UD-Q3_K_M instead, which matches FACTS.
   - device profile, the projection inputs with their measured/assumed kind, next steps, and the fixed hardware recommendation line
   - output paths

**Self-test**
- Every fixture gives the expected exit code: 4 GB → 4 (3 with PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1); 16 GB → 0; context-friend-1 → 4 (0 with override); container → 2; busy facts → 4.
- Runs in Docker: the x86 build image (exit 0, storage unknown) and the arm64 pi-emu image with `--memory 8g` (exit 2).
- New test file passes: 24 passed, 1 skipped (shellcheck not installed), including the Docker integration test.
entries.interface_notes:
CLI: `bash pi/00_feasibility.sh [--want 26b|31b|<model-id>] [--json OUT|-] [--sim FILE] [--facts FILE] [--facts-out FILE] [--catalog FILE] [--io-mem auto|none|PATH] [--calibration auto|none|PATH] [--device NAME] [--report FILE|none] [-q|--quiet] [-h|--help] [--version] [-- extra pigemma.feasibility args]`. The `--opt=value` form also works.

Defaults:
- `--json`: $PIGEMMA_OUT/feasibility.json (default pi/out/feasibility.json).
- `--facts-out`: $PIGEMMA_OUT/facts.json.
- `--report`: $PIGEMMA_OUT/feasibility.txt, a byte-identical copy of stdout.
- `--catalog`: $PIGEMMA_CATALOG.
- `--io-mem` and `--calibration`: not passed, so pigemma.feasibility's `auto` applies (results/pi/io_mem.json and calibration.json are picked up when present).
- Relative paths are resolved against the caller's cwd.

Option behaviour:
- `--facts F` skips fact collection. facts.json is not written, and the protected/busy state comes from the verdict JSON rather than from this machine.
- `--json -` puts the verdict JSON on stdout and the report on stderr.
- `-q` sets PIGEMMA_QUIET=1: no config dump and no info logs. The report is still printed.

Exit codes:
- 0: FITS_* or STREAM_OK available.
- 2: only slow operation possible.
- 3: nothing viable, or no Python >= 3.10 (the facts JSON is printed first).
- 4: refused, because the host is protected without PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1, or busy. Also 4 when the bash gate refuses but pigemma.feasibility did not; the summary then shows 'raised to exit 4'.
- 1: usage error, missing input file, or pigemma.feasibility error (e.g. an unknown `--want`).

Files written: only facts.json, feasibility.json and feasibility.txt (or the given paths), plus a scratch dir $PIGEMMA_OUT/.pg00.<pid> that is removed at exit. feasibility.json is moved into place only when a verdict exists (exit 0/2/3/4). If the run fails, an older file is kept and a warning says it is not from this run.

Stable report anchors that tests and docs can grep:
- First line: `pi-gemma4 feasibility report - pi/00_feasibility.sh <ver> - <UTC> - READ-ONLY ...`.
- Section headers: `==== host facts (read-only) ====`, `==== verdict table: ...`, `==== summary ====`.
- Banners: `PROTECTED HOST '<host>'`, `EVERY OTHER pi/*.sh SCRIPT REFUSES ON THIS HOST (exit 4)`, `OVERRIDE ACTIVE (PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1)`, `BUSY HOST '<host>'`.
- Summary labels, 2-space indent and 15-character label column: verdict (`exit N = OK|SLOW ONLY|NOT VIABLE|REFUSED|ERROR ...`), recommended, llama flags, on this host, download, draft, disk (pi/04) (`OK:` / `NOT ENOUGH:` / `already in the model dir`, with `-> pi/04_fetch_model.sh --model <family> --quant <quant>`), device profile, projections, inputs, next, hardware (= feasibility.json recommendation_line), outputs.

Environment read: everything in pi_config.env (THREADS, CTX, OS_RESERVE_GIB, MODEL_DIR, DENY_HOSTS, PROTECTED_SERVICE_GLOBS, ALLOW_MLOCK, MIN_FREE_DISK_FACTOR, KEEP_FREE_GB, NICE_LEVEL, PIGEMMA_I_KNOW, PIGEMMA_OUT), plus PIGEMMA_EMULATED, PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC, PIGEMMA_PYTHON, PIGEMMA_CATALOG and PIGEMMA_MAX_LOADAVG (via feasibility).

Test helpers in tests/test_pi_00_feasibility.py (module level): `_env(tmp_path, fake=None, **extra)`, which strips PIGEMMA_*/config vars and sets PIGEMMA_OUT and MODEL_DIR into tmp; `run00(bash, env, *args)`; `HERMETIC = ('--io-mem','none','--calibration','none')`.
entries.self_test:
Commands run from the repo root (Git Bash and Windows Python 3.14):
1. `bash -n pi/00_feasibility.sh`: OK. File is LF-only and pure ASCII with no control characters.
2. Fixture runs, with PIGEMMA_OUT=/tmp/..., MODEL_DIR=/srv/x and `--io-mem none --calibration none`:
   - pi_proc_4gb: exit 4, with the PROTECTED banner and the full table.
   - pi_proc_4gb with PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1: exit 3, all 26b rows NOT_VIABLE, the OVERRIDE banner shown.
   - pi_proc_16gb: exit 0. 26b-q4 is FITS_MAPPED with fits_repacked false; flags are `-nr -lm mmap+mlock ...` and mlock is allowed; the link reads `8.0 GT/s PCIe x1 = Gen3`.
   - pi_proc_cf1_16gb with PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1: exit 0. The flags shown for this host are `-nr -lm mmap ...`, with mlock removed. The disk line reads 'NOT ENOUGH: 26b-q4 needs ... 16.44 GB free on /; free 15.50 GB' and names `--model 26b --quant UD-Q3_K_M`.
   - pi_proc_cf1_16gb without the override: exit 4.
   - pi_proc_container: exit 2. Storage is unknown, with a 'services could not be listed' warning.
   - `--facts tests/fixtures/facts_pi5-8gb-nvme-busy.json`: exit 4, with the BUSY banner.
   - `--want 31b --json -`: stdout is valid JSON, exit 2, all rows NEVER_GOOD_SPEED.
   - Usage errors (`--bogus`, `--want` with no value, missing `--sim` file): exit 1. `--help` and `--version`: exit 0. Piping into `| head -2` keeps exit 0 and the report copy is still written.
3. Docker:
   - `bash pc/docker_run.sh --no-tty --no-stdin --env PIGEMMA_OUT=/tmp/pg00 -- bash pi/00_feasibility.sh --io-mem none --calibration none`: exit 0 in 3.5 s. x86 Ubuntu 24.04 image, 9p bind mount, storage unknown, 'x86 host: not a Pi CPU' hint.
   - `bash pc/docker_run.sh --pi-emu --memory 8g ...`: exit 2 in 12.9 s. EMULATED label, available RAM capped to 8.57 GB by the cgroup.
4. `python -m pytest tests/test_pi_00_feasibility.py -m "integration or not integration"`: 24 passed, 1 skipped (shellcheck not installed), Docker integration test included.
5. Related suites still pass: `python -m pytest tests/test_pi_scripts.py tests/test_experiment_plan.py tests/test_docs_hypotheses.py tests/test_feasibility.py`. test_pi_scripts' `bash -n` sweep picks up the new script, and the docs' pi/00 flags (`--want`, `--json`) exist in the script text.

No model inference was run, no Pi was contacted, and nothing outside tmp and pi/out was written.
open_issues: The catalog still lists context-friend-1 in protected_hosts. Even though DENY_HOSTS is now empty per FACTS, pi/00 (and every gate) refuses on the real Pi without PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1. FACTS says real-Pi runs use PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1, so this is consistent today. If the catalog owner drops the name, only the contextfriend-* service globs will protect that host.

pigemma.feasibility's draft note, which is printed inside the verdict table, still says 'MTP sidecars loaded but never drafted'. FACTS (later 2026-10-05 update) says MTP works with an explicit `--spec-type draft-mtp`. pi/00's own summary line says 'optional; measure first (-md <file> --spec-type draft-mtp)'. The feasibility.py text should be updated by its owner.

pigemma.feasibility's NO_DISK rule (1.05 x file bytes) ignores KEEP_FREE_GB, so on context-friend-1 it recommends 26b-q4 (14.44 GB, free 15.50 GB). pi/04's require_free_disk rule (max(1.1 x bytes, bytes + 2 GB on /)) will refuse that file. pi/00 keeps exit code = verdict code but prints 'disk (pi/04) NOT ENOUGH' and the best row that fits (26b-ud-q3_k_m). pi/04 should apply the same 'best row that fits the disk' choice when it auto-selects, or feasibility should take keep-free into account.

The catalog has no 'pi5-16gb-microsd-real' device yet (FACTS asks for one). context-friend-1 therefore gets a facts-built profile with an assumed microSD at 85 MB/s sequential instead of the measured 91.6 MB/s, until pi/03's io_mem.json is merged.

Deviation, added for safety: if the bash host gate (common.sh, which also matches a glob against the unit name without '.service') refuses while pigemma.feasibility did not, pi/00 raises the exit code to 4 and says so. This keeps pi/00 from being weaker than the gate every other script applies.

Options and outputs added beyond the manifest: --facts, --facts-out, --catalog, --io-mem, --calibration, --device, --report (plus the extra pi/out/feasibility.txt), -q, --version, `--json -`, and `--` pass-through. The manifest's three flags behave as specified.

The disk-check hint names `pi/04_fetch_model.sh --model <family> --quant <quant>` as specified for pi/04 in the manifest. pi/04 is not written yet; if its CLI differs, update the hint in pi/00's embedded renderer (function disk_lines).

entries.summary:
pi/01_tune_os.sh is finished and tested, along with its own test module tests/test_pi_01_tune_os.py. All 33 unit tests pass (shellcheck is skipped because it is not installed) and the Docker integration test passes.

The script already existed (1569 lines) from an earlier run of this same assignment that never returned. I reviewed it against the manifest spec and FACTS.md, tested it, and kept it with three small fixes:
- **Container banner:** in a container, the plan now says up front that `--apply` will be refused there.
- **Clean second apply:** a second `--apply` with nothing left prints "applying: nothing to do" instead of an empty `== applying ==` header.
- **Backup copy:** the config.txt backup now uses plain `cp` instead of `cp -p`. /boot/firmware is vfat, where preserving owner or mode can fail and would abort the item.

What the script does:
- **Default is a dry run.** For items (a)-(f) it prints the current value, the proposed value, a status (CHANGE, OK, SKIP, NOT SELECTED or ADVICE), notes, and the exact commands, including file contents shown as `sudo -n tee <<'EOF'` blocks.
- **`--apply`** (or `TUNE_APPLY=1`) runs those commands idempotently and prints the before and after values. It uses `sudo -n` per privileged command, or runs directly as root.
- **(a) PCIe Gen3:** appends a marked `[all]` + `dtparam=pciex1_gen=3` block to config.txt, once (grep guard on the marker), after taking a backup. It only proposes this when `TUNE_NVME_GEN3=1`, the board is a Pi 5 or CM5, an NVMe is present, and nothing shows a Hailo or AI HAT. It checks the HAT EEPROM product, lspci, PCI vendor 0x1e60 and /dev/hailo*. If a HAT is found it prints "PCIe lane used by the AI HAT: NVMe impossible without a dual-slot HAT" and skips. Only lines before the first section filter or under [all] / [pi5] count as already set. It prints REBOOT REQUIRED and never reboots.
- **(b) Governor:** sets the governor on every cpufreq policy and installs the oneshot unit pigemma-governor.service to persist it.
- **(c) sysctl:** sets vm.swappiness=10 and vm.vfs_cache_pressure=50 and writes /etc/sysctl.d/90-pigemma.conf.
- **(d) Read-ahead:** sets read_ahead_kb on the whole disk holding MODEL_DIR (found by common.sh's `detect_storage`) and writes a udev rule to persist it.
- **(e) Memlock:** writes the limits.d file (`* soft` and `* hard memlock unlimited`) and the systemd `DefaultLimitMEMLOCK=infinity` file. A re-login is needed.
- **(f) Advice only:** swap/zram, cooling (Active Cooler, throttling from 80 C), the get_throttled value decoded, power, and storage class.

Safety and extras:
- `assert_safe_host` runs before any plan is built (exit 4 on a protected host).
- With `PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1` on a protected host, the script changes live values only (no persistence files unless `--persist`), will not edit config.txt without `--allow-boot-edit`, and skips (e) unless `mlock_allowed`.
- It only writes files that are absent or carry its marker; anything else is left alone with a note.
- `--revert` uses the original live values recorded in `$PIGEMMA_OUT/tune_os.state`.
- `--apply` is refused (exit 3) inside a container, on a non-Linux host, and on a fake root unless a test sysroot is given.
- The script never reboots, never stops or restarts services, never installs packages, and never runs `sysctl --system`, `udevadm trigger` or `daemon-reexec`.
entries.interface_notes:
CLI: bash pi/01_tune_os.sh [--apply] [--no-pcie] [--dry-run|-n] [--revert] [--only LIST] [--skip LIST] [--persist|--runtime-only] [--allow-boot-edit] [-h|--help] [--version]
- LIST is the letters a-f, comma- or space-separated.
- `--dry-run` wins over TUNE_APPLY=1.
- `--help` and `--version` exit 0 before pigemma_init (they create no PIGEMMA_OUT).
- `--version` prints "pi/01_tune_os.sh 1.0.0".

Exit codes:
- 0: plan printed, applied, or nothing to do.
- 1: usage error, bad TUNE_VFS_CACHE_PRESSURE, a config error from pigemma_init, or a failed apply step. Completed items stay applied.
- 3: `--apply` precondition failed: not root and no passwordless `sudo -n`; inside a container; non-Linux; or PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC without PIGEMMA_TUNE_ROOT. Nothing is changed.
- 4: protected host (from assert_safe_host); nothing is printed on stdout.

Config (pi/pi_config.env; the environment wins): TUNE_APPLY, TUNE_NVME_GEN3 (default 0), TUNE_GOVERNOR (default performance; 'keep' or 'none' skips b), TUNE_SWAPPINESS (10), TUNE_READAHEAD_KB (2048), TUNE_MEMLOCK (1), ALLOW_MLOCK, PIGEMMA_I_KNOW, MODEL_DIR (selects the disk for d). The environment-only variable TUNE_VFS_CACHE_PRESSURE defaults to 50.

Test hooks:
- PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC: every read comes from the fixture root.
- PIGEMMA_BOOT_CONFIG=F: the boot config is read and written directly at F.
- PIGEMMA_TUNE_ROOT=DIR: every write lands in DIR/<system path>, live values are read back from there first, and systemctl/udevadm are printed but not run.
- lspci.txt in the fake root is the fake `lspci -nn` output.

Files written by `--apply`:
- the boot config: a block between '# >>> pi-gemma4 tune_os' and '# <<< pi-gemma4 tune_os', plus <file>.pigemma-<UTC timestamp>.bak
- /etc/systemd/system/pigemma-governor.service
- /etc/sysctl.d/90-pigemma.conf
- /etc/udev/rules.d/90-pigemma-readahead.rules
- /etc/security/limits.d/90-pigemma.conf
- /etc/systemd/system.conf.d/pigemma.conf
- $PIGEMMA_OUT/tune_os.state: '<system path><TAB><original value>' per line, removed by `--revert --apply`.

Every /etc file carries the marker 'Managed by pi-gemma4 pi/01_tune_os.sh'.

Output contract (stdout):
- line 1: 'pi-gemma4 OS tuning (pi/01_tune_os.sh 1.0.0) - <tune|revert> - <DRY RUN...|APPLY...>'
- per item: '(x) <title>' followed by '    current : ', '    proposed: ', '    status  : <CHANGE|OK|SKIP|NOT SELECTED|ADVICE>[ - why]', then 'note' lines and commands
- with `--apply`: an '== applying ...' section with before / after / status APPLIED|FAILED
- 'summary : ...'
- 'REBOOT REQUIRED' / 'RE-LOGIN REQUIRED' lines when they apply.

Logs and warnings go to stderr (common.sh `log`/`warn`).
entries.self_test:
Lint and fixtures:
- `bash -n pi/01_tune_os.sh` passes; no CR characters in either file.

Manual runs with PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC:
- **pi_proc_16gb:** dry run exits 0; (a) is OK (already Gen3); b-e are CHANGE with the exact commands; no files are written.
- **pi_proc_4gb (context-friend-1):** exits 4 with no plan printed.
- **pi_proc_4gb with PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1:** (a) is SKIPped with the AI HAT message; runtime-only; (e) is SKIPped because mlock is not allowed.
- **pi_proc_container:** exits 0 with a, b and d skipped and a logged warning.

Grep-guard test (the manifest's fixture test):
- Temp copy of config.txt via PIGEMMA_BOOT_CONFIG, with PIGEMMA_TUNE_ROOT and TUNE_NVME_GEN3=1.
- First `--apply` appends the block once and makes one .bak.
- Second `--apply` leaves config.txt byte-identical, reports "OK - already added ... (grep guard)", and prints "nothing to do".

Round trip:
- Cloned fixture with untuned values (ondemand x2, swappiness 60, vfs_cache_pressure 100, read-ahead 128).
- `--apply` writes the 5 marked files plus the state file.
- `--revert --apply` restores every value, deletes our files, makes config.txt byte-identical to the original, and removes the state file.

Docker:
- `bash pc/docker_run.sh -- bash pi/01_tune_os.sh` in pi-gemma4-build:latest: dry run exit 0, `--apply` exit 3, /etc unchanged.
- Same in the arm64 pi-emu image (`--pi-emu`): exit 0, labelled EMULATED.

Windows host (no fake root): dry run exits 0 with a, b and d skipped; `--apply` exits 3 ("needs Linux").

pytest:
- `python -m pytest tests/test_pi_01_tune_os.py`: 33 passed, 1 skipped (shellcheck not installed), 1 deselected, in about 104 s.
- `-m integration` (Docker dry run touches nothing, `--apply` refused): 1 passed in 4.6 s.
- Also passing: tests/test_experiment_plan.py, plus test_pi_scripts.py::test_bash_syntax and ::test_scripts_have_lf_line_endings.
open_issues: Deviation from the spec: item (c) does not run `sysctl --system`, because it would re-apply every sysctl.d file on a host that runs production services. It writes /proc/sys/vm/<key> directly (what `sysctl -w` does) and still installs the same /etc/sysctl.d/90-pigemma.conf.

Deviations from the spec: (b) runs `systemctl daemon-reload` + `enable` but not `--now`, because the live governor is written to sysfs directly. (d) runs `udevadm control --reload-rules` but not `trigger`. (e) never runs `daemon-reexec`; it prints a note instead.

Added safety on a protected host with PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1 (context-friend-1): runtime-only unless --persist; config.txt is edited only with --allow-boot-edit; (e) runs only when mlock_allowed. --apply is refused (exit 3) inside a container. On context-friend-1 this means the safest real-Pi usage is a dry run, or `PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1 ... --apply --only b,d` for live values only. Whether to touch the live governor or read-ahead on that box at all is the operator's decision.

Extra flags beyond the manifest: --dry-run, --revert, --only, --skip, --persist, --runtime-only, --allow-boot-edit. Extra test hook: PIGEMMA_TUNE_ROOT (test sysroot). TUNE_VFS_CACHE_PRESSURE is read from the environment only, because pi_config.env belongs to another agent and has no entry for it.
tests/test_pi_01_tune_os.py runs the script about 40 times through Git Bash, which takes about 100 s on Windows.

The current catalog.json still lists context-friend-1 under protected_hosts, so assert_safe_host refuses it even when DENY_HOSTS is empty. That matches FACTS.md (the override is PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1), but whoever maintains the catalog should know.

ASSUMED, not measured: that vm.swappiness=10 helps inference. The script states that low swappiness keeps anonymous memory (repacked weights, KV cache) out of swap, but does not keep mmap'ed -nr weights resident, since those are file pages. The Gen3 speeds in the advice are published or catalog values.

entries.summary:
pi/02_build_llama.sh builds llama.cpp natively on the Pi at the pinned commit (and optionally the pigemma tools). It checks RAM and disk before building and refuses to run on a protected host. The file already existed (1601 lines, apparently from an earlier interrupted attempt at this same task). I read all of it and checked it against the manifest spec, common.sh and tools/CMakeLists.txt. Testing found one real bug and one cosmetic problem, both now fixed; with two more small changes the file is 1625 lines.

1. Bug: build lock outlived the script. The progress-line subshell inherited fd 9, which holds the flock on $PIGEMMA_OUT/.build.lock. Its orphaned `sleep 30` kept the lock for up to 30 s after pi/02 exited, so a second pi/02 started right after a build was wrongly refused with exit 4. Fix: the subshell closes fd 9 and, on TERM, kills only its own sleep. It never kills a stale `$!`.
2. Wrong "detected" CPU flags after the fallback. The configure log is appended across attempts, so after the native-to-Pi-5 fallback the native attempt's "ARM detected flags" line was printed again and recorded as `arm_detected_flags`. Now only the current attempt's part of the log is read, and the native detection string is kept inside `fallback_reason`.
3. Small addition: a note when an existing build reports a build number other than b11398 (for example the Pi's ad-hoc build reports "build 1"). Such a build is kept as up to date; `--rebuild` relinks it to b11398 in seconds.
4. Small addition: a `_lines` helper for the per-attempt log reading.

What the script does (details in its header):
- Source: a depth-1 fetch of the full pinned hash, with the manifest's blob:none clone as fallback, or `--from-desktop` (rsync, or tar when rsync is missing). It never overwrites a directory that is not llama.cpp, and refuses a checkout with local changes.
- Configure: the manifest's cmake command. `--arch auto` builds native and falls back once to `-DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH=armv8.2-a+dotprod+fp16` when the native configure fails, when native detection enables i8mm/sve/sme that /proc/cpuinfo does not list, on an arch-flag compile error, or when the binary dies with SIGILL. Under emulation (PIGEMMA_EMULATED=1, or CPU implementer 0x00 = qemu) it goes straight to the Pi 5 flags.
- Build number: passes `-DLLAMA_BUILD_NUMBER=11398` when the shallow checkout is at the pinned commit, so binaries report b11398.
- Build: `nice -n 10`, jobs from `pick_jobs`, logs in $PIGEMMA_OUT/build-logs/, one progress line every 30 s.
- Re-runs: up-to-date llama and tools builds are skipped.
- Optional `--with-tools` build, `--clean-objects`, `--dry-run`.
- Output: binary paths, the version line and `llama-bench --help | head -1` on stdout, plus pi/out/build.json.

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 usage or failed step; 3 precondition (missing tool, disk, RAM, unusable source); 4 refused (protected host, bench lock held, another build running).
entries.interface_notes:
CLI: `pi/02_build_llama.sh [--commit C(7-40 hex, default LLAMA_COMMIT=a7b94df)] [--jobs N] [--with-tools] [--from-desktop user@host:/path | LOCAL_DIR] [--arch auto|native|pi5|generic] [--targets a,b,...] [--repo-url URL] [--tools-build-dir D] [--rebuild] [--clean-objects] [--min-free-gb 3] [--min-mem-gb 1.5] [--ignore-lock] [--configure-only] [--dry-run] [--verbose] [--json-out FILE] | -h/--help | --version`. The `--opt=value` form also works.
- Default targets: llama-cli, llama-completion, llama-bench, llama-perplexity, llama-server.
- `--from-desktop`: `user@host:/path` is rsync over ssh (BatchMode, 20 s connect timeout; PIGEMMA_RSYNC_RSH overrides). A local directory is copied with rsync, or with tar when rsync is missing. Build dirs are excluded and protected from `--delete`. The copied tree's git HEAD must match `--commit`, else exit 3.
- `--arch pi5` on a non-aarch64 host is exit 1.

Exit codes:
- 0: built, up to date, configured (`--configure-only`), or dry run.
- 1: usage error, or a failed git/rsync/configure/build step, or a binary that does not run.
- 3: missing cmake/gcc/g++/make (or ninja)/git (apt hint, never installs); not enough disk (`--min-free-gb`, plus KEEP_FREE_GB on /); not enough MemAvailable; LLAMA_DIR not empty and not llama.cpp; local modifications in the way; abbreviated hash missing from a shallow checkout; desktop tree at another commit.
- 4: protected host without PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1; results/.bench.lock held (checked via pigemma.paths.lock_status; PIGEMMA_LOCK_FILE honoured); another pi/02 holds $PIGEMMA_OUT/.build.lock.

Layout (consumed by later pi scripts):
- llama.cpp source in $LLAMA_DIR (default ~/llama.cpp from pi_config.env), binaries in $LLAMA_DIR/build/bin. This is what common.sh `llama_bin` resolves.
- Tools in $PIGEMMA_HOME/tools/build/bin (common.sh `tools_bin`). With `--tools-build-dir`, a hint to export PIGEMMA_TOOLS_BIN is printed.

stdout:
- `== llama.cpp <commit> in <bin_dir> ==`, one `%-17s path` line per target, `version`, `arch`, `build`.
- `== llama-bench --help | head -1 ==` plus that line.
- With `--with-tools`: `== pigemma tools: <bin> ==` and one line per tool, `build info`, `membw`/`pinner`/`pigemma-probe` version lines.
- Hints, then `build.json <path>`.
- `--dry-run` prints the commands as `+ cmd` lines and a `== DRY RUN ==` summary. It writes nothing and takes no build lock.
- Logs go to stderr.

build.json (default $PIGEMMA_OUT/build.json = pi/out/build.json; written atomically and validated with Python; also written with status "failed" when a step fails):
- Top level: format_version 1, tool, tool_version, created_at, status ok|configured|failed, error, argv.
- `host`: hostname, kernel, machine, page_size, nproc, ram_total_kb, ram_available_kb, cpu_model, cpu_implementer, cpu_part, cpu_features[], in_container, emulated, qemu_suspected, protected_override, fake_proc.
- `llama`: dir, repo_url, from_desktop, requested_commit, commit, commit_short, verified, shallow, dirty, source_method (use|fetch-depth1|clone-blob-none|switch|rsync|copy|unverified), source_changed, build_dir, bin_dir, build_number_override, configure_args[], generator, jobs, rebuilt, targets[{name, path, exists, bytes}], version, build_number, version_commit, llama_bench_help, seconds{source, configure, build}, logs{}.
- `llama.arch`: requested, mode, fallback_used, fallback_reason, cmake_flags[], arm_detected_flags, effective_flags[], machine_supports{dotprod, i8mm, sve, sme}.
- `tools`: null, or {source_dir, build_dir, bin_dir, rebuilt, seconds, configure_args, targets[], membw_version, pinner_version, probe_help, logs, build_info (the embedded pigemma-tools-build.json)}.
- `toolchain`: gcc, gxx, cmake, git, make, ninja.
- `disk`: path, free_before_bytes, free_after_bytes, source_bytes, llama_build_bytes, tools_build_bytes, objects_cleaned, objects_freed_bytes.
- `config`: nice_level, keep_free_gb, min_free_gb, min_mem_gb, build_jobs.
- `warnings[]`, `notes[]`.

Environment and test hooks: LLAMA_DIR, PIGEMMA_OUT, NICE_LEVEL, KEEP_FREE_GB, BUILD_JOBS (via pi_config.env and common.sh); PIGEMMA_MACHINE (overrides uname -m); PIGEMMA_HEARTBEAT_S (progress interval, default 30); LLAMA_REPO_URL; PIGEMMA_RSYNC_RSH; CMAKE_GENERATOR=Ninja selects ninja. PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC also redirects /proc/cpuinfo for the arch decision.

On the real Pi: `PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1 LLAMA_DIR=~/pigemma/llama.cpp nohup pi/02_build_llama.sh --with-tools > pi/out/build.out 2>&1 &` reuses the existing ad-hoc build (judged up to date, with a build-number note) and only compiles the tools.
entries.self_test:
All runs used container-local /tmp or the session scratchpad. The repo was mounted read-only after the first run, nothing was written under pi/out, tools/build or third_party, and all containers were started with --rm.
- `bash -n pi/02_build_llama.sh`: OK. No CR characters, ASCII. shellcheck is not installed.

Git Bash (Windows):
- `--version` and `--help` exit 0. Unknown option, bad `--commit`, `--jobs 0`, bad `--arch`, `--with-tools=1` and a missing value each exit 1.
- `LLAMA_DIR=/` exits 1. `--arch pi5` with PIGEMMA_MACHINE=x86_64 exits 1.
- PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC=tests/fixtures/pi_proc_cf1_16gb: exit 4 (protected host). With PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1 it gets past the gate and stops at exit 3 (no cmake on Windows).
- PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC=pi_proc_16gb: exit 3 (no cmake). Re-checked after all edits.

x86 Docker (pi-gemma4-build):
- T1/T1b: dry runs print the exact fetch/clone/cmake/build commands and create nothing.
- T7: a bench lock held via `python3 -m pigemma.paths lock --hold` gives exit 4; `--ignore-lock` gives 0.
- T2/B1: real build from `--from-desktop /work/third_party/llama.cpp` (tar path) with `--with-tools --jobs 10`. Exit 0 in 325 s and again in 339 s (llama build 179 s, tools 146 s). Reports `version: 0.5.0-dev (build 11398, commit a7b94df)`, all 5 llama binaries and 3 tools present, build.json valid, membw runs. Footprint: source 217 MB, llama build 199 MB, tools build 71 MB.
- T3: re-run is up to date in 1 s.
- First run found the lock bug: T3b and T4, started within 30 s of a finished build, were refused with exit 4.
- After the fix: B1 then B2 back-to-back, B2 takes the lock at once and exits 0; no orphaned `sleep 30` processes.
- B3: touching membw.c rebuilds only the tools.
- C3: an external `flock` on .build.lock gives exit 4.
- B4: `--clean-objects` freed 40 MB.
- T5: a non-llama LLAMA_DIR gives exit 3. T6/T6b: huge `--min-free-gb` / `--min-mem-gb` give exit 3.
- C1: real depth-1 fetch of a7b94df2c616 from GitHub plus `--configure-only` in 14 s (38 MB .git; shallow, clean, verified; LLAMA_BUILD_NUMBER=11398 in the cache).
- C2: the same directory is reused with no network.
- C4: a tree without .git is recorded as unverified.
- C5: a dirty checkout plus another commit gives exit 3.
- D1: an ad-hoc-style build (pi/adhoc recipe, reports "build 1") is judged up to date, with the build-number note.
- D2: `--rebuild` relinks in 11 s and reports build 11398.

arm64 qemu (pi-gemma4-pi-emu:trixie):
- A0: dry run with PIGEMMA_EMULATED=1 selects the Pi 5 flags.
- A1: without PIGEMMA_EMULATED, CPU implementer 0x00 is detected as qemu and goes straight to pi5 mode. Exit 0 in 72 s. Cache has GGML_NATIVE=OFF and GGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH=armv8.2-a+dotprod+fp16; effective flag `-march=armv8.2-a+dotprod+fp16`.
- A2/A2': a fake real-Pi cpuinfo (0x41, no i8mm) makes native detection pick qemu's `+i8mm+sve2...+sme`. The mismatch triggers the fallback to pi5. Exit 0 in 106 s; after the fix, detection is reported once and `arm_detected_flags` is null for the pi5 build.
- A3: pinner.c and membw.c compile on aarch64 gcc 14 with the CMake flags under -Werror, and run `--version`.

Not run: a complete aarch64 compile of llama.cpp plus tools through pi/02 under emulation (about 22 minutes for llama.cpp alone in the earlier emulated build; tools not measured), and any run on the real Pi.
open_issues: Not run on the real Pi, and no complete aarch64 compile through pi/02 under emulation. aarch64 coverage is configure-only (both arch paths) plus a direct compile of pinner and membw. The orchestrator's earlier emulated build of llama.cpp (1321 s) used the same Pi 5 flags.

On the real Pi the existing ad-hoc build is in ~/pigemma/llama.cpp, but pi_config.env defaults LLAMA_DIR to ~/llama.cpp. Use LLAMA_DIR=~/pigemma/llama.cpp to reuse it (pi/02 then just writes build.json, with a note that the binaries report build 1). Otherwise pi/02 fetches and builds a second copy (about 0.4 GB on the SD card).

The catalog's protected_hosts still lists context-friend-1, so the hostname itself is deny-listed. FACTS says it should not be by default. Every real-Pi run of pi/02 therefore needs PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1, which matches FACTS. The fix belongs in the catalog and common.sh, not this file.

common.sh pick_jobs caps the RAM-safe job count at 4 regardless of RAM. On a 22 GiB host `--jobs 10` therefore warns 'exceeds the RAM-safe value 4 ... the build may OOM', which is misleading there. The behaviour is fine on the Pi; the wording belongs to common.sh.

Deviations from the manifest spec, all documented in the script header: (a) a depth-1 fetch of the full hash is preferred over `git clone --filter=blob:none`; the clone is kept as fallback, and the spec's `fetch --depth 1` after a blob:none clone is not run because it would make the clone shallow and GitHub rejects abbreviated hashes. (b) The arch fallback triggers on more than configure failure: a cpuinfo mismatch, an arch-flag compile error, SIGILL, and emulation. (c) --with-tools uses the same arch flags as the llama build instead of a fixed -DGGML_NATIVE=ON, so emulated builds do not SIGILL on a real Pi. (d) -DLLAMA_BUILD_NUMBER=11398 is passed for a shallow checkout at the pinned commit. (e) The default disk gate is 3 GB plus KEEP_FREE_GB=2 on /.

--from-desktop user@host:/d/... needs an SSH server and rsync on the Windows desktop, and Git for Windows ships no rsync. The simpler path is to let the Pi fetch from GitHub (the measured fetch is about 40 MB). A tree copied from the Windows checkout shows as dirty (CRLF) and gets a warning; it builds fine.

The tools build compiles llama/ggml a second time because tools/CMakeLists.txt uses add_subdirectory. That roughly doubles compile time on the Pi; on x86 the tools tree is 71 MB and took 146 s at -j10. This is a possible improvement for tools/CMakeLists.txt, not this file.
No tests/test_pi_scripts.py cases exist for pi/02, and that file belongs to another agent. The scratchpad drivers t_x86*.sh and t_arm*.sh could be adapted into integration tests.

entries.summary:
pi/03_bench_io_mem.sh is finished and tested. An earlier, interrupted attempt at this same assignment had already left a complete script (1731 lines) and its test module. I checked it against the real interfaces of pi/lib/common.sh, pigemma/feasibility.py (merge_io_mem, load_catalog, storage_class_for, nominal_ram_gb, LLAMA_EFFICIENCY, DEFAULT_MEM_BW_GBPS), membw's JSON, the tests/fixtures fio and membw captures, pi/02 (--with-tools), pi/00 (io-mem auto) and pi/05 (reads memory.read_gbps_by_threads, writes results/pi/calibration.json). All of them match.

I made two changes:
- In the script, ionice support is now checked once before the first redirected fio/dd run. Before, run_nice_io's one-time "no ionice" warning would have gone into the first job's .stderr file instead of the terminal.
- In the Docker integration test, I added --no-busy-check. It failed once, correctly, because another agent's container (pigemma-p02-selftest) pushed the Docker VM's loadavg1 to 7.26, above the 6.00 limit.

What the script does:
- Refuses on a protected host unless PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1, refuses on a busy host, and refuses while the bench lock is held.
- Runs 5 fio jobs with JSON output, O_DIRECT and --readonly: sequential 1M at QD1 and QD8, random expert-slab reads at QD1 and QD4, random 16k at QD1.
- Runs membw at 1, 2 and 4 threads.
- Writes results/pi/io_mem.json (results/pi-emu/ when PIGEMMA_EMULATED=1). Every metric is {value, unit, source:'measured', cmd, method, job, detail}.
- Keeps raw evidence in results/pi/raw/io_mem-<UTC>/.
- Prints a report with the measured table, each catalog field before and after the merge, and the PROJECTED derived numbers: in-RAM ceiling = mem_bw x 0.65 (assumed until calibration.json exists) / bytes per token for every catalog model, all-miss tok/s, and the miss MB/token and minimum hit rate at 1.0 and 2.0 tok/s.
- Deletes its test file. When fio is missing it prints the apt command and falls back to a dd sequential read, flagged as such.

The real Pi (context-friend-1) has no fio today, so a run there will produce only seq_read_mbps_qd1 from dd until someone installs fio with the owner's approval.
entries.interface_notes:
CLI:
- `bash pi/03_bench_io_mem.sh [--file auto|new|PATH] [--dir DIR] [--size-mb 2048] [--seconds 20] [--quick] [--out FILE] [--device NAME] [--threads 1,2,4] [--membw-size-mb 512] [--membw-reps 5] [--ioengine libaio] [--slab-bytes N] [--skip-io] [--skip-mem] [--require-fio] [--no-busy-check] [--dry-run]`
- `--check-jobs`: runs fio --parse-only on 7 job strings (layout, probe and the 5 measurement jobs); prints 'OK <job> <cmd>' per job.
- `--from-raw DIR [--out F] [--device NAME]`: rebuilds io_mem.json from raw outputs and never writes into DIR.
- Also: -h/--help, --version (prints 'pi/03_bench_io_mem.sh 1.0.0'), and --opt=value forms.

Defaults and flag behaviour:
- `--file auto` uses the largest *.gguf of at least 1 GiB under --dir (default MODEL_DIR), read-only, with no writes. If there is none, it writes a test file and deletes it afterwards.
- `--quick` means 512 MiB, 5 s per job, membw 256 MiB, 3 reps.
- Creating a test file needs free disk >= max(1.2 x size, size + KEEP_FREE_GB) on /.

Exit codes:
- 0: written, possibly partial (complete:false).
- 1: usage, internal error, failed merge check, or a real run under PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC.
- 3: precondition failed (disk, RAM, python, fio with --require-fio, file too small) or nothing measured.
- 4: refused (protected host without PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1, busy host, or bench lock held).

fio jobs (names equal tests/fixtures/fio_sample.fio):
- seq_read_qd1 and seq_read_qd8: bs=1M.
- rand_read_3mb_qd1 and rand_read_3mb_qd4: bs = the catalog 26b-q4 expert_unit_bytes 3,345,408 rounded up to max(4096, page size). That is 3,358,720 on the Pi's 16 KiB pages and 3,346,432 on 4 KiB.
- rand_read_16k_qd1: bs=16k.
- Every job uses --direct=1 --readonly --invalidate=1 --randrepeat=0 --runtime=S --time_based --output-format=json.
- A probe read picks the engine and direct mode: if libaio fails it uses psync (QD>1 flagged as effectively QD1); if O_DIRECT fails it uses buffered reads (flagged as an upper bound).

io_mem.json:
- Fields from the data_formats spec: host, device, collected_at, storage{seq_read_mbps_qd1, seq_read_mbps_qd8, rand_read_3mb_mbps_qd1, rand_read_3mb_mbps_qd4, rand_read_16k_iops, access_ms}, memory{read_gbps_by_threads{'1','2','4'}, copy_gbps, triad_gbps (best over thread counts), source:'measured', cmd, ...}.
- Extra fields: format_version, generator, kind 'measured', device_source, started_at, emulated, protected_override, complete, skipped{metric: reason}, flags[], test_file, settings, conditions{before, after}, host_facts, derived (kind 'projected'), raw_dir, notes, and warnings when there are any.
- Unmeasured metrics are ABSENT, so the catalog keeps its assumed value for them.
- access_ms = fio lat_ns.mean of the 16k QD1 job.
- The JSON merges through feasibility.load_catalog(io_mem=path); the script verifies this itself after writing.

Device name (when neither --device nor PIGEMMA_DEVICE is set):
- On a Pi 5 (board model, an rpi-2712 kernel, or emulated): the catalog pi5 device with the same nominal RAM tier and storage class, otherwise 'pi5-<tier>gb-<class>', which feasibility synthesizes (context-friend-1 becomes pi5-16gb-microsd).
- Other hosts: 'linux-<GB>gb-<class>'.

Environment the script honours: PIGEMMA_TOOLS_BIN (membw directory, default tools/build/bin), PIGEMMA_EMULATED, PIGEMMA_I_KNOW, PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC (dry-run, --check-jobs and --from-raw only), NICE_LEVEL. fio and dd run under nice + ionice -c3, membw under nice.
entries.self_test:
- `bash -n pi/03_bench_io_mem.sh`: OK. The file has LF line endings and no CR.
- `python -m pytest tests/test_pi03_bench_io_mem.py -q`: 18 passed. Covered: help, version, usage errors; --from-raw on the fio_sample/membw_sample fixtures (values equal the raw numbers, the merge marks fields 'measured', the catalog file is untouched); the dd-fallback partial result; explicit device plus calibration.json; nothing measured gives exit 3; dry-run plan with the 16 KiB page giving fio bs 3,358,720; emulated output going to results/pi-emu; protected-host exit 4 and the PIGEMMA_I_KNOW override; disk refusal exit 3; a real run under a fake root gives exit 1.
- `pytest -m integration` (Docker): 2 passed. `--check-jobs`: all 7 fio --parse-only OK (fio-3.36). A short real run in the build image passed.
- Manual Docker runs (outputs removed afterwards). All measured inside Docker Desktop's VM, not on a Pi:
  - Build image, 256 MiB, 2 s per job: seq qd1 415.6 MB/s, qd8 513.1; rand slab qd1 439.0, qd4 466.5; 16k at 3018 IOPS, access 0.329 ms; membw read 39.4 / 43.5 / 43.3 GB/s at 1 / 2 / 4 threads. Merge check passed; 18 s wall time.
  - Build image with fio hidden from PATH: the dd fallback measured seq qd1 417.3 MB/s, complete=false, apt hint printed.
  - pi-emu arm64 image (`--pi-emu`): libaio fell back to psync with flags, membw was missing and reported, output labelled EMULATED; 38 s.
- `pytest tests/test_catalog.py tests/test_feasibility.py tests/test_pi_scripts.py -k 'io_mem or bash_n or syntax or 03'`: all passed (1 skipped).
open_issues: Deviation from the manifest: the spec says fio bs=3345k. That is 3,425,280 B, is not the expert unit and is not 4 KiB aligned for O_DIRECT. The script uses the catalog's expert_unit_bytes (3,345,408) rounded up to the page size instead, and records the value it used in settings.

The real Pi (context-friend-1) has no fio. Without it only seq_read_mbps_qd1 is measured (dd iflag=direct); rand_read_3mb and access_ms stay ASSUMED. The script never installs packages; installing fio there needs the operator's approval (sudo apt-get install -y fio).

membw for the Pi must be built first (bash pi/02_build_llama.sh --with-tools, which installs it in tools/build/bin), or PIGEMMA_TOOLS_BIN must point at it. There is no arm64 membw yet, so emulated runs skip the memory measurement.

The catalog has no 'pi5-16gb-microsd-real' device (FACTS.md asked for one). Auto-naming therefore gives context-friend-1 the synthesized 'pi5-16gb-microsd'. Pass --device or PIGEMMA_DEVICE to target a specific profile.
Emulated runs inside a Docker container with no --memory cap are named after the VM's RAM (for example pi5-32gb-unknown). With a --memory 8g/16g cap, facts.cgroup_mem_max gives the right tier.

The busy-host gate (loadavg1 > 2 x max(1, nproc/4)) correctly refuses on the desktop while other Docker jobs run. That is why the integration test now passes --no-busy-check; real measurements should keep the gate on.

I deleted 4 old self-test output folders, pi/out/selftest-p03{,-dd,-emu,-shm} (generator 'pi/03_bench_io_mem.sh 1.0.0', 08:52-08:55 UTC). They were left by the earlier, interrupted attempt at this same task; pi/out is gitignored.

entries.summary:
pi/04_fetch_model.sh is finished and tested. An earlier attempt had left a complete script (about 1490 lines) and tests/test_pi_04_fetch_model.py. I kept that work after checking it against the manifest spec, FACTS.md, pi/lib/common.sh, pigemma.feasibility and catalog.json.

Two bugs fixed:
1. Every real download died with exit 1 just before pi/out/fetch.json was written. In _fm_write_json, an array element `override:sn=$([ ... = 1 ] && echo PIGEMMA_I_KNOW)` returns 1 when there is no override, which trips set -e. Both values (override, emulated) are now computed before the assignment.
2. The 'upstream OK' log line printed 'matches the catalog<hash>' because of a ${x:+..}${x:-..} mistake.

Tests added:
- test_from_desktop_flat_layout_and_partial_resume: SRC/<file> fallback after rsync exit 23, plus appending to an existing .part.
- test_from_desktop_dry_run_plan.
- test_sha_from_x_linked_etag_or_unverified: no catalog sha256, so X-Linked-ETag is the reference; with neither, the file is recorded unverified with exit 0 and no stamp. A `no_etag` switch was added to the local test server for this.

Behaviour vs spec:
- assert_safe_host runs first.
- Auto mode collects fresh facts with MODEL_DIR = --dest, then runs `pigemma.feasibility --emit env [--want --model]`.
- Explicit --quant QUANT|ID is a plain catalog lookup.
- Placeholder catalog entries are refused (exit 3, catalog-refresh hint).
- Disk rule: max(MIN_FREE_DISK_FACTOR x remaining, remaining + KEEP_FREE_GB if on /).
- Auto mode falls back to the best model that fits the disk. On the real 16 GB microSD Pi that is 26b-ud-q3_k_m, matching FACTS.
- A HEAD check of X-Linked-Size / X-Linked-ETag happens before any download. Real HF headers matched the catalog byte for byte (26b-ud-q3_k_m, 31b-mtp).
- ETA comes from a timed 20 MB ranged probe, with a labelled 'assumed 10 MB/s' fallback.
- Download: separate `nice -n 10 ionice -c3 curl -fL -C -` attempts, each resuming from the current .part size (FACTS rule, instead of curl --retry).
- Byte size and sha256 are verified (catalog sha, else X-Linked-ETag), then <file>.part is renamed to <file> and a .sha256 stamp is written.
- --draft fetches the family's MTP sidecar (or DFlash with --draft-type dflash).
- --from-desktop uses rsync -aP --partial --append-verify.
- --bg runs detached with nohup; a lock allows one fetch per PIGEMMA_OUT.
- pi/out/fetch.json is written. --dry-run writes nothing and touches no network.
entries.interface_notes:
CLI: bash pi/04_fetch_model.sh [options] [-- extra pigemma.feasibility args]. --opt=value also works.

Options:
- --model 26b|31b|ID: passed to feasibility as --want in auto mode; restricts the family in explicit mode.
- --quant auto|QUANT|ID: default auto. A non-empty QUANT_OVERRIDE from config replaces the default. Matching is case-insensitive. A quant that exists in both families needs --model (exit 1).
- --draft; --draft-type mtp|dflash (default mtp; setting it implies --draft).
- --dest DIR: default MODEL_DIR, or the facts file's model_dir when --facts is given.
- --from-desktop SRC: user@host:/path/models or a local directory. Candidate paths tried in order: SRC/<catalog local_path minus models/>, SRC/<org>__<repo>/<file>, SRC/<file>, SRC/<basename>.
- --ssh-opts "OPTS", --facts FILE, --sim FILE, --catalog FILE.
- --json FILE: default $PIGEMMA_OUT/fetch.json = pi/out/fetch.json.
- --strict: exit 2 when only slow operation is possible (default: warn and fetch).
- --no-disk-fallback, --pin-revision (resolve/<catalog revision>), --token-file FILE.
- --no-probe, --no-verify, --reverify.
- --attempts N: default 30 consecutive attempts without progress. --retry-delay S: default 10, grows to 60.
- --bg, --dry-run, -h/--help, --version.

Exit codes:
- 0: ok, already present and verified, or a dry-run plan.
- 1: usage, network, verification, or a wrong-size existing file (never deleted).
- 2: slow only and --strict.
- 3: not viable, placeholder entry, not enough disk, missing tool.
- 4: protected or busy host, or another fetch is running (lock $PIGEMMA_OUT/.fetch.lock).

stdout: shell-safe `FETCH_*=value` lines (printf %q), eval-able. With --dry-run, '# <planned command>' comment lines come first. Keys:
- FETCH_DRY_RUN, FETCH_SELECTION (auto|auto-disk-fallback|explicit), FETCH_VERDICT, FETCH_VERDICT_EXIT
- FETCH_MODEL_ID, FETCH_FAMILY, FETCH_QUANT, FETCH_REPO, FETCH_FILE, FETCH_BYTES, FETCH_SHA256, FETCH_URL
- FETCH_SOURCE (huggingface | desktop:SRC), FETCH_DEST, FETCH_PATH, FETCH_STATE (absent|partial|complete), FETCH_STATUS (planned|downloaded|copied|present)
- FETCH_REMAINING_BYTES, FETCH_FREE_BYTES, FETCH_NEED_BYTES, FETCH_ETA_S, FETCH_ETA_SOURCE
- FETCH_LLAMA_FLAGS, FETCH_PROJECTED_TOK_S
- FETCH_DRAFT_ID, FETCH_DRAFT_FILE, FETCH_DRAFT_BYTES, FETCH_DRAFT_SPEC_TYPE, FETCH_DRAFT_URL, FETCH_DRAFT_PATH
- Real runs only: FETCH_DOWNLOADED_BYTES, FETCH_SHA256_VERIFIED, FETCH_DRAFT_SHA256_VERIFIED, FETCH_JSON.
- --bg prints FETCH_BG_PID, FETCH_LOG ($PIGEMMA_OUT/fetch.log) and FETCH_JSON instead.

Everything human-readable (config, verdict table, plan banner, progress every 30 s) goes to stderr.

fetch.json (atomic, UTF-8):
- Spec keys: model_id, file, bytes (int), sha256_verified (bool), seconds (int).
- Item keys: kind, quant, family, repo, revision, path, url, source, status, sha256, sha256_expected, sha256_source (catalog|x-linked-etag|null), downloaded_bytes, avg_mbps, attempts, verify_seconds, spec_type.
- Run keys: format_version 1, tool, created_at, host, dest, selection, verdict, verdict_exit, llama_flags, fits_repacked, projected_tok_s (+ projected_tok_s_kind 'projected'), probe_mbps, eta_s, eta_source, total_seconds, emulated, override ('PIGEMMA_I_KNOW'|null), notes[].
- draft: {same item keys} or null.

File placement:
- Final file: <dest>/<catalog file>; the 31B MTP lands at <dest>/MTP/mtp-gemma-4-31B-it-Q4_0.gguf. This is the first candidate pi/05_run.sh model_candidates() checks.
- Transfer file: <file>.part, renamed only after the size and sha256 checks pass.
- <file>.sha256 (sha256sum format) is a stamp: a later run trusts it while it is newer than the file.
- Existing copies at <dest>/<org>__<repo>/<file> and <dest>/<basename> are recognised as present.

Environment knobs: HF_ENDPOINT (default https://huggingface.co; used by the tests' local server), HF_TOKEN / HUGGING_FACE_TOKEN (sent via a 0600 `curl -H @file`, never printed), HF_LIMIT_RATE, PIGEMMA_FETCH_POLL_S (2), PIGEMMA_FETCH_PROGRESS_S (30), PIGEMMA_FETCH_PROBE_MIN (200000000), plus everything from pi_config.env / common.sh. In particular PIGEMMA_I_KNOW, MIN_FREE_DISK_FACTOR, KEEP_FREE_GB, NICE_LEVEL and QUANT_OVERRIDE.
open_issues: Deviation from the manifest: no `curl --retry 10 --retry-delay 5`. FACTS.md 2026-10-05 says curl's --retry restarts from the first attempt's offset and truncated a 4.3 GB partial on the real Pi, so each attempt is a separate `curl -C -` that resumes from the current .part size. It gives up after --attempts (30) consecutive attempts without progress. `--speed-limit 100000 --speed-time 60` aborts stalled Wi-Fi transfers.

Deviation: data goes to <file>.part and is renamed only after the size and sha256 checks pass. A verified file gets a <file>.sha256 stamp next to it, which pi/05 and gguf readers ignore. --from-desktop adds --append-verify to the manifest's `rsync -aP --partial`.

The manifest puts the URL-construction test in tests/test_pi_scripts.py, but that file belongs to the pi/lib/common.sh agent. The pi/04 tests live in tests/test_pi_04_fetch_model.py; the bash -n sweep in test_pi_scripts.py still covers pi/04.

Bug fixed from the earlier attempt: under set -e, every real run died with exit 1 just before fetch.json was written (a failing $(...) inside the FM_J=(...) assignment). Any earlier claim that the end-to-end tests passed was wrong; they pass now.

--from-desktop has only been tested against a local directory on Linux. Copying over real ssh to the Windows desktop is untested: the desktop needs an sshd and rsync, and neither is known to exist. On Windows/Git Bash there is no rsync, so those tests skip there.

On the real 16 GB microSD Pi, `--model 31b` in auto mode picks 31b-q3_k_s (13.21 GB, which leaves 2.01 GB free with the draft), not the 31B UD-IQ3_XXS that FACTS plans for the real-Pi tests. The ranking belongs to pigemma.feasibility. Use `--quant UD-IQ3_XXS --model 31b` explicitly for that test.

assert_safe_host reports 'context-friend-1' as deny-listed via catalog.protected_hosts, although FACTS says DENY_HOSTS must no longer contain it. The contextfriend* service check requires PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1 on that box anyway. This is the catalog's or common.sh's concern, not this file's.

The speed probe only runs when more than PIGEMMA_FETCH_PROBE_MIN (200 MB) remain; otherwise the ETA uses the labelled assumption of ~10 MB/s. In dry runs the ETA is always that assumption, because a dry run makes no network calls.
--bg detaches with nohup only (no setsid), as FACTS recommends. curl inherits the ignored SIGHUP. Poll pi/out/fetch.log and fetch.json for progress and the result.

entries.summary:
pi/05_run.sh is finished and tested. A 2,061-line version from an earlier, interrupted run of this assignment was already there, with no test file. I reviewed it against the real common.sh, bench.py, feasibility.py and llama.cpp a7b94df flags, fixed what was wrong and added tests/test_pi05_run.py (51 tests).

Fixes:
- **Quant bug:** for a model file not in the catalog the quant was always set to "" (a garbage expression); it now comes from paths.guess_quant.
- **Model lookup:** files are now looked up only in MODEL_DIR, the same places pigemma.feasibility checks. The old extra fallback to the repo's own models/ folder meant a run could pick a model the verdict thought was missing, and made the tests depend on this desktop's downloads.
- **Disk-blocked rows:** a model the verdict blocked only because there was no room to download it (NO_DISK, or a dense model that would run slowly) is allowed again when its file is already present.
- **Quoted extra flags:** for chat and server, --flags are now split with shell quoting rules, so `--api-key 'a b'` stays one argument.
- **New --calibration-out option:** writes the calibration file somewhere other than results/pi/calibration.json, so tests no longer write into the repo.
- **No stray folder:** chat and server no longer create results/pi/raw (they write no results). My first test runs had left an empty results/pi/raw; I removed it.

What the script does:
- **Checks first:** safe host, not busy, then the feasibility verdict (a "slow only" verdict, exit 2, is accepted). It then picks the model and flags from pi/out/feasibility.json, adding -nr whenever the model does not fit with repacking.
- **Mlock:** removed from the flags on protected hosts.
- **Protected host with PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1:** -nr is forced, and the repack variant is refused unless --allow-repack.
- **RAM check (exit 3):** needs file bytes + 0.5 GB when the model fits in RAM, or non-expert bytes + 0.5 GB when it streams experts. A draft adds its size; memory already locked by a running pinner is credited.
- **bench:** one `pigemma.bench matrix` run per variant (llama-bench -t 2,3,4 -p 64 -n 32 -r 3 -o json [--repack 0] ...). The default/repack variant is refused when the model does not fit with repacking.
- **stream-bench:** `pigemma.bench completion` on the English calibration text (-n 64 --temp 0), with `vmstat 1` alongside, then a Hebrew chat sample. Both outputs are printed.
- **chat / server:** llama-cli / llama-server with an optional draft (--draft auto picks the family's MTP sidecar and passes --spec-type draft-mtp explicitly). The server holds the bench lock for its lifetime and refuses a port already in use.
- **Calibration:** results/pi/calibration.json gets the measured in-RAM efficiency, tg x bytes/token / memory bandwidth. Bandwidth comes from results/pi/io_mem.json; without it the value is labelled assumed. pigemma.feasibility.load_calibration reads the file.
- **Records:** each results file gets extra.pi05 with the run's context, and pi/out/last_run.json plus last_<subcommand>.json are written.
entries.interface_notes:
USAGE (identical to the manifest; a test checks it):
`pi/05_run.sh bench|stream-bench|chat|server [--model <gguf>] [--draft <gguf>] [--variants default,norepack] [--pin] [-p 'text']`
Run it as `bash pi/05_run.sh ...` from anywhere; it sources pi/lib/common.sh.

COMMON OPTIONS (`--opt=value` also works):
- `--model GGUF|catalog-id`, `--want 26b|31b|ID`
- `-t N` (bench also takes a comma list), `-c N`
- `--flags "..."` (repeatable; also anything after a bare `--`)
- `--pin` and `--pin-arg ARG` (repeatable)
- `--allow-repack`, `--out DIR` (default results/pi; results/pi-emu when PIGEMMA_EMULATED=1), `--experiment E0..E8|adhoc` (default E8)
- `--sim F`, `--feasibility-arg ARG` (repeatable; e.g. `--feasibility-arg=--io-mem --feasibility-arg=none`)
- `--idle-check-s S` (default 10), `--idle-max-pct P` (default 5), `--timeout S`
- `--no-calibrate`, `--calibration-out F` (default results/pi/calibration.json), `--io-mem F` (default results/pi/io_mem.json)
- `--dry-run`, `-h/--help`, `--version`

PER SUBCOMMAND:
- bench: `--variants LIST` (default norepack, plus default when the model fits with repacking and repack is allowed; names default norepack nommap mlock kvq8 hybrid_negctrl, joined with '+'), `--bench-threads LIST` (default 2,3,4; counts above nproc are dropped), `--pp|-p N` (64), `--tg|-n N` (32), `-r N` (3), `--no-verdict-flags`.
- stream-bench: `-f FILE` or `-p TEXT` (default data/calibration/en_tech_moe_streaming.txt), `-n N` (64), `--chat`, `--no-he`, `--he-prompt-id ID` (gen-he-explain-01), `--he-n N` (48).
- chat / server: `--draft GGUF|ID|auto` (auto = the family's catalog MTP sidecar), `--spec-type T|none` (default: from the draft), `--draft-n-max N`. chat also takes `-p` / `-f` (one turn, adds -st) and `-n`. server takes `--host` (0.0.0.0) and `--port` (8080), and no -p/-n.

EXIT CODES:
- 0 ok.
- 1 usage or internal error, or a run failed (its results file is still written with a 'failed:' note).
- 3 precondition failed: verdict not viable, RAM check, model / draft / binary / prompt missing, size mismatch, every bench variant refused, QUANT_OVERRIDE matches nothing.
- 4 refused: protected or busy host, bench lock held, port in use, `--pin` where mlock is not allowed.
- chat and server pass through the llama tool's own exit code.

STDOUT: one path per written results file (whatever bench.py prints). With `--dry-run`, the exact command lines instead (for chat/server: `nice -n 10 <bin> ...`; with --pin, the pi/06 command comes first). Everything else goes to stderr.

FILES WRITTEN:
- `<out>/E8_*.json` results files, each with extra.pi05 = {script, version, subcommand, label, argv, model_path, verdict, mode, projected_tok_s, verdict_reason, verdict_flags, effective_flags, extra_flags, mlock_removed, forced_nr, protected_override, emulated, selection_notes, feasibility_json, facts_json, ram_gate{need_bytes, mem_available_bytes, rule}, pin{pid, vm_lck_bytes, started_here}|null, thermal{before, after}, vmstat{file, n_samples, mean, max}, raw_bench_json}. Notes are added for a PIGEMMA_I_KNOW override, removed mlock, forced -nr, emulation, pinning, and random-token llama-bench in streaming mode.
- `<out>/bench_<model>_<variant>_<UTC>.json`: the raw llama-bench JSON. `<out>/raw/pi05_<sub>_<model>_<UTC>.vmstat.log`.
- calibration.json = {format_version 1, generator, created_at, host, llama_efficiency{value, source ('measured: ...' or 'assumed: ...'), from: [tg tok/s, bytes/token, mem_bw GB/s]}, inputs{...}, notes, history[]}. Written only for in-RAM runs, never when emulated, and skipped when a run read more than 2% of bytes/token from storage or the value falls outside 0.05..1.5.
- `$PIGEMMA_OUT/last_run.json` and `last_<subcommand>.json` = {subcommand, exit_code, model{id, path}, verdict, mode, effective_flags, pinned, results[], metrics[{file, label, variant, threads, pp_tok_s, tg_tok_s, read_bytes_per_token, majflt_per_token, load_s, coherent, failed}], calibration, out_dir, emulated, protected_override}. pi/06 `ab` can read last_stream-bench.json.

WHAT pi/06_pin_hotset.sh MUST PROVIDE (not written yet):
- `start --model <gguf> [pin args]` exits 0 (2 = partial, accepted).
- `stop`.
- A pidfile at `$PIGEMMA_OUT/pinner.pid` naming a live process whose /proc comm starts with 'pinner'; its VmLck is credited in the RAM check.
- pi/05 only stops a pinner it started itself.

ENVIRONMENT: everything from common.sh (THREADS, CTX, QUANT_OVERRIDE, MODEL_DIR, LLAMA_DIR / PIGEMMA_LLAMA_BIN, NICE_LEVEL, ALLOW_MLOCK, PIGEMMA_I_KNOW, PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC, PIGEMMA_EMULATED, PIGEMMA_CATALOG, PIGEMMA_LOCK_FILE, PIGEMMA_PYTHON).

TESTS: tests/test_pi05_run.py can be imported for its helpers: `helper_source()` extracts the embedded Python helper, `_env()` builds a hermetic environment, plus `fake_root()`, `write_exe()`, `ARGV_ECHO`, `_tiny_catalog()`.
entries.self_test:
No model inference was run; none was required.
- `bash -n pi/05_run.sh`: OK. The file has LF line endings, the right shebang and `set -euo pipefail`.
- **Windows** (Git Bash + Python 3.14): `python -m pytest tests/test_pi05_run.py`: 48 passed, 1 skipped (the Linux-only end-to-end test), about 2.5 min.
- **Neighbouring test modules:** test_pi_scripts.py (runs `bash -n` over every pi script), test_experiment_plan.py (checks documented commands against the scripts) and test_docs_hypotheses.py all passed, apart from 11 tests skipped because shellcheck is not installed.
- **Linux, Docker build image** (Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.12): the full module, 49 passed, including the end-to-end test. pytest's pure-Python packages were mounted read-only from the Windows install; nothing was installed into the image.
- **Emulated Pi image** (arm64 Debian 13, bash 5.2.37, Python 3.13.5): a 6-test subset (end-to-end, dry-run bench, model selection, protected-host override, chat/server): all passed.
- **Manual dry runs:**
  - 16 GB NVMe fixture: 26b-q4 FITS_MAPPED, bench plans one llama-bench line `-t 2,3,4 -p 64 -n 32 -r 3 -o json --repack 0 -lm mmap+mlock -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0`; asking for the default variant is refused.
  - context-friend-1 fixture: exit 4 without the override; with PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1 mlock is removed (`-lm mmap`) and --pin exits 4.
- **Manual end-to-end in Docker** with fake binaries: bench wrote 4 results files plus the raw JSON copy, and calibration came out at llama_efficiency 0.4980 (measured). stream-bench wrote the English and Hebrew results files and printed both outputs. Without the fake system root, vmstat recorded 6 samples into extra.pi05.vmstat.
- **Clean-up check:** after the final runs nothing is left under results/pi or pi/out.
open_issues: The file already existed from an earlier, interrupted run of this same assignment (2,061 lines, no tests). I kept its design, fixed the problems listed in the summary and wrote tests/test_pi05_run.py.

Deviation from the spec: bench runs `python3 -m pigemma.bench matrix` once per variant instead of a bare llama-bench followed by `pigemma.bench parse-bench`. The llama-bench command line and the results format are the same, and this adds the bench lock, idle check, failure records and raw logs. The raw JSON is saved as results/pi/bench_<model>_<variant>_<UTC>.json rather than bench_<variant>.json. EXPERIMENT_PLAN's table already says bench_*.json.

Behaviour beyond the spec: on a protected host run with PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1, -nr is forced for stream-bench, chat and server, and the default (repack) bench variant is refused unless --allow-repack. Reason: the repacked copy lives in anonymous memory the system cannot reclaim for the host's services, which is the same problem as mlock.

--pin relies on pi/06_pin_hotset.sh, which is not written yet. It must accept `start --model <gguf> [args]` and `stop`, and keep the pinner pid in $PIGEMMA_OUT/pinner.pid. If pi/06 is missing, a real --pin run exits 3; the dry run only prints the planned command.

pigemma.feasibility's disk check marks the 14.44 GB 26b-q4 as fitting on context-friend-1's microSD (15.50 GB free), although FACTS.md says it does not fit once the 2 GB free-space rule is applied. This belongs to feasibility and pi/04. pi/05 is unaffected unless the file is actually there; on the real Pi it falls back to the downloaded UD-Q3_K_M.

Config mismatch on the real Pi: CLAUDE.md says the Pi's llama.cpp build is in ~/pigemma/llama.cpp/build/bin, but pi_config.env defaults LLAMA_DIR to ~/llama.cpp. Set LLAMA_DIR or PIGEMMA_LLAMA_BIN on the Pi, otherwise pi/05 exits 3 with 'llama-* not found'. The runbook should say this.
chat only checks the bench lock and does not hold it, because nothing supervises an interactive session; server holds it for its whole lifetime.

stream-bench's vmstat log covers the whole llama-completion run (lock, idle check, load, prompt, generation). It is skipped under PIGEMMA_FAKE_PROC, so in tests it only ran in the manual Docker run without the fake system root. The per-token read and page-fault numbers come from bench.py, sampled during generation only.

The calibration formula (tg x (non-expert + K experts per layer bytes) / memory bandwidth) counts each token's experts as fully read from RAM. For llama-bench's random-token runs this is fine in RAM mode. Calibration is skipped when more than 2% of bytes/token came from storage, which on a first cold run is likely, so stream-bench may skip it until the page cache is warm.

The Linux-only end-to-end test is skipped on Windows (Windows Python cannot run an extensionless fake binary). For self-testing it was run in Docker with pytest mounted from the Windows install; the build image itself has no pytest.

entries.summary:
I wrote pc/trace_collect.sh, the E3 driver, plus its test module. The real `--smoke` run on the 26B passed. `--quick` and `--full` were not run on the real model: the rules allow only the smoke run. The full host pipeline for those tiers (validate, meta, merge, stats, checks, envelope) is tested with a fake Docker runner.

**What the script does**
- It runs `pigemma-probe --mode moe-trace` in Docker through `pc/docker_run.sh`, using the spec's exact command form. There is one probe run per corpus file in data/calibration, plus one for gen_prompts.json (with `--chat --gen 256`).
