- After each run it calls `python -m pigemma.trace validate` and writes `<trace>.meta.json` with `python -m pigemma.trace meta`. The meta records the container's fingerprint, a sha256 of the GGUF's first 16 MiB, the corpus sha256, the probe's own wall time and the coherence check.
- For `--quick`/`--full` it then merges into `<out>/all.moetrace`, validates that, and runs `trace stats` to `<out>/all.stats.json` plus `results/h1/all.*.csv`.
- It prints CHECK lines for the E3 "Trace VALID" rule, an E3 preview (coverage@32, adjacent reuse, skew class, prefetch gain, C3), and a projected duration for `--full` based on the quick run's probe tok/s.
- It holds the bench lock for the whole tier by re-running itself under `python -m pigemma.paths lock --hold --min-free-gb 20`. The per-run `lock --hold` inside the container then sees the lock as inherited; this was confirmed in the real run.

**Real smoke run (MEASURED, 14:20–14:36, Docker, -t 6)**
- Validate clean; 72 records = 64 prefill + 8 generated; all 30 MoE layers.
- Token ids and expert sets are 100% identical to tests/fixtures/golden_26b_72tok.moetrace, even though the golden used `-ub 512` and this run `-ub 256`.
- Probe speed: prompt 39.2 tok/s, generation 14.3 tok/s, callback overhead 3 ms.
- Model load took 894 s, not the ~1-2 min in FACTS. During the run D: was also serving another job's 31B download/split; background CPU was ~12%.
- Outputs: traces/26b/smoke/en_tech_moe_streaming.moetrace (+ sidecars) and results/h1/raw/trace_collect_20261005T122053Z_*.log.

**Gates seen working on the real machine**
- Before that run, real attempts were refused with exit 4 while other agents held the bench lock (31B act-dump, H2 decompose/oracle).
- One attempt was refused because `llama-gguf-split` was running. That job only moves file bytes, so I narrowed the busy check to model-loading tools.

**Deviations from the spec (all documented in the script header as D1–D13)**
- The merge takes an explicit list of this run's traces instead of the `traces/26b/*.moetrace` glob, so an old `all.moetrace` or smoke trace is never merged.
- The smoke trace goes to `<out>/smoke/` so it never mixes with the quick/full traces. The golden fixture is never overwritten; the copy command is only printed.
- New exit code 5: traces were written but an acceptance check failed.
- One E3 results envelope per quick/full run in results/h1/ (passes `pigemma.results validate --strict`). The spec doesn't ask for it; `--no-envelope` turns it off.
- Before a run, the outputs it will regenerate are deleted, so a failed run never leaves a stale file that looks current.
- `-c` is raised automatically when a chunk plus generation does not fit.
- The script refuses (exit 4) while another llama/probe job runs; `--ignore-busy` overrides.

**Added options:** `--resume`, `--keep-going` and `--files` (the full option list is in the interface notes).
entries.interface_notes:
**CLI**
`bash pc/trace_collect.sh [--smoke|--quick|--full] [--gen N] [--threads 12] [--probs-top K] [--out traces/26b]`. The `--opt=value` form also works.

Extra options:
- `--prompt-gen N` (default 256)
- `--model ID|PATH` (an MoE GGUF inside the repo; default 26b-q4; a dense model is exit 2)
- `--chunk-tokens N` (smoke 64, quick 1024, full 2048)
- `--ctx 4096`, `--batch 2048`, `--ubatch 256`
- `--files a,b` (corpus names or stems; run in the given order)
- `--prompts F`, `--no-prompts`
- `--probe-arg ARG` (repeatable, passed to the probe)
- `--csv-dir results/h1`, `--results-dir results/h1`, `--no-envelope`, `--log-dir results/h1/raw`
- `--resume`, `--keep-going`, `--no-merge`
- `--min-free-gb 20`, `--no-lock`, `--ignore-busy`
- `--verbose`, `--dry-run|-n`, `-h|--help`, `--version` (prints "pc/trace_collect.sh 1.0.0")

**Tiers**
- smoke: `-f en_tech_moe_streaming.txt --chunk-tokens 64 --gen 8 --tokens 72 --max-chunks 1`, written to `<out>/smoke/en_tech_moe_streaming.moetrace`. No merge, stats or envelope.
- quick: every data/calibration file with suffix txt|c|cc|cpp|cxx|h|hh|hpp|py|js|ts|rs|go|java|sh. README*, all.* (the quality corpus file), hidden and empty files are excluded. Order is C-locale sorted. Corpus id = the file stem (on a collision, or for all/smoke/the prompts stem: the name with '.' replaced by '_'). Then gen_prompts with `--chat --gen 256`.
- full: as quick with chunk 2048 and `--gen 256`.
- Probe flags on every run: `-nr -t T -c C -b B -ub U [--probs-top K]`.

**Outputs (quick/full, defaults)**
- `traces/26b/<id>.moetrace` with `.tokens.bin`, `.gen.txt`, `.meta.json`; `gen_prompts.moetrace` likewise.
- `traces/26b/all.moetrace` (+ sidecars, merged meta), `traces/26b/all.stats.json`, `results/h1/all.{per_layer,freq,lru_curve,cross_layer}.csv`.
- `results/h1/E3_<model>_moe-trace-<tier>_<threads>_<ts>_<run>.json`: kind measured; pp/tg = token-weighted probe tok/s; coherent; host = container fingerprint; extra has tier, n_prefill, n_gen, checks{name:{pass,detail}}, trace_valid, e3_preview, full_tier_projection (kind projected), runs[], background_cpu.
- Logs (gitignored): `results/h1/raw/trace_collect_<UTC>_<tier>.log` (driver), `..._<id>.probe.log` (full llama.cpp stderr + PIGEMMA_SUMMARY), `..._<tier>.runs.log` (JSON lines ledger).

**stdout / stderr**
- stdout: the plan (with `--dry-run`) or the final report: per-run table, `CHECK <name>: PASS|FAIL|SKIP (...)` lines, `TRACE VALID|NOT VALID`, the E3 preview, `PROJECTED --full ...`, and an outputs list. Smoke prints `CHECK smoke ...`, `INFO golden ...` and `SMOKE PASS|FAIL`.
- stderr: progress, a heartbeat every minute, and the probe's own lines.

**Exit codes**
- 0: ok (also --help and --dry-run)
- 1: a run or step failed
- 2: usage (including a path outside the repo or a dense model)
- 3: missing GGUF (or wrong size), probe, corpus/prompts file, Python 3.10+ with numpy, or Docker image
- 4: refused (bench lock held or low RAM, busy, disk < 1 GB, Docker unavailable); stderr line `trace_collect: REFUSED: ...`
- 5: traces written but an acceptance check failed
- 130: interrupted

**Environment hooks**
- `PIGEMMA_TRACE_DOCKER_RUN` replaces pc/docker_run.sh (same CLI).
- `PIGEMMA_TRACE_PROBE`: container-side probe path.
- `PIGEMMA_TRACE_BGCPU_S`: background-CPU sample length (default 5, 0 = off).
- Also honoured: `PIGEMMA_PYTHON`, `PIGEMMA_LOCK_HELD` (inherited lock), `PIGEMMA_IMAGE`.
open_issues: Load time: the first model load in Docker took 894 s (MEASURED; another job's 31B download/split was also using D:), against ~1-2 min in FACTS. It is unknown whether the Docker Desktop VM keeps the bind-mounted GGUF cached between containers. If it does not, --quick pays 8 such loads (up to ~2 h). Run --quick when D: is idle and compare the second run's load time in its probe log. Possible fix, not implemented: read the GGUF from the pigemma-models Docker volume (as pc/pagecache_limit.sh does).

The >= 10,000 prefill check passes by a small margin only: the corpus is 10,101 tokens (MEASURED with llama-tokenize, vocab only) plus ~0.4k prompt prefill. Removing or shrinking a calibration file makes --quick exit 5.
--quick and --full were not run on the real model (only the smoke run was allowed). They are covered by dry-runs and by fake-runner tests of the whole host pipeline.
Deviation: the merge takes an explicit list of this run's traces, not the spec's glob traces/26b/*.moetrace (docs/EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md says the same).

Deviation: the smoke trace goes to <out>/smoke/en_tech_moe_streaming.moetrace and adds --max-chunks 1. The golden fixture is never copied; only the cp command is printed. The new smoke trace matches the golden 100%.

Additions not in the spec: exit code 5 (traces written but an acceptance check failed); an E3 results envelope in results/h1/ (--no-envelope turns it off); a busy check that refuses (exit 4, --ignore-busy) while another model-loading llama tool or probe runs; options --resume, --keep-going, --files, --no-merge.
Before each run, the outputs that run will regenerate (per-item traces and sidecars, all.moetrace and sidecars, all.stats.json) are deleted, so a failed run leaves no stale file.
Coherence uses pigemma.quality.is_coherent on the raw gen.txt text through trace.build_meta, without strip_thinking. The prompts run uses the probe's default chat style (GGUF template, thinking off).
The probe tok/s in metas and the E3 envelope are measured with the recording callback active, inside Docker, during other agents' jobs. They are a by-product of E3, not engine speed (E0 owns that).
tests/test_trace_collect.py writes a temporary directory inside the repo (traces/_pytest_tc_<uuid>) because the driver only accepts repo paths. A pytest killed mid-test can leave one behind.
traces/26b/smoke/en_tech_moe_streaming.moetrace.meta.json from the real smoke run is tracked by git (the .gitignore keeps traces/**/*.json). The .moetrace and .tokens.bin files are ignored.

entries.summary:
pc/desktop_bench.ps1 is the desktop driver for E0, E1 and E2 (Windows PowerShell 5.1, also runs on PowerShell 7). It runs one model job at a time through pigemma.bench and pigemma.quality; the bench lock is enforced on the Python side.

- **Stage bench (E0):** measures membw (D5) in Docker under the lock and writes results/<date>/membw_desktop.json. Then runs `bench matrix` (26B: threads 4,6,12, tg 32, r 3; 31B: threads 6,12, tg 16, r 2), and `bench completion` per variant (-n 64, 6 threads, EN prompt). Finally it evaluates the E0 repack gate and the ±20% speed band and writes results/<date>/E0_GATE.md, printing PASS/FAIL per check.
- **Stage spec (E1):** per the 2026-10-05 FACTS update, it starts with `server-spec --variant plain,mtp-explicit --rounds 2` (interleaved) on both models. Then one round each of 26B mtp, dflash and ngram, plus dflash-explicit when mtp or dflash never drafted; for 31B, one round of mtp. It writes E1_SUMMARY.md: speedup vs plain, prompts at >= 1.2x, accept_rate, spec_active, spec_type_effective, identical_to_plain and a one-word verdict (useful / inactive / slower / bug / marginal).
- **Stage quality (E2):** `quality corpus`, kld-base (6 x 512), kld for norepack and hybrid_negctrl, and qa (plain plus every E1 variant that was spec_active). Optional: the hard Q&A set (-QaHard), and with -AllowDownload one lower quant per model (download via huggingface_hub with size and sha256 checks, then kld and qa, then delete).
- **End:** `results summarize results/<date> [+ this run's results/quality/qa_*.json] --md docs/results/DESKTOP_<date>.md`.
- **Resume and time box:** steps are skipped when their results already exist, unless -Force. A step that is re-run renames its earlier envelopes to *.superseded only after the re-run succeeds. -MaxMinutes stops new steps from starting (exit 5); per-child timeouts also apply.
- **Dry run:** -DryRun prints every driver command plus the exact llama.cpp command lines from each tool's own --dry-run, and writes nothing.
entries.interface_notes:
INVOCATION
- From a PowerShell session: `.\pc\desktop_bench.ps1 -Stage bench,spec,quality [-Models 26b,31b] [-Threads 4,6,12] [-Quick] [-Force] [-AllowDownload] [-DryRun]`.
- From cmd or Git Bash: `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File pc\desktop_bench.ps1 ...`. Comma lists work in both forms because the script splits them itself. With -Command the exit code is lost.
- -Help prints usage. `Get-Help pc\desktop_bench.ps1 -Full` gives full help. -Version prints `pc/desktop_bench.ps1 1.0.0`.

-STAGE AND -MODELS
- -Stage is required: bench|spec|quality, also E0/E1/E2 or all. Stages always run in the order bench, spec, quality.
- -Models accepts 26b, 31b (mapped to 26b-q4/31b-q4), any catalog id, or a .gguf path. 26B-family models always run before the 31B.

OTHER PARAMETERS (defaults)
- Paths and date: -Date yyyy-MM-dd (default today), -OutDir (default results/<date>/), -QualityDir (default results/quality/), -SummaryMd (default docs/results/DESKTOP_<date>.md).
- Time limits: -MaxMinutes 0, -StepTimeoutMin 60 (passed as --timeout to matrix, completion, kld-base and kld), -RequestTimeoutS 900.
- Runs: -RunThreads 6, -CompletionTokens 64, -Port 18080, -SpecRounds 2, -SpecTokens 200, -SpecPrompts 0 (all 8), -DraftNMax 0, -QaTokens 160, -KldChunks 6.
- Lock and idle check: -MinFreeGB 20, -IdleCheckS 10, -IdleMaxPct 5, -IdleWaitS 0, -RequireIdle.
- Lower quants and extras: -LowerQuant26 26b-ud-q3_k_m, -LowerQuant31 31b-ud-iq3_xxs, -KeepDownloads, -QaHard, -NoMembw, -NoSummary, -Python EXE (else PIGEMMA_PYTHON, then python, python3, py -3).

-QUICK
- Results go to results/<date>-quick/ and the summary to docs/results/DESKTOP_<date>-quick.md.
- Matrix: threads 6, r 1.
- E1: core only, 1 round, 2 prompts, 64 tokens.
- KLD: 2 chunks; reference logits under <out>/quality/.
- QA: ids en-01,en-02,he-01,he-02,num-01,num-02.
- No lower quants and no hard Q&A set.
- Explicitly passed parameters override these quick defaults.

EXIT CODES (worst wins, in this order)
- 4: refused. A step exited 4, or the bench lock was held at start. The run stops; the summary still renders.
- 3: missing model, binary, python or input.
- 1: a step failed, or an internal error.
- 6: everything ran, but the E0 repack gate is FAIL or INCOMPLETE for a model of this run.
- 5: the time box was reached.
- 2: usage error. This covers a missing or unknown -Stage, an unknown model, a bad -Threads or -Date, and stray arguments. Exception: a non-numeric value for an [int]/[double] parameter given via -File gives PowerShell's binding error, exit 1.
- 0: ok.
- Speed band, KLD and QA thresholds are results, not errors.

FILES WRITTEN
- results/<date>/:
  - E0_*, E1_* and E2_* envelopes (from bench.py and quality.py).
  - membw_desktop.json: raw `membw --json`, which cache_sim --e0-dir picks up.
  - E0_GATE.md: per model, a repack-gate table (Check / Value / Threshold / Result / Evidence), the speed band, the full matrix with tg/default ratios (the norepack penalty), the completion load/memory/buffer table, the membw best read and a verdict.
  - E1_SUMMARY.md.
  - raw/desktop_bench_<UTC>.log: driver log with commands, return codes and seconds.
- results/quality/:
  - ref_<model>.logits and its .json sidecar (written by quality.py).
  - qa_<model>_<variant>.json.
  - hard/qa_<model>_plain.json.
- docs/results/DESKTOP_<date>.md.
- Superseded results are renamed in place to <name>.<UTC>.superseded, which results summarize ignores. QA files get a backup copy before they are re-run.

SKIP RULES (what counts as "done")
- E0 matrix: one OK envelope per variant x thread x pp128/tg<N> with n >= reps. Only the missing variants are re-run, in one `--variants` invocation.
- E0 completion: an OK envelope with tg, per variant.
- E1 core: OK plain and mtp-explicit for every round 1..R, with matching extra.rounds, n_predict and n_requests.
- E1 other variants: an OK rounds=1 envelope for that variant.
- kld-base: the logits sidecar has ok, chunks == N, ctx 512, model bytes equal and the current all.txt sha256.
- kld: an OK E2 role=kld envelope against the same base logits path.
- qa: the file has qa_score, the current qa_set sha256 and the expected n_items.
- corpus: `quality corpus --check` returns 0.
- membw: a valid membw JSON is present.

E0 GATE RULE
- Uses the newest OK llama-completion envelope per variant.
- norepack: CPU_Mapped_mib >= 0.95 x model.bytes / 2^20, no CPU_REPACK* key, and private_peak_mb < 1500.
- hybrid_negctrl: a CPU_REPACK* key is present.
- Missing data gives INCOMPLETE, which also yields exit 6.
entries.self_test:
All commands were run from the repo root. Python is 3.14 on Windows.

1. **Parser:** System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser::ParseFile reports 0 errors.
2. **Help and usage:**
   - -Version and -Help exit 0.
   - These cases each exit 2 with a specific message: no -Stage, `-Stage foo`, `-Models 40b`, `-Threads 4,x`, a stray argument, `-Date 2026/10/05`, and a draft id passed as a model.
3. **Full dry run:** `-Stage bench,spec,quality -DryRun -AllowDownload -QaHard` exits 0 in about 26 s.
   - It lists all 36 steps, each with the driver command and the exact llama-bench/completion/server/perplexity lines.
   - It writes nothing: results/ is unchanged and no files were created.
   - The `-Quick -DryRun` and in-session `.\pc\desktop_bench.ps1 -Stage bench,spec -Models 26b,31b -Threads 4,6 -DryRun` variants also exit 0.
4. **Synthetic resume test:** realistic E0/E1/E2 envelopes, QA files and logits sidecars generated with pigemma.results.write_result in the scratchpad. PIGEMMA_LLAMA_BIN pointed at a nonexistent directory, plus a scratch lock.
   - All 32 steps skipped. The gate gave PASS for 26b and FAIL for a 31b with a synthetic 1600 MB private peak, so exit 6. With 26b only, exit 0.
   - E1_SUMMARY verdicts came out right: useful / inactive / bug / slower.
   - Partial state (one matrix row and one completion removed): only `--variants norepack` and that one completion re-ran. Earlier results were kept because the re-run failed. Exit 3.
   - `-MaxMinutes 0.0001` gave exit 5, and the summary still ran.
   - A lock held via `paths lock --hold` was refused at start with exit 4.
5. **Real binaries on a tiny synthetic llama GGUF** (tests/synth.write_tiny_llama_gguf, 76 KB), run only while results/.bench.lock was free:
   - bench stage: matrix with 4 variants x threads 2,4 plus 4 completions, gate and summary, in 6.7 s. Exit 6, because llama.cpp rounds a 0.07 MiB buffer, so the tiny model's gate is expected to fail.
   - -Force re-ran everything and superseded 20 old envelopes only after success. A plain re-run then skipped all steps.
   - spec stage against the real llama-server.exe: plain rounds 1 and 2 were measured. Draft variants failed as expected (no draft for a non-catalog model). ngram came out inactive. E1_SUMMARY.md was written. Exit 1.
   - quality stage: kld-base, KLD norepack (mean 2.1e-05) and hybrid_negctrl (mean 0.0), QA 0/16 (random weights) and the summary. Exit 0. A re-run skipped every step, exit 0.
6. **Plan test:** `pytest tests/test_experiment_plan.py`: 15 passed. This includes test_command_flags_exist_in_written_tools, which checks the documented -Stage, -Models, -DryRun and -AllowDownload parameters against this script.
7. **Download path:** exercised for real, though by mistake (see open issues). The 26b-ud-q3_k_m download completed: 12,728,497,888 B in 162 s with sha256 verified in 12 s. The file was then deleted.
open_issues: A self-test mistakenly passed -AllowDownload. It downloaded 26b-ud-q3_k_m (12.73 GB, sha256 verified) and about 11.66 GB of 31b-ud-iq3_xxs into models/unsloth__gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-GGUF and models/unsloth__gemma-4-31B-it-GGUF before the test's timeout killed it. I deleted both directories and the temp helper at about 14:14; no process of mine was left running, and D: went back to ~30 GB free. The models/unsloth__gemma-4-31B-it-GGUF directory that exists now was created at 14:17 by the orchestrator's pc/adhoc_31b_to_pi.sh, not by me, and I left it alone.
No real 26B or 31B run was made, per the rules; the test field says 'integration today'. E0, E1 and E2 on the real models are still pending.

Deviation (FACTS update): the core of E1 is plain vs mtp-explicit interleaved with --rounds 2 on both models, instead of the manifest's 'mtp, and mtp-explicit only if mtp never drafts'. mtp, dflash and ngram (26B) and mtp (31B) then run one round each. dflash-explicit runs when mtp or dflash did not draft. Budget: the 31B core alone is 4 server runs of about 11 min each.
Deviation: the default 31B lower quant is 31b-ud-iq3_xxs, the quant the real Pi runs (EXPERIMENT_PLAN D2), not the manifest's UD-IQ2_XXS. `-LowerQuant31 31b-ud-iq2_xxs` restores the manifest choice.

Stricter download disk gate: free >= max(1.3 x size, size + 4 GB), so at least 4 GB is always left for logits and results. A file this script downloaded is deleted once its kld and qa both finished, unless -KeepDownloads; if either fails it is kept so a re-run resumes without downloading again.

Additions beyond the spec: E1_SUMMARY.md, which adds the verdict word 'marginal' (active and lossless but below the useful rule); exit codes 5 (time box) and 6 (repack gate not PASS); renaming superseded results to *.<UTC>.superseded; the -QaHard set; and the driver log under results/<date>/raw/.

The membw step (D5) needs Docker Desktop, Git Bash and tools/build-linux-x86/bin/membw. When any of them is missing, or the run fails, the step is reported as a warning and does not change the exit code. The step holds the bench lock through `paths lock --hold`.
Any E0 gate data that is missing (INCOMPLETE) also yields exit 6, so a run cannot look like a pass without evidence.

QA results stay in results/quality/, as the plan's Writes row says, so they are not under results/<date>. The summary step therefore adds this run's results/quality/qa_<model>_*.json files (and hard/) as extra inputs.

Not my file: CLAUDE.md now notes 'use the chat endpoint for QA' after the thinking-markup glitches on the Pi. quality.py's qa still uses /completion with chat_wrap, so that concern belongs to quality.py.

This script does no idle check of its own; it passes bench.py's --idle-check-s, --idle-max-pct, --idle-wait-s and --require-idle through. Without -RequireIdle, timings taken on a busy machine are recorded with a note in the envelope rather than refused.

entries.summary: pc/h2_run.ps1 (PowerShell 5.1, pure ASCII, LF, 1108 lines). E7 driver: map (gguf_map build --reuse; run first, header only) -> corpus (python -m pigemma.quality corpus --check / rebuild) -> acts (bash pc/docker_run.sh --no-stdin -- python -m pigemma.paths lock --hold --min-free-gb 20 -- tools/build-linux-x86/bin/pigemma-probe --mode act-dump ... -nr -t 12 -c 1024 -b 512 -ub 128 --kinds ffn_norm,ffn_geglu,ffn_out; 384 prefill + 128 generated per chunk; written to <acts>.partial and swapped in only after verification) -> decompose (--lock) -> oracle (--lock, also --layers/--mats/--bases/--map) -> verdict line. It prints free disk, RAM, a measured/assumed ETA formula and the wall time per step. It refuses >8 layers or >1024 tokens without -Force (exit 4) and refuses up front when the bench lock is held. It reuses usable acts (complete, same GGUF, enough tokens, all layers/kinds, same corpus). It writes <out dir>/h2_run.json and retires superseded E7 envelopes that cite the same oracle.json. MEASURED on a real -Quick integration run (exit 0, ~20.6 min): probe built via -BuildProbe in 94 s; 31B act-dump load 929.8 s and 1077.1 s through the Docker Desktop bind mount (~16-19 MB/s); prefill 5.6-6.5 tok/s and gen 1.6-2.1 tok/s at -t 6 in Docker; decompose ~15 s and oracle ~15 s per q2 case at 128 tokens. Oracle sanity medians were 0.0053 and 0.0062 (pass) with 0 soundness violations. Quick verdict NO_ADVANTAGE (frac@3% median 0.964, cert eff 0.070, 23.34 GB/token PROJECTED). These are quick-sample numbers, not the E7 result.
entries.interface_notes:
INVOCATION: .\pc\h2_run.ps1 [...] from PowerShell, or powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File pc\h2_run.ps1 [...] (works from any cwd; Push/Set-Location to the repo root, restored at exit; PYTHONUTF8/PYTHONIOENCODING set only for the run and restored). List params accept PS arrays (-Layers 5,20) and comma strings (-File form); -Layers also accepts ranges a-b.

PARAMETERS (defaults): -Layers 5,20,35,50 | -Tokens 512 | -Group 128 | -Bases q2,lowrank256 | -ResBits 4 (2,3,4,5,6,8,16) | -Force | -SkipActs | -Quick (layers 20,45; tokens 128 = 96 prefill + 32 gen; bases q2; group 128; explicit params win) | -Mats gate,up,down | -Eps 0.01,0.03,0.10 | -Model 31b-q4 (registry id or GGUF path; a model outside the repo is mounted at /h2model:ro) | -Corpus data/calibration/all.txt (must be inside the repo) | -Threads 12 | -ChunkTokens 0=auto (384, or round(0.75*T) if T<512) | -Gen -1=auto (128, or T-chunk) | -Ctx 0=auto (max(1024, chunk+gen rounded up to 256)) | -ActsDir traces/h2/acts/31b (-Quick: 31b-quick; must be inside the repo) | -DecompDir traces/h2/decomp | -MapPath traces/h2/map31.json | -Out results/h2/oracle.json (-Quick: results/h2-quick/oracle.json) | -Md docs/results/H2_RESULTS.md (-Quick: docs/results/H2_RESULTS_quick.md) | -RedoActs | -Recompute (decompose --force) | -BuildProbe (bash pc/docker_run.sh build-tools --targets pigemma-probe when the probe is missing) | -NoLock | -KeepOldEnvelopes | -MinFreeGb 20 (lock RAM gate of the Docker capture) | -MinFreeDiskGb 2 | -Python (default $env:PIGEMMA_PYTHON or python) | -DryRun (gates + exact commands incl. docker_run.sh --dry-run and decompose --dry-run; loads/writes nothing; exit 0 unless a usage/limit gate fails) | -Help. Unknown parameters or stray args -> exit 2.

EXIT CODES: 0 ok (oracle pipeline VALID or UNKNOWN); 1 step failed / oracle pipeline INVALID (verdict printed as VOID, outputs written) / unexpected error; 2 usage; 3 missing (model, probe binary, Git Bash, python+numpy, map, -Corpus file, acts with -SkipActs); 4 refused (>8 layers or >1024 tokens without -Force, bench lock held, not enough disk, or a step refused); 130 interrupted. A step's own 1/2/3/4/130 is forwarded; other codes (docker 125/126/127) become 1. Errors and refusals go to stderr as 'h2_run: ERROR (exit N): ...' or 'h2_run: REFUSED: ...'.

STDOUT ANCHORS: 'h2_run: ---- step <name>: exit N after <dur>'; 'h2_run: wall time per step:' plus one row per step (map, build-probe, corpus, acts, decompose, oracle; status ok|failed|skipped|cached|dry-run); final line 'h2_run: E7 VERDICT: <PROMISING|WEAK|NO_ADVANTAGE|NOT_SUPPORTED> (best base B; pipeline VALID|UNKNOWN) | frac@3% median X | cert eff median Y | implied Z GB/token (PROJECTED) | S s/token @850 MB/s (PROJECTED) | T tok/s @10 GB/s (PROJECTED)', or 'E7 VERDICT: VOID (pipeline INVALID: ...) - raw ...'.

FILES WRITTEN AT RUNTIME: acts dir (via <acts>.partial staging), decomp npz and index.json, oracle.json + markdown + E7 envelopes (oracle), and <dir of -Out>/h2_run.json = {record:'pigemma.h2_run', driver, version, started_at, finished_at, wall_s, host, argv[], config{model, model_path, corpus, layers, mats, bases, group, res_bits, tokens, eps, quick, chunk_tokens, gen, ctx, threads, acts_dir, decomp_dir, map, out, md, lock, min_free_gb, acts_captured}, steps[{step, status, seconds, exit, command}], exit_code, verdict}. It has no 'experiment' key, so results summarize skips it.

LOCKING: a host-side pre-check refuses when results/.bench.lock is held. The Docker step takes the lock via paths lock --hold; decompose and oracle take it via --lock (4 GB RAM gate). To hold the lock across all steps: python -m pigemma.paths lock --hold -- powershell -NoProfile -File pc\h2_run.ps1 ... (PIGEMMA_LOCK_HELD is inherited). ENV honoured: PIGEMMA_PYTHON, PIGEMMA_BASH (Git Bash path), plus everything docker_run.sh forwards (e.g. PIGEMMA_IMAGE, PIGEMMA_MIN_FREE_GB).

open_issues: Chunk 0 of data/calibration/all.txt is C++ source cut mid-line; in the -Quick capture greedy generation produced 32 '/' characters, so the oracle's 'gen' phase (control C3) of short runs only covers code continuation. Deviations from the spec command list: the map step runs before the capture (header only, needed for the layer check and disk projection), and the oracle also gets --layers/--mats/--bases/--map so stale npz files in traces/h2/decomp/ cannot leak into the verdict.

FACTS.md says loading a 14 GB GGUF through the bind mount takes 1-2 min; MEASURED here it is 930-1077 s for 17.65 GB (mmap page faults through Docker Desktop, ~16-19 MB/s). The manifest's '~20 min' for the act-dump is right. The ETA constants now use the slower measured values. The manifest's 60 s per (layer, matrix, base) is kept, though MEASURED q2 at 128 tokens was ~30 s.

Artifacts left by my test runs: tools/build-linux-x86/bin/pigemma-probe (+ build tree; canonical location), data/calibration/all.txt (python -m pigemma.quality corpus), traces/h2/acts/31b-quick/, traces/h2/decomp/L{20,45}.{gate,up,down}.q2.npz + index.json (2.77 GB), results/h2-quick/{oracle.json, 2 E7 envelopes, h2_run.json}, docs/results/H2_RESULTS_quick.md. The L45 npz (1.39 GB) are not in the full E7 layer set (5,20,35,50) and can be deleted if D: gets tight (17.8 GB free; the full run needs ~9.84 GB more).

During testing, an earlier version removed the existing -Quick dump before a capture that then failed. The dump was my own artifact and was re-captured; the design is fixed (capture goes to <acts>.partial and is swapped in only after verification) and both paths are tested.

entries.summary:
I wrote pi/06_pin_hotset.sh (bash, 2158 lines). It sources pi/lib/common.sh and embeds a stdlib Python helper inside the script, the same pattern pi/05 uses. I also wrote tests/test_pi06_pin_hotset.py (44 tests).

The script has four subcommands:
- **start** runs the gates: assert_safe_host, mlock_allowed, no live pinner, and the bench lock not held by another job. It then resolves the model and the map. results/map26.json is used when it describes the local GGUF; otherwise a map is built on the host into pi/out/map_<stem>.json. Next come the stats (traces/26b/all.stats.json, optional; without them only the non-expert tensors are pinned) and the budget. It checks memlock and the pinner's RAM guard, then runs the manifest's `python3 -m pigemma.gguf_map hotset ... --page-size <runtime page> --out pi/out/hotset.json`. Finally it starts `nohup nice -n 10 pinner --gguf M --ranges pi/out/hotset.ranges.txt --verify --json --pidfile pi/out/pinner.pid > pi/out/pinner.log &`, waits for the JSON summary line, writes pi/out/pin_state.json and prints the locked and resident bytes and the expert coverage.
- **stop** sends SIGTERM to the pidfile's process only, and only after checking it is a pinner.
- **status** reports VmLck plus mincore residency via `pinner --verify-only`.
- **ab** plans the hot set once. Per round it then runs `pi/05_run.sh stream-bench` unpinned and pinned, measures hot-set residency around every run, and writes results/pi/pin_ab.json plus a timestamped copy. That file holds both runs' tok/s and read_bytes_per_token, the ratios, and the pre-registered E6 PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE check. The whole A/B holds the bench lock.

Budget: --budget-bytes, else PIN_BUDGET_BYTES, else auto = MemAvailable - KV(ctx, q8_0 from the map) - 0.3e9 - 0.5e9, capped at the file size.

Additions beyond the manifest (all tested):
- --max-hold, which makes the pinner expire by itself. On a protected host run with the override it defaults to 7200 s.
- --hotset, to reuse an existing plan.
- --best-effort, --rounds (ABBA order), --dry-run and --json.
- Refusal of split GGUFs.
- Cleanup that stops a pinner this run started if the start is interrupted or times out.
entries.interface_notes:
CLI: `bash pi/06_pin_hotset.sh start|stop|status|ab [--model GGUF|catalog-id] [--map F] [--stats F | --no-stats] [--budget-bytes N]`. --opt=value works for every option.

Options for start and ab:
- `-c/--ctx N` (default CTX)
- `--kv-type q8_0` (f32 f16 bf16 q8_0 q5_1 q5_0 q4_1 q4_0 iq4_nl)
- `--compute-bytes 0.3e9`, `--headroom-bytes 0.5e9`
- `--rank count|weight`, `--per-layer-min N`
- `--hotset hotset.json` (start: skip planning; the ranges file is <json minus .json>.ranges.txt)
- `--pinner PATH`
- `--start-timeout 1800`, `--stop-timeout 60`
- `--best-effort`
- `--max-hold S` (pinner --hold-seconds; 0 = until stop)
- `--allow-protected-host` (forwarded to the pinner; never automatic)
- `--json` (start/status), `--dry-run`, `-h`, `--version` (prints "pi/06_pin_hotset.sh 1.0.0")

Options for ab only:
- `--rounds N`: odd rounds run unpinned then pinned, even rounds pinned then unpinned
- `-n N`, `--with-he` (default passes --no-he to pi/05)
- `--results-dir DIR` (pi/05 --out; default results/pi, or results/pi-emu when PIGEMMA_EMULATED=1)
- `--out FILE` (default <results-dir>/pin_ab.json)
- `--run-arg ARG` (repeatable) and everything after a bare `--`: passed to pi/05_run.sh
- `--no-lock`

Default model when --model is absent: the recommended model id in pi/out/feasibility.json, looked up in MODEL_DIR.

Budget precedence: --budget-bytes, then PIN_BUDGET_BYTES (unless auto), then auto = MemAvailable(effective) - map.kv_bytes(CTX, kv-type) - compute - headroom, capped at the file size. Formats: 5200000000, 5.2e9, 5.2GB, 2GiB, 512MiB.

Exit codes:
- 0 ok
- 1 usage, internal error, failed run, pinner failure or start timeout
- 2 start: partial pin; the daemon keeps holding what it locked, and pi/05 accepts 2
- 3 precondition (model, pinner, map, stats or python missing; memlock limit too small; RAM; budget below the non-expert set; split GGUF), and status when no pinner is running
- 4 refused (protected host, mlock not allowed, a pinner already running, the bench lock held by another job, the pinner's own protected-host guard)
- stop exits 0 when nothing is running

Files (PIGEMMA_OUT = pi/out):
- hotset.json and hotset.ranges.txt
- map_<stem>.json (map built on the host)
- pinner.pid
- pinner.log: exactly the pinner's one JSON line
- pinner.stderr.log (the previous run's logs are kept as *.prev)
- pin_state.json: {format_version, generator, version, created_at, updated_at, state running|exited|timeout|stopped|gone, host, emulated, protected_override, pid, pidfile, log, stderr_log, pinner, argv, exit_code, model{id,path,bytes}, map, stats, hotset, ranges, plan, page_size, max_hold_s, budget{bytes,source,formula,mem_available_bytes,kv_bytes,kv_source,kv_type,ctx,compute_bytes,headroom_bytes}, hotset_info{...}, summary (the pinner JSON), notes[], stopped_at, stop_wait_s, vm_lck_bytes_at_stop}
- pin_ab_<UTC>/: per-run copies of last_stream-bench.json, pin_state.json and the verify-only JSON before and after each run

pin_ab.json is not a results envelope: it has no "experiment" key, so `results summarize` skips it. Keys: format_version, generator, version, created_at, kind 'measured', experiment_ref, host, emulated, protected_override, argv, model{}, hotset{json, ranges, map, stats, budget_bytes, budget_source, budget_formula, total_bytes, n_ranges, n_experts, n_expert_items_total, expert_coverage_fraction, nonexpert_included, nonexpert_bytes_aligned, page_size, rank}, rounds, order[], runs[{label, round, exit_code, failed, started_at, ended_at, result_files[], tg_tok_s, pp_tok_s, read_bytes_per_token, majflt_per_token, load_s, coherent, mode, effective_flags, pinned_by_pi05, pinner{...}|null, hot_set_requested_bytes, hot_set_resident_before_bytes, hot_set_resident_after_bytes, mincore_reliable, last_run_copy, notes}], unpinned/pinned{n, n_failed, tg_tok_s, read_bytes_per_token, majflt_per_token}, ratio{tok_s_pinned_over_unpinned, read_bytes_per_token_pinned_over_unpinned, bytes_per_token_reduction, majflt_per_token_pinned_over_unpinned}, bytes_per_token_worst, in_ram, threshold_check{rule, tok_s_ratio_min 1.15, bytes_reduction_min 0.20, result PASS|FAIL|INCONCLUSIVE, reason}, notes[].

stdout:
- start: the text summary (with --json: pin_state.json)
- status: the summary or JSON {running, pid, vm_lck_bytes, pidfile, verify, verify_exit_code, state, checked_at, notes}
- stop: one line, "pinner: stopped (...)" or "pinner: not running"
- ab: pi/05's envelope paths, then pin_ab.json and its timestamped copy
- dry-run: the exact commands

The pi/05 contract is met:
- `start --model <gguf> [pin args]` returns 0, or 2 for a partial pin.
- `stop` stops the pinner.
- A live 'pinner' process is named in $PIGEMMA_OUT/pinner.pid.

Test helpers in tests/test_pi06_pin_hotset.py: helper_source(), _env(), fake_root(..., pinner_pid=, ulimit_l=, mem_available_kb=), stats_for_map26(), kv().
entries.self_test:
1. `bash -n pi/06_pin_hotset.sh` passes under Git Bash and under the Ubuntu 24.04 bash in Docker. The file uses LF line endings and has a shebang.

2. `python -m pytest tests/test_pi06_pin_hotset.py`: 43 passed, 1 skipped (the `linux` end-to-end test, on Windows). They cover:
   - usage line equal to the manifest, and usage errors
   - helper units: byte parsing, the auto budget using the map's KV of 155,975,680 B at 4096 q8_0, check-map, check-stats, resolve-model, pinner-summary, state file and reports, and the ab-report PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE logic
   - dry-run plans on the fake roots, including the map rebuild when --map describes another GGUF
   - every refusal path: protected host, override without mlock, the protected flag, ALLOW_MLOCK=0, memlock 8192 kB, low RAM below the non-expert set, a pinner already running, split GGUF, and real runs under a fake root
   - status and stop with no pinner and with a fake pinner pid; no signal is sent there

3. `python -m pytest tests/test_pi06_pin_hotset.py tests/test_pi05_run.py tests/test_experiment_plan.py tests/test_docs_hypotheses.py`: all pass, 2 linux-only tests skipped.

4. Real pinner in Docker (pi-gemma4-build image, no pytest there). The pinner was compiled from tools/pinner/pinner.c inside the container, because the repo binary is stale (see open issues). The model was a synthetic 4-layer, 16-expert, 14.5 MB MoE GGUF from tests/synth, with a tiny catalog entry. Driver scripts were in the scratchpad. All results matched expectations:
   - start: map built with the stdlib reader; 26 ranges, 3,989,504 B locked; VmLck 3896 kB equals locked_bytes
   - status: exit 0, 100% resident
   - second start: exit 4
   - stop: exit 0; pinner gone and pidfile removed
   - status after stop: exit 3; second stop: exit 0
   - auto budget: capped at the file size
   - --no-stats: non-expert tensors only
   - `ulimit -l 64`: exit 3
   - `ulimit -l 1024 --best-effort`: partial, exit 2, the daemon holds 972 kB
   - --max-hold 3: the pinner exits by itself
   - --hotset reuse: works; a hot set planned for another file size gives exit 1
   - a pinner that never prints its summary hits --start-timeout: exit 1 and it is stopped
   - SIGINT while waiting: the started pinner is stopped, nothing left over
   - a process named /opt/contextfriend-box/run makes the pinner's own guard refuse: exit 4
   - a pinner usage error: exit 1
   - budget below the non-expert set: exit 3
   - bench lock held by another job: exit 4 for start and ab
   - **ab** end to end through pi/05_run.sh with the llama-completion double: exit 0; pi/05 ran the inner `start --hotset` and the stop; the pinned run's envelope recorded the pinner; pin_ab.json was written (INCONCLUSIVE, in_ram, as expected for an in-RAM toy); no pinner and no pidfile were left behind.

No inference was run on the real models.
open_issues: tools/build-linux-x86/bin/pinner is out of date: it was built at 08:34, but tools/pinner/pinner.c was changed at 08:50. The binary has no --allow-protected-host and no protected-host guard. Rebuild it with `bash pc/docker_run.sh build-tools` (that agent owns the file). My Docker self-test compiled pinner.c from source into /tmp inside the container instead.

ab does not run the manifest's literal `start; stream-bench; stop`. Its pinned run is `pi/05_run.sh stream-bench --pin --pin-arg=--hotset ...`, so pi/05 starts this script after its own gates and stops the pinner at exit. The reason: with the pinner holding the auto budget, MemAvailable drops to about KV + 0.8 GB, under 1 GB, and pi/05's assert_not_busy would refuse.

status uses `pinner --verify-only` instead of the manifest's `pinner --verify --once`. A second locking pass while the daemon runs would be refused by the pinner's memory guard; this is the pinner's own documented recommendation.

memlock: the manifest says unlimited is required. A finite `ulimit -l` that is at least the hot set, or an effective CAP_IPC_LOCK, is also accepted, with a note. --best-effort turns the refusal into a partial pin (exit 2).

Protected hosts (context-friend-1): pinning is refused (exit 4) unless ALLOW_MLOCK=1 and --allow-protected-host are both given. Even then --max-hold defaults to 7200 s, so the experiment always expires. EXPERIMENT_PLAN D4 says no pinning on that host; the newer CLAUDE.md allows bounded pinner experiments. This needs the operator's explicit flags.

Split GGUFs are refused with exit 3: the map, the hot set and the pinner all address offsets in one file. The QAT Q4_0 26B on the Pi's FAT32 USB stick is a 5-part split, so pinning it needs a merged single file on a filesystem that allows files over 4 GB.

No memory balloon is built in. On the 16 GB Pi every 26B file fits in RAM, so `ab` reports INCONCLUSIVE (in_ram). The decisive H1 test needs `sudo python3 pi/adhoc/balloon.py <GiB> <max_s>` started first; the auto budget then uses the reduced MemAvailable. This is documented in --help and the header.

The default stats (traces/26b/all.stats.json) do not exist yet; E3 has not shipped them. Without stats only the non-expert tensors are pinned, with a warning. Stats from the 26B Q4_0 trace are applied by layer and expert index to other quants of the same model (e.g. UD-Q3_K_M); their routing may differ slightly, and only the stats path is recorded.

The auto budget follows the manifest formula. That leaves only about the 0.5 GB headroom of page cache for streaming the cold experts, and the compute and headroom terms are ASSUMED values (tunable via --compute-bytes / --headroom-bytes).
The linux-marked end-to-end pytest cannot run in the pi-gemma4-build image (no pytest there). The same sequence was run by hand with driver scripts in that image.
When ab re-executes itself under `pigemma.paths lock --hold`, the configuration dump and the safety-gate warnings are printed twice (once outside the lock, once inside). This is cosmetic.
pin_ab.json deliberately has no 'experiment' key, so it is not a results envelope. The per-run E8 envelopes written by pi/05 are the envelopes.

I wrote docs/PI_RUNBOOK.md (about 970 lines, UTF-8, LF line endings) and its own test module, tests/test_pi_runbook.py. All 22 tests in the module pass.

What the runbook covers:
- **Quick start.** The full 00→06 sequence for a Pi you own, plus a separate, shorter one for context-friend-1.
- **Exit codes and refusal rules.** The shared exit codes 0/1/2/3/4 and a refusal-rules table.
  - The table covers: the deny-listed hostname (now through the catalog's `protected_hosts`), protected service globs, busy host, bench lock, RAM and disk gates, mlock not allowed, AI HAT on the PCIe lane, container `--apply`, and split GGUFs.
  - It also lists the context-friend-1 safety rules.
- **Hardware options table.** It covers 4/8/16 GB × microSD / USB 3.0 SSD / NVMe Gen2 / NVMe Gen3, plus AI HAT and multi-Pi rows.
  - The tok/s values are recomputed by pigemma.feasibility.
  - The real-Pi measurements come from results/pi-real/README.md.
  - Recommendation: 16 GB + NVMe Gen3 + Active Cooler.
- **Prerequisites.** apt packages; Active Cooler; NVMe HAT; `ulimit -l unlimited` with a re-login.
- **Setup.** Copying the repo with tar over ssh (Git Bash has no rsync; the stream measured 4.9 MB). Filling pi/pi_config.env through a host file outside the checkout, with a variable table.
- **Steps 00–06.** Each step gives the command, what the script does, needs and writes, its stdout and its exit codes.
  - Steps 00, 01 and 04 show expected output from real desktop runs against the context-friend-1 fixture. This includes pi/04's disk fallback from 26b-q4 to 26b-ud-q3_k_m.
- **Flags per verdict.** The exact `FLAGS_*` strings, and why repack is refused, with llama.cpp line references I re-checked (src/llama-model.cpp line 1856, src/llama-model-loader.cpp lines 1240–1242).
- **Shipping artefacts.** Sending map26.json, all.stats.json, sim.json and hot sets to the Pi with scp or rsync, and bringing results back.
- **Measured replaces assumed.** A merge table and the loop pi/03 + pi/05 → pi/00 → cache_sim re-projection on the desktop → `pi/00 --sim`.
- **Smoke tests.** EN + HE chat, stream-bench, and the pin A/B, each with a pass rule fixed before the run.
- **Troubleshooting.** The 5 required cases (OOM on load in repack mode, ETIMEDOUT downloads, memlock EPERM, read-ahead thrash, thermal throttling) plus 7 more.
- **Closing sections.** A MEASURED/PROJECTED/ASSUMED status table, a usage reference card copied verbatim from the scripts, and a list of deviations from the manifest spec.

The test module checks that:
- every script's `Usage:` lines (read from the script source, with `$VAR` expanded) appear verbatim in the runbook;
- all 78 pi script invocations use real scripts, subcommands and long options;
- `python -m pigemma.*` flags exist in each module's `--help`;
- flags quoted in code spans exist in some project or llama.cpp source;
- the per-verdict flags equal `feasibility.FLAGS_*`;
- the hardware grid values equal a fresh feasibility computation;
- the context-friend-1 rows (verdict, tok/s, pi/04 disk need) equal feasibility on the real-Pi fixture with the override;
- the MEASURED numbers quoted occur in their source files;

- 26B: data_offset 15,823,936, 658 tensors, expert unit 3,345,408 B, 802,897,920 B/token worst case, non-expert 1,577,172,088 B, experts 12,846,366,720 B. All match.
- 31B: data_offset 15,833,440, 833 tensors, each FFN matrix 65,028,096 B, FFN total 11,705,057,280 B. All match.
- The new maps are identical to the repo's results/map26.json and traces/h2/map31.json except for created_at, so I left those files as they are. As implemented, the 31B map lives at traces/h2/map31.json (decompose, oracle and h2_run.ps1 read it there); there is no results/map31.json.
remaining_problems: catalog.json protected_hosts still lists context-friend-1. FACTS says DENY_HOSTS must no longer contain it by default, so the hostname is still refused by name unless PIGEMMA_I_KNOW=1. In practice the outcome is the same, because its contextfriend-* services already trigger exit 4, and the README and PI_RUNBOOK describe the current behaviour. I left it for the operator to decide.

feasibility KV_Q8_4K['31b'] = 420e6 is a manifest-specified assumption, but gguf_map computes 623.9 MB for the 31B at 4096 context with q8_0 (an upper bound). The 26B value of 160e6 is consistent. Correcting it would change the 31b-q3_k_s fit on 16 GB, where the margin is about 30 MB, and the numbers quoted in the docs, so I did not change it.

The catalog has no 'pi5-16gb-microsd-real' device profile, although FACTS asks for one. feasibility and cache_sim synthesize a profile from the facts or io_mem.json. Adding the device also requires updating the constants block in docs/HYPOTHESES.md §8, which test_docs_hypotheses checks.

The pigemma-probe binary has not been linked on aarch64; only probe.cpp.o was compiled with gcc 14. A full Pi build through pi/02 --with-tools, or a qemu build of about 25 minutes or more, is still untested.
The Linux-only real-pinner test in test_pi06_pin_hotset was not run: the build image has no numpy and the arm64 image has no x86 pinner. The pi/06 agent ran the same sequence by hand earlier.
Linux-marked tests run under pytest only through a manual container trick, because neither Docker image has pytest and nothing may be pip-installed.

docs/HYPOTHESES.md §3.3 still says the real-Pi 26B UD-Q3_K_M run is unfinished. results/pi-real/README.md now has it: 3.17-3.27 tok/s measured against 2.14 projected, above the pre-registered E8 band of 1.7-3.0. HYPOTHESES gives 2.13; the README and runbook give 2.14.
pi_config.env defaults LLAMA_DIR to ~/llama.cpp, while the existing build on the real Pi is at ~/pigemma/llama.cpp. Set LLAMA_DIR or PIGEMMA_LLAMA_BIN there, as documented in the runbook.
build_test.summary:
The repo builds and the unit tests pass. Clean Docker build: exit 0, no warnings. Unit suite: 891 passed, 21 skipped, 0 failed (after-edit re-runs green). bash -n and the PowerShell parser show no errors. Both maps match every verified constant.

**Build.** `bash pc/docker_run.sh build-tools --require-all` rebuilt the stale pinner. pigemma-probe, pinner and membw are in tools/build-linux-x86/bin, which is where pigemma/paths.py looks for them. On aarch64 with gcc 14, probe.cpp compiles to an object and pinner and membw build and run; the full aarch64 probe link is still untested.

**Pytest on Windows** (`python -m pytest -q`): 912 collected, 891 passed, 21 skipped (shellcheck, rsync, Linux-only), 0 failed. The 11 integration tests also pass.

**Changes:**
- Fixed a flaky timing bound in tests/test_bench_parse.py.
- Updated the stale MTP draft note in pigemma/feasibility.py to match FACTS.
- Corrected the E8 verdict expectation in docs/EXPERIMENT_PLAN.md from FITS_MAPPED to FITS_REPACKED, with deviation D6.
- Added the readme field to pyproject.toml.
- Added .gitattributes so scripts stay LF and data, results and fixtures are never converted.

**Shared contracts.** I checked the probe vs trace.py trace format, the map.json consumers, the results envelope and the catalog loader; no drift.

**GGUF maps.** Rebuilt from the real files, both match every verified constant (26B: 15,823,936 / 3,345,408 / 802,897,920 / 1,577,172,088; 31B: 15,833,440 / 833 tensors). They are byte-identical to results/map26.json and traces/h2/map31.json apart from the timestamp, so I left those files as they are.
